title: CMI co-organises Nordic peace mediation seminar during Nordic Council Session
content:
CMI co-organises a seminar on Nordic peace mediation at the Parliament of Finland in Helsinki on 26 October. Held in conjunction with the 78th Session of the Nordic Council, ‘Nordic peace mediation in a changing world order’ will examine opportunities for closer Nordic cooperation in peace mediation amid a changing geopolitical environment.

Organised by the Finnish delegation to the Nordic Council and CMI, the side-event brings together Nordic Council parliamentarians, political leaders and peace mediation experts to discuss how the Nordic countries can strengthen their collective contribution to international peace and stability.

The seminar can be watched live from 13.00–13.50 with a recording available on the website of the Nordic Council. Panellists are expected to speak in their own Nordic language.

Monday’s discussion takes place against a backdrop of intensified power politics, growing strategic competition and increasing pressure on the rules-based international order. These developments have changed the international environment for peace mediation and challenged the capacity of traditional multilateral institutions to address conflicts.

title: Verify Before You Contribute: Connecting Fact-Checking with Wikipedia Editing
content:
I participated in the Abuja edition of the Interactive Media Seminar for Electoral Integrity, organised by the Foundation for Investigative Journalism and Accountability (FIAP) through FactCheckAfrica, in collaboration with Wikimedia Nigeria. The seminar was held from 28 to 30 September 2026 as part of the European Union’s support to the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in the areas of peace, security, and governance.

The seminar brought together Wikimedia contributors, newsroom editors, and fact-checkers for practical sessions on information disorder, source verification, digital investigations, and the responsible creation, contribution, and use of information.

The experience provided an opportunity to learn new skills, reinforce existing knowledge, and reflect on practical ways to identify and counter misinformation. One of the most important lessons I learned was the need to investigate and verify information before believing it, sharing it, or using it to contribute to online knowledge platforms.

title: Between two shores: The ‘Monhés,’ nationality, and a sense of belonging in Mozambique
content:
Being Mozambican is a matter of belonging — regardless of one’s origin, appearance, or surname

Originally published on Global Voices

Indians in Mozambique celebrating the Hindu festival of Navratri. Image by Kash_if via Flickr. CC BY 2.0.

In Mozambique, the word monhé has a much deeper history than its everyday use might suggest. Depending on who says it and the context, it can simply be a reference to the population of Indian origin, an identity marker, or a prejudiced remark. But behind the word there is a history of migration, trade, colonialism, independence, displacement, and, above all, belonging.

The question of who is Mozambican gets particularly interesting when we look at the communities of Indian origin, who have lived in the country for several generations. Are they Mozambicans? Indians? Foreigners? Or, in some cases, stateless persons? The answer cannot be found in appearance, surname, religion, or family origin alone. It is found in the country’s history and, particularly, in its nationality law.

Being Mozambican is a matter of belonging — regardless of one’s origin, appearance, or surname

title: South Korea: Medication Abortion Rules Too Restrictive
content:
(Tokyo) – A South Korean government proposal would allow medication abortion in South Korea in 2027, but overly restrictive regulations will continue to impair the right of women and girls to safe and affordable abortion services, Human Rights Watch said today. National Assembly members have questioned government officials about the plan during a parliamentary audit. 

Seven years after South Korea’s Constitutional Court ruled the country’s decades-long abortion ban unconstitutional, effectively decriminalizing abortion and ordering legal reform by the end of 2020, the government has yet to amend the law to explicitly guarantee abortion rights. The government’s new proposal would finally establish a regulatory framework for medication abortion using Mifegymiso, a combination of Misoprostol and Mifepristone recognized by the World Health Organization (WHO) as the safest and most effective regimen. But access to the medication will remain unnecessarily impaired.

title: Sri Lanka Records Zero Prosecutions Amid Online Scam Surge
content:
Authorities in Sri Lanka have failed to successfully prosecute a single transnational cyber scam case, police have said, despite more than a thousand arrests so far this year of suspected members of Asian fraud syndicates who have surged into the South Asian country.

The admission comes as experts warn the island nation is becoming a destination of choice for thousands of scam workers fleeing Southeast Asian nations such as Cambodia, which had in recent years become home to massive scam compounds, many of them reliant on trafficked workers.

Recently crackdowns in scam centers in Southeast Asia have driven mostly Chinese-origin scam syndicates to set up shop in vulnerable states from Madagascar to Papua New Guinea.
Among the countries of South Asia, Sri Lanka stands out for being at “serious risk of becoming a hub for industrial-scale cyber scams,” the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC) said last month.

From January until September, Sri Lankan police have conducted raids on 27 suspected scam compounds around the country and arrested 1093 people, Sri Lankan police spokesman Fredrick Wootler told OCCRP and Sri Lanka’s The Sunday Times.

title: A Texas Cop Signed on to Help ICE Deport His Neighbors. It Tore the Town Apart.
content:
The new patrol officer parked his black Dodge Charger outside a house off Main Street and approached on foot. A Mexican ballad was playing. Someone had called in a noise complaint, claiming it sounded as if people were fighting.

But as the officer, Jaron Alexander, got closer, he found nothing of the sort. A middle-aged woman greeted him as her daughter, Joanna Martinez, petite and visibly pregnant, looked on. “What kind of party are you all having?” she remembers him asking. Behind her were three generations of an extended family. They were celebrating a 3-month-old’s baptism over pozole verde, horchata and beers.

Alexander ran some IDs and found no issues. The music wasn’t even that loud, he thought. He told them to have a good night, and then he left.

That encounter, in early October last year, was the first of many that Alexander and Martinez would have in tiny Ingram, Texas, a 1.5-square-mile town of 1,900 people beside the Guadalupe River. But it was the only one before Ingram signed an agreement with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement that would roil the town and tear Martinez’s family apart.

title: Canada and Europe want to reshape the global order. But whose vision will prevail?
content:
Mark Carney’s push for a middle-powers alliance meets Ursula von der Leyen’s bid for influence.

By ZI-ANN LUM, SEBASTIAN STARCEVIC
and CAMILLE GIJS

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

Mark Carney’s pursuit of a global alliance of middle powers has a Europe problem.

Canada’s prime minister wants to help build a new world order that can counterbalance the power of the United States and China. But his vision depends on a new relationship with a Europe that doesn’t see itself as a middle power at all. 

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has a different vision: a Brussels-centered bloc that extends the EU’s economic and geopolitical influence, starting with Canada. The idea, according to senior European lawmaker Siegfried Mureșan, is to create an opportunity for the EU to become the “global center of gravity for liberal democracies.”

title: Anthropic sued for allegedly using 274 Elvis Presley songs to train AI models
content:
Authentic Brands Group says AI company infringed on rights of songs by the King such as Can’t Help Falling in Love

The owners of Elvis Presley’s music catalogue are suing artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic for allegedly using Presley’s songs to train their models without permission.

Authentic Brands Group, the licensing organization that has ownership of both Presley’s music and likeness, is accusing Anthropic of infringing on the rights of 274 songs by Presley. The lawsuit, first reported by Billboard, was filed on Friday.

title: Ukrainassa puolustusteknologiaa kehitetään rohkein harppauksin, Suomessa harkituin askelin
content:
Autonomiset järjestelmät ja kehittyvä teknologia muuttavat sodankäyntiä nopeammin kuin perinteiset puolustusorganisaatiot kykenevät mukautumaan. Ukraina on olosuhteiden pakottamana osoittanut tässä suhteessa edistyksellisyyttä testaamalla uutta puolustusteknologiaa ketterästi: matalalla kynnyksellä ja nopealla syklillä. Suomessa lähestymistapa on maltillisempi. Analyysissa syvennytään suomalaisen puolustusteknologiayritys Kova Labsin kokemuksiin Ukrainasta, jossa toimintaympäristö on teknologisen kehityksen kannalta otollinen.

Sotateknologian kehitystä ajoi toisen maailmansodan aikaan valtiojohtoinen innovaatioekosysteemi, jossa valtio rahoitti ja koordinoi teknologista kehitystä sotilaallisten tarpeiden pohjalta. 2020-luvun muuttuneessa turvallisuuspoliittisessa ympäristössä tilanne on käänteinen, sillä puolustusorganisaatioiden kehitys ei pysy siviilijohtoisen teknologisen kilpajuoksun tahdissa.

title: Learning, Sharing, and Connecting: My First Experience at Open Knowledge in the CEE Region
content:
Sometimes, a conference is valuable not because it answers your questions, but because it helps you discover which questions to ask next.

That was my experience at Open Knowledge: Wikimedia & Research in the CEE Region in Katowice, Poland. I arrived hoping to share my experience of using Wikipedia in university teaching and to meet researchers working on similar topics. But I was also a newcomer, still learning about the wider Wikimedia movement and the community behind the projects I had brought into my classroom.

I had designed and taught my first Wikipedia-based course at Abdullah Gül University in Kayseri, Türkiye, and I wanted to share what my students and I had learned. I also hoped to discover new tools, meet people with similar interests, and explore opportunities for future collaboration.

title: Queer mediums of the cult of María Lionza are redefining the gender binary in Venezuela’s sacred mountain
content:
Gender diversity, resistance and ritual cross-dressing in Venezuela's sacred cult

Originally published on Global Voices

Portrait of Wander Rodríguez, part of the María Dolores Rodríguez Caravan and its powers, and the LGBTIQ+ community. Sorte (Yaracuy, Venezuela). October 12. Freisy González Portales. Used with permission.

In Venezuela, Spiritism as a religion is part of the collective imagination, of our identity; popular beliefs and ritual practices that take us back to our ancestors in colonial times. Over the years, Spiritism has evolved into a vibrant, contemporary national cult centered on the figure of María Lionza as the principal protector of waters and the charms of nature, a figure who challenges the notions of the patriarchal state and opposes monotheistic religions.

This religious system has been studied in depth by anthropologists in our country (Daisy Barreto, Angelina Pollak-Eltz, Michelle Asencio, Francisco Ferrándiz, Cesar Escalona, among others), which I had read about and found interesting at the time, but which I later witnessed for the first time in its most important sites, such as Quibayo and Sorte, in the state of Yaracuy, Venezuela.

title: Chinese Scam Boss Murdered in Sri Lanka Had Multiple Identities
content:
A Chinese cyber scam boss who was kidnapped and murdered in Sri Lanka’s capital in July went by three separate aliases and carried at least two passports, according to documents obtained by OCCRP and The Sunday Times.

Chen Guoqing, 31, was abducted from the Colombo Port City special economic zone in the early hours of July 23 by a group of over a dozen men, one of them brandishing a pistol, according to a copy of the police investigative report into the incident. He was driven to a rural area over 70 kilometers east of Colombo, tortured to death, and his body was abandoned.

The murder of Chen — and the hunt for his killers — received extensive media coverage in Sri Lanka, amid fears that the South Asian country is becoming a new base for Asian criminal syndicates that target victims around the world with sophisticated online fraud schemes.

title: Wikimedia Foundation Senior Manager Veronica Thamaini Visits Dagbani Wikimedians User Group in Tamale
content:
On October 8–9, 2026, the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group (DWUG) had the pleasure of hosting Veronica Thamaini, Senior Manager of Regional Funding Programs at the Wikimedia Foundation, at its office in Tamale, Ghana. The two-day visit provided an opportunity to showcase our work across the Mabia language communities, reflect on our achievements, discuss ongoing challenges, and explore opportunities to strengthen and sustain our impact.

The visit combined cultural exploration with strategic discussions on language preservation, free knowledge, education, community development, and the future of Wikimedia projects in Ghana.

On October 8, we visited Red Clay Studio and the Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art (SCCA) in Tamale to explore the region’s vibrant creative and cultural landscape, learn more about initiatives preserving and promoting artistic expression, and share some of the cultural spaces that make northern Ghana unique.

The visits also underscored the importance of documenting and making cultural knowledge accessible, values that closely align with our commitment to preserving and sharing knowledge through Wikimedia projects.

title: Wikimedia Jakarta Community’s Bonding Night Trip: Exploring Knowledge and Building Togetherness in the Land of the Kanekes Baduy Luar
content:
The community event of bonding night, known as Makrab (Malam Keakraban), returned as part of GSF26, with the Wikimedia Jakarta Community warmly and enthusiastically welcoming the occasion.

Coordinated by Kume Gucci and Hzu Hzu, who served as treasurer, the event brought together 13 participants for a community bonding night trip in Kanekes, home to the Baduy people.

The event took place on September 5–6, 2026, in the Kanekes area, Leuwidamar District, Lebak Regency, Banten Province. This year’s Wikimedia Jakarta Community bonding trip focused on Kanekes, Lebak, Banten, which is known as the home of the Baduy people.

The location was chosen because of its relatively close proximity to Jakarta and its potential to offer insights into local culture and ways of life that could be documented and shared through Wikimedia projects, particularly Wikimedia Commons and Wikivoyage.

title: Lara Croft is 30! We look at the video game icon’s biggest blunders
content:
We all know the highlights of the tomb raider’s storied career – but what about the lowlights? We dig deep to unearth the archaeologist’s less glorious moments

Happy birthday, Lara! This month marks 30 years since Ms Croft first swan-dived into our lives with her unique blend of athletic prowess, archaeological expertise and giant knockers. More than 100 million Tomb Raider games have been sold since. We all remember the good times: the bold design and sheer playability of the original titles; the establishment of Lara as a 90s icon, embodying both lads’ mag culture and girl power; the way she made games cool, even appearing on the cover of the Face. We’ve had blockbuster movies, big budget reboots, and shiny reissues. And who could forget the time we got to powerwash her house?

But no one gets to 30 without a few skeletons in the closet – or in Lara’s case, butlers in the freezer. So here’s a look at the darker parts of her past.

The Content Partnerships Hub Helpdesk helps Wikimedians to find support for collaborations that bring knowledge and freely reusable content to Wikimedia projects: whether you are exploring your first partnership or navigating a challenge in an established project, the Helpdesk offers a place to ask questions and connect with relevant experience across the movement.

The Hub involves many different kinds of work. title: Tutkija: Yksi tilasto ei anna kokonaiskuvaa rikollisuudesta – poliisikin kuulee vain osan laittomuuksista
content:
Rikoksia kirjattiin viime vuonna 30 000 enemmän kuin vuotta aiemmin. Karulta kuulostaa. Onko se kuitenkaan koko totuus rikollisuudesta ja sen kehityksestä Suomessa? Yliopistonlehtori Matti Näsin mukaan ei.

Kriminologian ja oikeuspolitiikan instituutissa (Krimo) Helsingin yliopistossa työskentelevän Näsin mukaan rikollisuuden määrässä tapahtuu lopulta melko vähän muutoksia, vaikka mediasta ja julkisesta keskustelusta voi saada toisenlaisen kuvan.

– Se on iso valtamerialus, joka kääntyy tosi hitaasti, hän kuvailee rikollisuuden kehitystä pitkällä aikavälillä.

Usein uutisoinnin kärjessä on poliisin tietoon tullut rikollisuus. Näissä tilastoissa näkyy Näsin mukaan yleensä enemmän vaihtelua.

Viranomaisten kirjaamien rikosten määrän vaikuttavat monet asiat lainsäädännön muutoksista poliisin käytössä oleviin resursseihin ja siihen, miten niitä kohdennetaan.

– Se elää tosi paljon, mutta se otetaan ikään kuin enemmän totena ja indikaattorina väkivallan kehityksestä, vaikka kokonaiskuva on huomattavasti laajempi. Poliisin tietoon tullut on vain jäävuoren huippu rikollisuudesta ja pelkästään sen pohjalta johtopäätösten vetäminen on aika haastavaa, Näsi sanoo.

title: Murals for free culture: Schools in Córdoba celebrate Wikipedia’s 25th anniversary
content:
Painting the mural at the Gobernador López school (Córdoba, Argentina)

The “25×25 Celebrando Wikipedia” project took place between February and September 2026 in Córdoba, Argentina, where we commemorated and celebrated Wikipedia’s 25th anniversary through the collective creation of two Wikipedia-inspired murals, while promoting Wikimedia projects, open access, and Creative Commons licenses. Implemented in one primary school and one secondary school in partnership with the Colectivo Artístico ALLI -Arte Libre Laboratorio e Innovación, the project involved students in learning activities about Wikipedia and in artistic production, which culminated in the painting of the murals together with families and community organizations.

The process, documented and shared on Wikimedia Commons, included workshops on Wikimedia projects, particularly Wikipedia, as well as on free culture and Creative Commons licenses.

Students designed images based on what they had learned, representing the philosophy of Wikipedia, Wikimedia Commons, and free culture. They then decided which images would go on the mural, as well as the colors to be used.

There are more autocracies in the world in 2026 than there are democracies. Some researchers identify digital authoritarianism as the use of digital technology by regimes to surveil, repress, and manipulate domestic and foreign populations. title: The Old Bus Was an Adventure. Will the New One Last?
content:
A schoolboy commuter’s memories of Sri Lanka in the 1980s and 90s — and a look at the country’s new Metro Bus service.

By Feroz Deen*

COLOMBO | 24 October 2026 (IDN) — In the 1980s and 90s, catching a bus in Sri Lanka was an adventure. Getting on was a struggle, never mind getting a seat. As teenagers, hanging on the footboard of a bus was the equivalent of a Sathutu Uyana jet ride at Viharamahadevi Park — the only theme park many Sri Lankan kids had access to back then.

As I grew older, I realised how dangerous — and potentially fatal — riding on the footboard could be. I would never encourage anyone to do it today.

On the bus, passengers smoked despite signs prohibiting it. It was a time when smoking was taken much more lightly. I remember a friend of mine, arrogant as only a teenager can be, telling off an older man for lighting up. Nobody was quite sure who had won.

On the way home from Wesley College, Borella Junction was the big stop. The driver wouldn’t move until he had collected his quota of passengers. And if another bus tried to overtake, the Grand Prix would begin.
snippet:
A schoolboy commuter’s memories of Sri Lanka in the 1980s and 90s — and a look at the country’s new Metro Bus service.

title: Starlink connection restored at high speed in Ukraine, defense minister says
content:
SpaceX’s Starlink and Starshield satellite communications services have been restored in Ukraine, allowing the country’s forces to operate drones at high speed, Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said on Saturday.

“The Ministry of Defense’s monitoring systems indicate that Starlink/Starshield speeds have been restored,” Khmara told reporters in WhatsApp messages. “We are recording speeds exceeding 400 km/h, and the connection is stable.”

Since last week, Kyiv had been reporting speed limits on Starshield, Starlink’s military-grade service, affecting Ukraine’s ability to use drones and carry out defensive strikes. The throttling came amid growing tensions between Washington and Kyiv, with Trump blaming President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for the continuation of the war with Russia.

On Friday, Ukrainian officials told POLITICO that drones continued to lose signal at speeds above 160 km/h, despite U.S. President Donald Trump saying on Thursday that SpaceX CEO Elon Musk had “put it back.” British Prime Minister Andy Burnham raised the issue in a phone call with Trump on Friday.
snippet: SpaceX’s Starlink and Starshield satellite communications services have been restored in Ukraine, allowing the country’s forces to operate drones at high speed, Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said

title: Lakkasiko Suomi auttamasta palestiinalaispakolaisia? Hallituksen UNRWA-päätös puntarissa
content:

YK:n palestiinalaispakolaisjärjestö UNRWA on ajettu ahtaalle, ja Suomi on liittynyt järjestön rahoituksen lakkauttaneiden maiden joukkoon muun muassa Yhdysvaltojen ja Ruotsin rinnalla. Samaan aikaan Suomi jatkaa puolustusmateriaaliyhteistyötä Israelin kanssa, korostaa monenkeskisen järjestelmän ja kansainvälisen oikeuden kunnioittamista ulkopolitiikkansa perustana ja kampanjoi pääsystä YK:n turvallisuusneuvoston vaihtuvaksi jäseneksi.

Miten rahoituksen supistuminen näkyy UNRWAn toiminnassa, ja miten Suomen päätös vetäytyä pois rahoittajamaiden joukosta asettuu osaksi Suomen ulkopolitiikan suuria linjoja? Onnistuuko Suomi säilyttämään ulkopoliittisen uskottavuutensa kotimaisen ja kansainvälisen yhteisön silmissä? Näitä kysymyksiä ruoditaan The Ulkopolitistin syyskauden kolmannessa jaksossa. title: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield
content:
We’ve heard much about the end of the west. At the proposed summit between Trump, Putin and Xi, those fears could crystallise

In the final two years of a US presidency, when Congress has been lost, approval ratings have sunk like a stone and their party has started to think about who’s coming next, the person occupying the Oval Office can feel their power draining away. Domestic legislation, particularly in an era where bipartisan cooperation is almost nonexistent, grinds to a halt. But as the days tick by until the end, and as presidents begin to think about their legacy, there is one part of the job where they still have power: the rest of the world.

In the final weeks of his presidency in 1992 George HW Bush sent 28,000 American troops to Somalia to help end a famine. For Bill Clinton, it was a quixotic attempt to bring peace to the Middle East by ending the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Barack Obama restored diplomatic ties with Cuba, making a historic visit to Havana, as well as a final, successful push on the Iran nuclear deal.

title: In Brazil’s elections, big techs’ transparency and cooperation policies translate as governance washing, according to this expert
content:

Originally published on Global Voices

Art by Global Voices, created in Canva Pro.

Amid a series of corruption scandals, the 2026 general election in Brazil is also flooded with headlines about social media companies’ role in the campaign. Users supporting the candidacy of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the incumbent center-left candidate running for re-election, have been reporting a sudden drop in their Instagram Stories views when posting about politics. They say that Meta AI refused to generate images featuring Lula’s name and party number, while delivering the same request for Flávio Bolsonaro, his far-right opponent and the son of the imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro.

On October 16, Meta admitted technical problems on its platforms which affected how pro-Lula content was delivered to users. As reported by the Associated Press, despite acknowledging “global technical glitches, strict anti-fraud measures, and regulatory compliance rather than targeted suppression,” the company that owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook denied any political bias.

title: Inside the cyber flaw scramble that brought the AI threat to life
content:
The exposure was immense, with AI multiplying the risks — and yet time-tested global cybersecurity procedures appeared to be functioning. Then suddenly, it all broke down.        

The decision by a cybersecurity company on Wednesday to prematurely release information about a flaw in the popular PHP computer programming language left much of the web exposed to hackers, triggering a panic that brought to life months of warnings of how the AI-powered era could cause widespread damage.

The flaws in PHP, discovered using AI tools through a months-long process coordinated by OpenAI, caused cyber agencies across Europe, the U.S., the U.K., Australia and Canada to post urgent warnings Wednesday. Numerous governments took websites offline as a precaution.

While no major hacking damage was immediately apparent, the way the incident unfolded over 72 hours showed how easily cybersecurity processes can break down and the outsized consequences of cyber risks in the AI era.
snippet: The exposure was immense, with AI multiplying the risks — and yet time-tested global cybersecurity procedures appeared to be functioning. Then suddenly, it all broke down.

title: The datacentre next door: on the frontline of tech’s latest David v Goliath battle
content:
The AI boom is pitting local residents against corporate giants seeking to power their energy-hungry networks – but one Welsh city is fighting back

Dale Johnston opens the gate to his neat suburban garden on the western fringes of Newport in South Wales. There’s a trampoline and a slide on the lawn for his grandchildren, and chairs for him and his wife. He should be enjoying the light draining from the perfect autumnal sky – but almost his entire view is blotted out by a vast expanse of prefabricated panels.

The 23 metre-high grey hulk looming over him and his neighbours is a hyperscale datacentre. It is heralded by the area’s Labour politicians as a job creator, yet all Johnston can think about is what he has lost: “Before, the sun used to come around here and it was lovely.” The way residents have been treated is “disgusting”.

title: Israel/OPT: Elections must not deflect attention from Israel’s international crimes
content:
Ahead of parliamentary elections in Israel on 27 October, Erika Guevara Rosas, Amnesty International’s Senior Director for Research, Policy, Advocacy and Campaigns said:

“While much of the world’s attention is focused on Israel’s upcoming parliamentary elections, Palestinians who have endured decades of crimes and systematic violations at the hands of successive Israeli governments have little reason to expect the outcome to deliver positive human rights change.  

“In recent months, electoral candidates have shamelessly exploited anti-Palestinian sentiment or even threatened to step up human rights violations and crimes under international law in a bid to score political points. Candidates have used dehumanizing rhetoric against Palestinians, promised to further entrench Israel’s illegal annexation measures in the occupied West Bank, and threatened further devastation of the occupied Gaza Strip. Candidates across the political spectrum also pushed for the disqualification of Sami Abu Shehadeh, Palestinian citizen of Israel and chairperson of the Tajammou’ (Balad) party, displaying utter disregard for the right to freedom of association, expression, and assembly.

title: Chart: A record two-thirds of car sales in China are now electric vehicles
content:
• NEV record
  • Impact of Hormuz
  • NEV demand down 
  • Exports surge

    • For the first time, new-energy vehicles (NEVs) made up 67% of new car sales in China in September, according to the latest data from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA).

    The figures show that NEVs, which include battery electric cars and plug-in hybrids, captured a record share of sales, even though fewer were sold than last year.

    This is because sales of combustion-engine cars are falling steeply, a trend that the CPCA has attributed to rising petrol prices following the start of the Hormuz crisis.

    Indeed, sales of fuel-only cars were down 31% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, with plug-in hybrid sales down 26% – whereas battery EV sales were only down 4%.

    One analyst tells Carbon Brief that China’s rapidly growing EV fleet has offset demand for 143m barrels of oil since the start of the Hormuz crisis.

    Another says that the crisis is “reinforcing China’s electrification of road transport”.

    Meanwhile, amid slowing domestic sales, Chinese carmakers’ exports of NEVs more than doubled [in 2026 to date / in September] from a year earlier.

title: Ukraine Combats AI Cyberattacks
content:
Hackers associated with the FSB secret service or the Russian General Staff are unleashing AI tools to break into Ukrainian IT networks. Once inside, Russian AI agents move on their own from machine to machine and report back to human operators, who then decide whether to steal data, plant malware, or shut down the service.  

AI allows for cheap, fast cyber-attacks. While hackers previously used the technology for isolated tasks like writing phishing emails, AI is behind a 2500% increase in low-severity attacks for the first half of 2026, compared to the previous year.

Targets range from law enforcement agencies to private notaries and medical institutions. Some attacks jam military mobile devices. Others generate fake air raid alerts. And still others steal geolocation, photos, contacts, and call logs.

title: "Dying in Detention": Al Jazeera Investigates Immigrant Deaths in California's Adelanto ICE Jail
content:
At least 59 people have died in ICE custody since the start of President Donald Trump’s second term, the highest number in more than a decade. Many deaths have been linked to medical neglect, including four of five recent deaths at California’s Adelanto Processing Center, according to a 2026 report by the state attorney general. Al Jazeera English’s Fault Lines investigated deaths at the facility, which is operated by the private prison company GEO Group, in the new documentary Dying in Detention.

“GEO Group has made over a billion dollars in profits from immigration detention. They have given more than a million dollars … to help reelect Donald Trump,” says correspondent Natasha Del Toro. “That raises a lot of questions for us about the relationship between GEO and the federal government, and some of these conflicts of interest.”

title: Ville Skinnari: Tieteen vapaus vaarantuu, jos asiantuntijakin joutuu varomaan sanomisiaan
content:
Olemme tottuneet pitämään Suomea avoimena yhteiskuntana, jossa tieto ja kriittinen ajattelu ohjaavat päätöksentekoa. Mutta kuinka vapaata ajattelumme lopulta nykyilmapiirissä on?

Tieteellisten seurain valtuuskunta nosti kesällä kannanotossaan esiin huolestuttavan kehityksen. Tieteen vapaus on Suomessa heikentynyt.

Kansainvälisessä akateemisen vapauden vertailussa Suomen sijoitus on pudonnut 38 sijaa kahdessa vuodessa. Myös suomalaiset tutkijat kertovat lisääntyneestä paineesta ja itsesensuurista.

Suomessa on vahva konsensuksen kulttuuri. Erityisesti ulko- ja turvallisuuspolitiikassa yhteisen linjan merkitystä on korostettu vuosikymmeniä. Pienelle maalle yhtenäisyys on ollut vahvuus.

Samalla meidän pitäisi kysyä, kuinka hyvin siedämme näkemyksiä, jotka eroavat kulloinkin vallitsevasta käsityksestä.

POLIITTINEN yhteisymmärrys voi olla arvokasta, mutta sen rinnalla tarvitaan avointa ja riippumatonta asiantuntijakeskustelua. Puhumattakaan rohkeista, systeemisistä avauksista.

Saako ulko- ja turvallisuuspolitiikan tutkija kyseenalaistaa Suomen valintoja ilman, että hänen asiantuntemuksensa asetetaan epäilyksenalaiseksi?

title: ECCCH-ACCESS Project Kick-off in Ankara
content:
Held in Ankara on the 2nd October 2026, the ECCCH-ACCESS Project Kick-Off introduced the project’s aim to connect cultural heritage institutions in Turkey (Türkiye) with the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH) ecosystem.

Coordinated by Koç University Suna Kıraç Library and KARMA Lab, in partnership with MÜZEDER, Europa Nostra Türkiye, and Ankara AKS, the event featured presentations introducing the ECHOES consortium and the ECCCH approach, followed by a panel exploring experiences and practices in cultural heritage digitisation in Turkey.

The ECCCH process

ECCCH-ACCESS combines four complementary components:

  • awareness and community expansion through webinars and outreach activities;
  • sector mapping and feedback collection through surveys and moderated discussions;
  • knowledge translation through a dedicated website, multilingual training materials, and
  • AI-assisted dissemination; and participatory engagement through hackathons and co-design sessions.

    • Activities will engage museums, archaeological projects, libraries, researchers, and heritage professionals across Turkey through established institutional and professional networks.

title: The Vulnerability Apocalypse and Why We Should Fund Open Source
content:
If you use the internet at all, you may have noticed that a large percentage of sites suddenly went down earlier this week—and all your nerdiest friends were talking about "The Vulnerability Apocalypse” and this thing called PHP that powers nearly 70% of the websites on the internet. You may find yourself wondering: what is PHP, what just happened, what is the vulnerability apocalypse, and what do I need to do?  

To find out what you can personally do read the first blog post in this series!  

PHP is a programming language used mainly to create interactive websites. Facebook, Wordpress, Wikipedia, Etsy, and other major sites all use or were originally built on PHP. It is a long-established mainstay of web development. But because it is open-source, maintenance of these critical systems depends on a small number of volunteers working on this in their free time. The disaster scenario that happened this past week is the perfect example of why we need more money and people supporting open-source projects. Corporations should be contributing both.

title: Amnesty: Uudet tiedot Sudanin Al-Faširista paljastavat ihmisten elävän kidutuksen, nälän ja pelon keskellä
content:
Maailman johtajat eivät ole onnistuneet puuttumaan Al-Faširin asukkaiden epätoivoiseen tilanteeseen sen jälkeen, kun sisällissodan osapuolena taistelevat puolisotilaalliset RSF-joukot valtasivat kaupungin väkivaltaisesti lokakuussa 2025. Humanitaaristen järjestöjen mukaan kaupungissa asuu nykyisin alle 70 000 ihmistä, kun ennen sotaa asukkaita oli yli miljoona.

Amnestyn haastattelemat ihmiset, jotka selviytyivät kaupungin verisestä valtaamisesta, kuvaavat Al-Faširia täysin tuhoutuneeksi: julkinen infrastruktuuri, viranomaisrakennukset ja sairaalat ovat raunioina. Humanitaarisen avun pääsy kaupunkiin on erittäin rajallista. RSF valvoo jatkuvasti sekä avustustyöntekijöitä että siviilejä.

”RSF-joukot väittävät, että Al-Faširiin on turvallista palata kaupungissa tapahtuneiden hirvittävien joukkomurhien jälkeen. Todellisuus on kuitenkin täysin toinen”, toteaa Amnestyn pääsihteeri Agnès Callamard.

Välkommen till en konsert som rör sig i gränslandet mellan affekternas anatomi, naturmystik och musikalisk extas. Barockens känsloträdgård var vildvuxen och prunkande. Musiken tilldelades den fruktsamma uppgiften att gestalta själens innersta skiftningar och blottlägga hjärtats flora. Här möts jordisk passion och himmelsk hängivenhet i arior där kärleken blomstrar i triumferande glans, för att i nästa stund snärjas i sorg och förlust.

Genom konserten löper en tråd av samtida kärleksdikt från våra nordliga breddgrader, som tillsammans med nutida lyrik från Finland ger röst åt samma tidlösa längtan som barocktonsättarna fångade.

  • Karolina Åsberg, mezzosopran
  • Ingrid Rådholm Konvicka, alt
  • Mariangiola Martello, cembalo
  • Magnus Lanning, cello

title: In Bosnia and Herzegovina, children with Down syndrome are using a video game to safely navigate the internet
content:
A virtual assistant called Sol the Owl guides kids through the game

Originally published on Global Voices

SafeClick is a video game that teaches children with Down syndrome about digital safety. A virtual assistant, Sol the Owl, that guides them through the game. Image by the game's developers, used with permission.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement. 

Like their peers, children and young people with Down syndrome are curious about technology and the internet, but there are often no suitable, dedicated tools to help them learn how to safely navigate the web. This is true in Bosnia and Herzegovina as well, where children with cognitive disabilities are underserved and tend to end up in digital isolation because of caregivers’ concerns about digital safety and the risks of being online.

title: Two Prisoners Executed in Mashhad Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Haal Vsh, two prisoners were executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad on Tuesday, October 20, 2026.

The prisoners have been identified as Abdollah Narouei (Hashem Shavabzehi), approximately 43 years old, a father of five, originally from Zahedan and residing in Mashhad, and Issa Narouei (Lakzehi), 30 years old, son of Osman, unmarried, originally from Zahedan and residing in Mashhad.

According to the report, Abdollah Narouei was arrested by security forces at his home in Mashhad on November 3, 2023. He was subsequently sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court of Mashhad in December 2025–January 2026 on drug-related charges. His execution was carried out without allowing him a final visit with his family.

Issa Narouei was also arrested by security forces at his home in Mashhad in 2025–2026. He was subsequently sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court of Mashhad on drug-related charges.

As of the time of this report, the executions of these prisoners have not been officially announced by prison authorities or the relevant institutions.

title: Mexico: Delay in Legal Reform Harms People With Disabilities
content:
(Mexico City) – Mexico’s Senate should amend legislation approved by the Chamber of Deputies on October 20, 2026, to ensure that people with disabilities can appoint supporters to make legal decisions by April 1, 2027, as originally planned, Human Rights Watch said today. The current legislation would postpone the deadline for implementing the National Code of Civil and Family Procedures, which requires these appointments, to July 1, 2031.

The code, adopted in June 2023, introduced reforms to improve access to justice and guarantee the right of people with disabilities throughout Mexico to make legally recognized decisions. However, implementation has lagged. Mexico City is the only jurisdiction to have declared the code partially in force, including provisions allowing adults to designate supporters to help them exercise their legal capacity.

title: Renewing the Momentum for Rights-based Poverty Reduction in Asia and the Pacific
content:
By Katinka Weinberger and Mizuho Okimoto-Kaewtathip*

BANGKOK | 23 October 2026 (IDN) — Eradicating poverty in all its forms is one of the most pressing development challenges across Asia and the Pacific. While the region has made remarkable progress in reducing poverty over recent decades, multiple and overlapping crises have exposed the fragility of these achievements and highlighted how easily gains can be reversed.

Poverty is a dynamic phenomenon shaped by structural drivers that reinforce vulnerability and widen inequalities across societies and generations. Economic growth has been the main driver of poverty reduction in the region, but inequality has weakened its impact and undermined the full benefits of this progress. Inequalities slow economic progress and trap many countries in chronic poverty patterns that can persist across generations.

title: Kutsu: Writing of Disaster @ Viirus GUEST
content:
Viirus GUEST: Writing of Disaster
Jenni-Elina von Bagh ja työryhmä
Näyttämöllinen kirjoitus elämästä ja tuhosta

Writing of Disaster on koreografinen melodraama ja postfarssi. Siinä tuho ja elämä kulkevat käsi kädessä ja luovat ruumiillisia murtumia ilon ja tragedian välille. Teos on näyttämöllinen sovitus Maurice Blanchotin filosofisesta teoksesta ”The Writing of a Disaster” (suom.Tuhon kirjoitus/ Viljami Hukka, 2024). Voiko tuhon tuhasta löytyä uusi alku, ja miten se löydetään?

Teoksessa kolme kokenutta esiintyjää tutkivat epäonnistumisen komiikkaa – olemisemme reunamia ja pimeää pistettä, posthumaanisia voimia, kauhun ja naurun herkullista tasapainoa.

Esiintyjät ammentavat ruumiin omasta vaeltavasta tapahtumarikkaudesta, joka syntyy epäkäytännöllisistä, naurettavista ja itse asetetuista haasteista. Teos löytää jatkuvasti uusia tapoja ilmaista itseään, sotkeentua, kaatua ja jälleen koota itseään — pohtia elämän ihmeellisyyttä, sitä, että olemme elossa.

Neljä viimeistä esitystä toteutetaan yhteistyössä Liikkeellä marraskuussa -festivaalin kanssa.

title: Energiakriisi on vienyt Kuuban koulut uuteen normaaliin: Ei koulupukupakkoa eikä aina kirjojakaan
content:
Kun kuubalainen koululainen lähtee aamulla kouluun, hänen ei enää tarvitse pukea koulupukua.

”Lukuvuoden alussa kerrottiin, että tänä vuonna säännöistä joustetaan. Jos kotona ei ole sähköä tai vettä eikä univormua saada pestyä, lapsen voi lähettää tunnille t-paidassa ja housuissa”, havannalainen äiti Jennifer Suárez kertoo.

Kuuban uusi lukuvuosi alkoi syyskuussa. Resurssi-, polttoaine- ja rahapula näkyvät koulujen arjessa. Oppilaisiin kohdistuvia vaatimuksia on siksi höllennetty ja opetusta mukautettu olosuhteisiin.

Suárezin tytär aloitti alakoulun toisen luokan. Hän saa opetusta kaikissa tarvittavissa oppiaineissa niihin koulutetuilta opettajilta, mikä ei ole Kuubassa nykyisin itsestään selvää.

Opetusministeri Naima Trujillon mukaan lukuvuoden alkaessa maan 135 000 opettajan tehtävistä oli täytetty vain 73 prosenttia.

Opettajia on jo vuosien ajan lähtenyt ulkomaille tai siirtynyt muille aloille matalien palkkojen vuoksi. Opettajapula vaikuttaa noin 1,4 miljoonan lapsen ja nuoren koulunkäyntiin.

title: Noema’s AI Reading List
content:
AI’s climb up the capability ladder is moving more rapidly, even exponentially, than its progenitors expected. To keep up and put it in perspective, Noema has compiled a reading list of our best essays and interviews from a couple of years ago through the present. No doubt, we will need a new list again a few months down the road.

For now, here is a resource for following the trajectory of the most important technological breakthrough of this century so far.

1. How To Future-Proof Your Career In The Age Of AI

The most prized workers will be those who can decode a sea of outputs, spot the meaningful signal and translate it into action that others understand and trust.

by Nils Gilman

2. Whose AI Will Rule The World

As AI changes everything, the Chinese seem more optimistic than the Americans. Why?

by Jacob Dreyer

3. How AI Will Change Us

When the most patient, well-read, emotionally responsive conversationalist in the world is always available, what will we still need from one another?

by Houda Nait El Barj

4. AI Could Actually Help Rebuild The Middle Class

AI doesn’t have to be a job destroyer. It offers us the opportunity to extend expertise to a larger set of workers.

by David Autor

title: Cyprus Parliament Reviews Reports on Abramovich-Linked Asset Transfers
content:
The Cypriot Parliament this week discussed recent revelations about corporate maneuvers that allowed firms ultimately owned by Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich to sidestep tax and transparency requirements.

The parliamentary hearings followed an investigation last week by OCCRP, CIReN, BBC, and TBIJ. The reports detailed how the Cyprus affiliate of multinational accountancy firm Deloitte, and corporate service provider MeritServus, worked together to backdate documents relating to companies beneficially owned by Abramovich. 

Doing so helped the companies retroactively transfer billions of dollars in assets from Cyprus to the British Virgin Islands, where they would not be subject to Cypriot laws on tax and public disclosure. 

OCCRP reached out to Deloitte’s offices in Cyprus and internationally for comment on the parliamentary hearing, but did not receive a response by the time of publication. Deloitte Cyprus previously told OCCRP it "acts in compliance with applicable laws."

MeritServus has been dissolved and it was not possible to obtain a comment.

title: Watch Rome Rise, Fall, and Rise Again in a Three-Minute 3D Timelapse
content:
Scholars disagree on when, exactly, Rome fell. But if you watch the new video from City 3D Timelapse above, you’ll understand the lack of debate on the question of whether it fell. Around the turn of the sixth century AD, buildings start vanishing at a rate that soon turns alarming; long before the end of the first millennium, it’s clear that Rome has been plunged into very hard times indeed. In the video’s accelerated visual history, that much-scrutinized 500-year span passes in a little more than five seconds. Just one minute later, it has spread not just beyond the old city limits, but beyond the very frame of the aerial view, becoming the vast urbanized region we know today.

Legend has it that Rome was founded in 753 BC, when Romulus killed his twin brother Remus. As reflected by the video, archaeological evidence suggests that the area was settled earlier, though the traditional date of Rome’s founding roughly coincides with the emergence of what we know as the Roman Kingdom.

title: Presidentti Stubb: Suomella ja Mongolialla on paljon yhteistä
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb isännöi Mongolian presidentti Ukhnaa Khurelsukhin työvierailua Suomeen perjantaina 23. lokakuuta 2026.

Presidentti Stubb ja presidentti Khurelsukh tapasivat Presidentinlinnassa, jossa he keskustelivat Suomen ja Mongolian kahdenvälisten suhteiden lisäksi alueellisista turvallisuuskysymyksistä ja monenvälisestä yhteistyöstä.

”Suomella ja Mongolialla on paljon yhteistä. Arvostamme molemmat demokratiaa ja vakautta. Olemme molemmat pieniä maita suurten naapureiden vieressä sekä monenvälisen järjestelmän ja YK:n tukijoita”, presidentti Stubb sanoi keskustelun alussa.

Presidentti Stubb kertoi myös ajankohtaisen päivityksen Euroopan turvallisuustilanteesta ja Venäjän hyökkäyssodasta Ukrainassa.

Vierailun aikana allekirjoitettiin neljä yhteisymmärryspöytäkirjaa. Suomi ja Mongolia tiivistävät yhteistyötä koulutuksen ja kulttuurin aloilla.

Iltapäivällä presidentit osallistuivat Suomen ja Mongolian väliseen yritystapahtumaan Säätytalolla. Yksi työvierailun tavoitteista oli vahvistaa Suomen ja Mongolian välistä kauppaa. Presidentti Khurelsukhin mukana oli lähes 70 henkilön kokoinen yritysvaltuuskunta.

title: After Millions in Stolen SNAP Benefits, Trump Administration Moves to Fight Theft
content:
The Trump administration this week announced an overhaul of the nation’s food stamp payment system, aimed at modernizing benefit cards to protect families from electronic theft. The move comes a week after ProPublica published an investigation showing how $470 million in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, benefits were stolen from recipients last year alone, in large part because these cards are technologically outdated.

ProPublica’s story highlighted victims’ experiences and examined repeated failures by Congress and the U.S. Department of Agriculture to upgrade Electronic Benefits Transfer, or EBT, cards nationally. ProPublica’s reporting was shared around the department, according to two USDA officials.

title: ”On ristiriitaista, että kirjastolainaamiseen kannustetaan, mutta tekijöiden tulot laskevat” Kirjallisuuskahveilla keskusteltiin lainauskorvauksen tasosta
content:
Sanasto järjesti torstaina 22.10. eduskunnan sivistysvaliokunnalle ja sivistys- ja tiedejaostolle perinteiset Kirjallisuuskahvit. Lainauskorvauksen 20-vuotisjuhlavuosi lähenee, mutta tekijöille maksettava lainakohtainen korvaus uhkaa pudota jo alle sen tason, jossa se oli 10 vuotta sitten. 

Kirjallisuuskahvien avauspuheenvuossa Sanaston puheenjohtaja Maria Lassila-Merisalo kertoi toimineensa puheenjohtajan tehtävässä pian vuoden ajan, mutta Sanaston kirjallisuuskummen joukossa hän on ollut kuluneen hallituskauden alusta asti. Näiden neljän vuoden ajan kansanedustajille on viety samoja viestejä – lainauskorvauksen määrärahaa tulisi korottaa, verkkokirjahyllyt ja Celian sähköiset lainat tulisi saada korvauksen piiriin. Kirjallisuuskahvit alkoivat Lassila-Merisalon kysymyksellä siitä, miksi kirjallisuuden tekijöille tärkeät asiat eivät etene, vaikka mainitut asiat saavat kansanedustajien keskuudessa kannatusta yli puoluerajojen.

title: PHP2Shell exposes the funding gap in open-source security
content:
On 21 October 2026, the PHP project released fixes for two critical security vulnerabilities, collectively known as PHP2Shell. Under certain conditions, these vulnerabilities could allow attackers to execute code on affected web servers without authentication.

PHP underpins a substantial share of the web, including public services, businesses, and widely used publishing platforms. The incident highlights a fundamental challenge in open-source security: finding vulnerabilities is only the first step. Fixing them, and preventing similar flaws in the future, requires sustained investment.

In 2024, the Sovereign Tech Agency funded the first external security audit of PHP’s core in over a decade, coordinated by OSTIF and conducted by Quarkslab. The audit identified 17 security-related findings and contributed to subsequent work on the underlying problem behind one of the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. The organization explicitly recognised the value of this investment.

title: Unga skribenter värnar om sin egen röst i en tid av AI
content:
Wilhelmina Meyer från Gymnasiet Lärkan i Helsingfors vinner årets ”Argh? – kolumntävlingen för dig som har något på hjärtat”. I novelltävlingen ”Vad händer?” för årskurserna 7-9 tar Saga Saloviin från Winellska skolan i Kyrkslätt hem segern.

Kolumner och noveller är utmanande genrer. På Helsingfors bokmässa prisbelönas åtta unga som skriver med personlig närhet, samhällsengagemang och språklig säkerhet.

Under våren ordnade Svenska modersmålslärarföreningen i Finland (SMLF) två skrivtävlingar – en kolumntävling för studerande vid andra stadiet och en novelltävling för elever i årskurserna 7-9.

Många av bidragen i årets kolumntävling Argh? handlar om hur AI och algoritmer påverkar samhället. Samtidigt ser juryn en tydlig vilja hos skribenterna att tänka självständigt och skriva med en egen röst.

Psykisk ohälsa är ett tema som återkommer år efter år. I årets texter kommer temat nära, med skildringar av både egna och närståendes erfarenheter.

I novelltävlingen Vad händer? ser juryn en gemensam nämnare: det märks att skribenterna är vana läsare. De vet hur både intrig och språk driver en berättelse framåt och håller läsarens intresse vid liv.

title: Top ICC official urges EU to act ‘as soon as possible’ on US sanctions
content:
THE HAGUE — The European Commission should act “as soon as possible” to give clear guidance on U.S. sanctions against the International Criminal Court, its top administrative official told POLITICO in an interview.

Osvaldo Zavala Giler, who oversees the day-to-day functioning of the Hague-based court as the institution’s registrar, said his job became “preparing for sanctions” as the White House imposed an escalating regime of restrictions against it.

The Trump administration targeted prosecutors and judges from the court first in February 2025 before announcing blanket sanctions on Oct. 9 this year. The EU has repeatedly backed the Court against Washington, but it has resisted calls to activate a mechanism that would forbid firms from complying with U.S. laws.

That has agonized senior figures in The Hague. Zavala Giler said the Commission’s “lack of clarity” left private companies and NGOs in the dark over whether they should comply with sanctions decided by Washington — and what risks they face if they don’t.

title: ‘Black October’: cybersecurity experts sound the alarm over new era of AI-enabled hacking
content:
After discovery of severe bug in the PHP programming language, executives warn of ‘vulnerability tsunami’

Leaders in cybersecurity are sounding the alarm after the discovery of a major vulnerability this week. They are predicting that artificial intelligence tools will expose more fundamental weaknesses in global internet infrastructure in the months to come.

“I no longer think we’re going to be able to patch all bugs,” said Sam Altman on Thursday evening, joining the chorus of executives. In the midst of what’s being called “Black October”, for which researchers used AI to help identify critical flaws in a coding language that is used across millions of websites and may have been unpatched for years, tech executives are warning about the ways AI will be used both to identify and exploit security vulnerabilities at an unprecedented scale and pace.

title: US midterms: what a new Congress could – and could not – change for Europe
content:
US midterm elections traditionally attract fewer voters than presidential contests. But this year’s vote is drawing considerable attention at home and abroad, especially in Europe.

Europe has not even needed to wait for the election results to feel their impact. With fuel prices weighing on American voters, Donald Trump has recently reached a deal to start importing Russian diesel in the hope of lowering fuel prices before election day. It was a stunning reversal of years of US pressure on Moscow over its war against Ukraine.

The contrast with Europe is striking. On October 12, the EU adopted its largest single expansion of sanctions against Russia’s military-industrial complex, targeting 1,569 individuals and entities. Four days later, Trump waived major new US sanctions on Russia, under legislation he had signed just a few weeks before.

These decisions send an uncomfortable message to Kyiv and European capitals: pressure on Russia is not a given, and can be relaxed when US electoral interests take priority.

With Republican losses looking increasingly likely, US Congress could look very different in a few weeks. But could a new Congress change US-Europe relations?

title: Unlocking the secrets of the ‘Dragon Man’ skull – and what it reveals about human evolution
content:
In September 2018, China Daily ran a story that found its way to my desk. It featured the photograph of a beautifully preserved fossil skull with huge brow-ridges, with a caption speculating – wrongly, as it would turn out – that it belonged to a species of human known as Homo heidelbergensis.

The article told a remarkable story about the discovery of this fossil some 85 years earlier. Japanese forces had been occupying the city of Harbin in north-eastern China in 1933. They ordered a team of local workers to help build a railway bridge across the Songhua River.

The workers uncovered the skull in river deposits, and one of them hid it from the Japanese by lowering it down a disused well. Feeling ashamed of having worked for the enemy, he kept quiet about the find for many years. Finally some 80 years later he told his son and grandson as he lay dying, which led to the almost intact skull being recovered and later donated to Hebei Geo University near Beijing.

title: The Nordic-Baltic Eight policy brief: China’s green statecraft and NB8 Arctic security
content:
New publication in the NB8 policy brief series by Dana Dūda (LIIA), Konstantinas Andrijauskas (IIRPS VU) and Björn Cappelin (UI).

Energy dependence has become a geopolitical liability. Russia’s war against Ukraine, the US-Iran war and tensions with the Kingdom of Denmark over Greenland have all exposed the strategic weight of energy independence, critical minerals, and Arctic access. For the eight Nordic-Baltic states (NB8), the next vulnerability may emerge from the green transition itself, where China’s dominance in clean technologies and critical mineral processing can be converted into strategic leverage. Some dependence is unavoidable in the short term; the task is to manage it deliberately rather than let it accumulate by default. This policy brief argues for integrating green energy security and Arctic security within a one strategic framework, because the Arctic’s critical mineral resources, renewable energy infrastructure and emerging transport and digital connectivity projects are relevant to Europe’s efforts to strengthen its energy dependence. This brief proposes collective measures to limit strategic dependence on China in the long term.

content:
Date: 6 November, 2026

Time: 12.15-13.15

Place: Seminar Room 106, Language Center (Fabianinkatu 26, Helsinki)

Title: Walter Burley Griffin, the Canberra Plan and the Uses of History

Abstract:

A presentation in honor of the 150th anniversary of the birth of Walter Burley Griffin (1876-1937), Architect, Landscape Architect & City Planner.

This lecture will briefly survey Walter Burley Griffin’s career in America, Australia, and India, then focus on his major work, undertaken in association with his wife Marion Mahony Griffin (1871-1961): the design of Canberra, the Australian Federal Capital, winner of the international competition conducted by the Australian Government in 1911-1912. The interpretation, and misinterpretation of the ‘Griffin Legacy’ in the planning of Canberra will be critically examined as a case study in ’the uses of history’: the manner in which architectural history is deployed in the service of power and ideology.

title: Kuilu nais- ja miesvaltaisten alojen työelämän laadussa kasvanut hallituskaudella
content:
Suomen Ammattiliittojen Keskusjärjestön (SAK) uusi seurantatutkimus osoittaa, että työelämän laatu on heikentynyt naisvaltaisilla aloilla, kun taas miesvaltaisilla aloilla se on palannut lähelle huipputasoa. Erot ovat kasvaneet voimakkaasti Petteri Orpon hallituksen kaudella.

SAK:n julkaisema Hyvän työn mittari seuraa työelämän laatua keskusjärjestön kattamilla aloilla, joista suurimpia ovat teollisuus, yksityinen palveluala (esimerkiksi kaupat) ja julkinen sektori. Mittarin mukaan elpyminen vuoden 2024 notkahduksesta on tapahtunut vain osittain, ja nousu on ollut eritahtista eri toimialoilla. Selvimmin on elpynyt teollisuuden työntekijöiden työelämän laatu.

SAK:n mittaushistorian pahin kuoppa työelämän laadussa näkyi vuosien 2022–2024 luvuissa, jolloin laadultaan huonon työn osuus kasvoi järjestön aloilla kuudesta prosentista kymmeneen.

Naisvaltaisilla julkisilla palvelualoilla työelämän laatu on heikentynyt edelleen vuodesta 2024. Yksityisillä palvelualoilla 35 prosenttia työntekijöistä on laadultaan huonossa työssä. Julkisilla palvelualoilla huonon työn osuus on 25 prosenttia, mikä on sekin historiallisen korkea tulos. Laatua mitataan kymmenellä eri mittarilla.

title: Extremists have no idea what Norse mythology is really about
content: Thor, the Norse god of thunder, once visited the giant Utgard-Loki. The giant challenged him to empty a drinking horn, lift a cat, and wrestle an old woman. He failed all three and left questioning his power. As it turned out, Utgard-Loki had used magic to hide Thor's real opponents. He had been drinking from the ocean, and the cat was Jörmungandr, the gigantic sea serpent encircling the earth. The old lady? Old age itself. This is the Norse myth I remember most clearly. For most people across Scandinavia and Iceland, the old myths don’t play a big role in everyday life, but there are subtle signs of them. Weekdays, streets, and people are named after Norse gods, for instance. Or the countless TV shows, comics, books, and music inspired by old gods and myths. We don't know when and how Norse mythology started, but it was definitely practised in Scandinavia and Iceland in the late Iron Age (from 500 AD) and Viking Age (800-1050 AD). Northern Europe was then gradually Christianised around the year 1000, through missionaries and due to pressure from foreign trade from the south. title: Cuba: Two years after being named prisoners of conscience, Félix Navarro, Sayli Navarro and Roberto Pérez Fonseca must be released
content:
On 23 October 2024, Amnesty International named Félix Navarro, Sayli Navarro and Roberto Pérez Fonseca prisoners of conscience, concluding that they had been deprived of their liberty solely for peacefully exercising their human rights. Two years later, they remain unjustly imprisoned amid the continued politically motivated detention and repression of critical voices in Cuba.

In response, Ana Piquer, Amnesty International’s Americas Director, said:

“Two years after being named prisoners of conscience, Félix Navarro, Sayli Navarro and Roberto Pérez Fonseca remain unjustly deprived of their liberty. That means two more years separated from their families, subjected to the harsh conditions of Cuba’s prison system and punished solely for exercising their human rights. The Cuban authorities must release them immediately and unconditionally. They should not spend another day behind bars.”

title: Solar Surprise: Dealing with a Surplus
content:
Spain and China share a common problem: they produce too much solar power. 

The two countries are committed to a green future and have made dizzying progress. Over the past two years, Chinese renewables exceeded ten trillion kWh of electricity for the first time and are expected to account for a third of growth in global demand by 2040, driven by its ever-expanding electric car fleet, industrial transformation, and artificial intelligence data centers.

Although my home country of Spain is much smaller than China, it too is experiencing a renewable boom. More than $80 billion in capital has been invested over the last 15 years in renewables, with solar costs dropping from $0.36/kWh in 2010 to just $0.04/kWh. Green energy accounts for two-thirds of the total national power grid. 

The price of solar panels has fallen by roughly 90% over the last decade. Solar is not dependent on moving parts that wear out, and production can be managed with software, without the need to maintain turbines or furnaces.
snippet: Spain and China share a common problem: they produce too much solar power.

title: Computer Security Is About to Get a Lot Worse, Here’s What You Can Do
content: It is a commonly held truth among computer geeks that there is no such thing as bug free software, or a secure computer. Any piece of software that anyone actually uses will have a security vulnerability somewhere in the code. The more complex that software is, the more likely there will be a vulnerability. Fortunately for everyone, finding severe vulnerabilities was generally considered an expensive and difficult task requiring years of training and deep knowledge of how computers and software worked. Until recently there was a steady background hum of vulnerabilities being found and patched, with major vulnerabilities that could cripple the entire internet only happening every few years. Now that is no longer the case.

Följ med på en musikalisk resa mellan Finland och Sverige! Konserten På tonernas brygga utforskar hur dikter från Finland landstigit hos svenska och nordiska tonsättare och hur Finlands främsta musikskapare tonsatt svensk lyrik – från både Finland och Sverige. Studerande och lärare från Sibelius-Akademin i Helsingfors gästar Finlandsinstitutet med sånger från olika tider i en skön blandning av stilar.

För sången står sopranerna Alvilda Elmarsdóttir, Hanna Hasu och Inka Österberg samt barytonen Petteri Salomaa. Vid flygeln sitter Gustav Djupsjöbacka och David Szilasi.

title: Complementary forces: Why activism needs art to drive action
content:
‘A striking action, a touch of humor, or an unexpected scene can attract attention.’

Originally published on Global Voices

An urban art piece called “The Post is fast, it's only the letters that arrive slowly” in front of the main Post Office in Skopje, North Macedonia.

This post is by Nikola Pisarev, an art historian and a pioneer of creative activism in North Macedonia, who serves as the program director at the Contemporary Art Center in Skopje. It is also part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” You can support this coverage by donating here.

In recent decades, practices that bring art directly into people’s everyday lives have become increasingly common. They may be initiated by artists, activists, informal groups, or citizens who use creative means to draw attention to a problem, express disagreement, or call for change. Public spaces become a place where an action meets an audience, provokes a response, and starts a conversation. This approach, when artistic and creative means are used to press for solutions or encourage social change, is called artistic activism.

title: Denied Medical Care: A Report on the Latest Situation of Teacher Hadi Jalali in Jiroft Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Hadi Jalali remains deprived of access to his medications and appropriate medical treatment.

An informed source close to Jalali’s family told HRANA: “Mr. Jalali, who is serving his prison sentence in Jiroft Prison, has been denied access to his medications despite suffering from mental health conditions.”

The source added: “He is being held in a ward designated for prisoners convicted of ordinary criminal offenses, in violation of the principle of separation of prisoners based on the nature of their offenses. He is also forced to sleep on the floor due to the lack of a bed and has been deprived of basic prison facilities.”

Jalali was transferred to Jiroft Prison in August 2026 to begin serving his prison sentence.

On June 9, 2026, Branch 7 of the Kerman Province Court of Appeals upheld the teacher’s conviction in full. He had previously been sentenced by the lower court to two years and seven months in prison on the charge of “disrupting national security.” His trial was held on February 11, 2025, before Branch 1 of the Revolutionary Court in Kerman.

title: Inbjudan: Writing of Disaster @ Viirus GUEST
content:
Viirus GUEST: Writing of Disaster
Av Jenni-Elina von Bagh och arbetsgrupp
En scenisk skildring av livet och undergången

Writing of Disaster är ett koreografiskt melodrama och en postfars där undergång och liv går hand i hand och . Verket är en konstnärlig bearbetning av Maurice Blanchots filosofiska verk ”The Writing of a Disaster” (sv. Katastrofens skrivande/ Viljami Hukka, 2024). Kan en ny början uppstå ur askan om undergång, och hur finner man den?

I verket utforskar tre erfarna åskådare misslyckandets komik – vår existens, gränser och mörka punkter, posthumana krafter, den delikata balansen mellan skräck och skratt. Åskådarna hämtar inspiration från kroppens egen vandrande händelse rikedom, som uppstår ur opraktiska, löjliga och självpåtagna utmaningar. Verket hittar ständigt nya sätt att uttrycka sig, trassla in sig, falla och åter samla sig – att fundera över livets under, över det faktum att vi lever.

title: Many in Serbia’s Youth Movement Fear a Rigged Election on Sunday
content:
Riding an extraordinary wave of public mobilization, Serbia’s student-led opposition heads into Sunday’s snap parliamentary election genuinely believing it can break President Aleksandar Vučić’s 14-year grip on power.

Yet beneath the euphoria of this week’s mass rallies lies a pervasive conviction among its supporters that the contest will be anything but fair—and that the ruling party will resort to outright ballot theft rather than concede defeat.

On Thursday night, that tension was on full display as hundreds of thousands of people flooded into Belgrade’s central Slavija Square, filling the surrounding boulevards in a buoyant, flag-waving display of collective defiance. The assembly marked the movement's final campaign rally ahead of an early vote that serves as the culmination of nearly two years of youth-led unrest against Vučić’s rule.

What began in November 2024 as grief and outrage following the collapse of a newly renovated railway station canopy in the northern city of Novi Sad—a disaster that killed 16 people and was turned by the protesting youth into a lethal symbol of state corruption and crony contracting—has since metastasized into a nationwide rebellion.

title: Ken Paxton Says He’s Tough on Crime. His Trust Invested $600,000 in a Convicted Fraudster’s Company.
content:
Four years after North Texas home builder Scott Sherman completed a federal prison sentence for mortgage fraud, his new construction materials business received a $600,000 cash infusion.

The financial boost came from a blind trust set up to prevent Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and his wife, state Sen. Angela Paxton, from any overlap in their personal investments and their actions as elected officials. But previously unreleased records from the attorney general’s 2023 impeachment investigation show the trust was far from blind and did not shield the Paxtons from its business dealings, including the investment in Sherman’s business.

Before long, Wildcatter Sand Services and Grayson County Sand and Gravel, which Sherman built with his father, grew into a vast enterprise with various locations and subsidiaries. And along the way, some of those businesses stopped paying taxes to local governments, including school districts.

title: Starlink still restricted for Ukraine despite Trump saying Musk lifted speed limits
content:
KYIV — Ukrainian interceptors still cannot use the internet at high speed to shoot down Russian attack drones or conduct mid-strike operations as of Friday morning, Ukrainian officials and a drone operator said, despite U.S. President Donald Trump saying SpaceX founder Elon Musk had lifted speed restrictions on his Starshield service.

“Morning tests show the speed limits of 140–160 km/h are still there, and the navigation isn’t working properly,” a Ukrainian government official told POLITICO on condition of anonymity.

“As of this morning, instances of connectivity loss at speeds of 161 km/h are still being observed. There is currently no confirmation that the restrictions have been lifted,” a defense ministry official told reporters on Friday.

Ukrainian drone units started testing speed limits from Thursday evening, shortly after Trump told reporters that Musk had restored Starlink. While some tests recorded speeds of up to 200 km/h over the Black Sea and noted an improvement, the drones still rapidly lost signal once flying above the 160 km/h speed limit.

title: A farewell to BioWare, maker of some of the best games of the 21st century | Lucy James
content:
The closure of the studio responsible for some of the best games of the 21st century leaves the world of RPGs feeling smaller without the hope of another instalment of the much-loved sci-fi series

Earlier this week, EA announced the closure of BioWare, a game studio with a 30-year history of compelling role-playing games, complex characters and bold, choice-driven narratives. Its forthcoming game in the Mass Effect sci-fi series has been cancelled, and more than 400 people are losing their jobs. As someone who has worked in the video games industry for 15 years and spent almost 20 as a BioWare fan, I am among millions of mourners today.

title: The Crucible: Arthur Miller’s morality tale was as much a reaction to his own marital failings as it was to the ‘red scare’
content:
Written at the height of the cold war “red scare”, Arthur Miller’s 1952 play The Crucible was a retelling of the 17th-century Salem witch trials (1692-93) which soon became the classic parable of mass hysteria.

Miller’s play has long been described as “a cornerstone of American theatre” and “an allegory of our times”. Adapted into a 1996 Oscar-nominated Hollywood film, recent stage revivals on Broadway (2016) and at the UK’s National Theatre (2022) further confirm its enduring popularity.

A staple of the high-school syllabus (a YouTube search yields over 3,200 school productions), the play has also come to shape popular understandings of early modern witchcraft. As Miller (1915-2005) foresaw, its interpretation of Salem became a flexible model applicable to other tragedies – so flexible, in fact, that “witch-hunt” has in recent years devolved into a virtually meaningless political catchphrase.

title: Tekoäly nopeuttaa haavoittuvuuksien löytymistä – kriittiset PHP-haavoittuvuudet aiheuttavat palvelukatkoja
content:
Tekoäly nopeuttaa haavoittuvuuksien löytymistä – kriittiset PHP-haavoittuvuudet aiheuttavat palvelukatkoja

Traficomin mukaan tietoturvahaavoittuvuuksia löydetään ennätystahtia. Kehitys edellyttää organisaatioilta entistä nopeampaa reagointia.

Tekoäly nopeuttaa tietoturvahaavoittuvuuksien löytämistä ja mahdollista hyväksikäyttöä. Ajankohtainen esimerkki ovat laajasti käytetyn PHP-verkkopalveluteknologian kriittiset haavoittuvuudet, joiden vuoksi osa verkkopalveluista on ollut tilapäisesti poissa käytöstä. Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficomin Kyberturvallisuuskeskuksen mukaan Suomessa ei ole toistaiseksi havaittu PHP-haavoittuvuuksien onnistunutta hyväksikäyttöä.

title: Vihreiden Forsgrén vaatii ministeri Rydmanilta selvitystä paperittomien terveysneuvonnan päättymisestä
content:
Lääkärien sosiaalinen vastuu ry, LSV, on saanut ennakkotiedon paperittomuustyönsä STEA-rahoituksen päättymisestä ensi vuonna. Järjestön mukaan ennakkotiedossa vedotaan sosiaali- ja terveysministeri Wille Rydmanin toiveeseen. Asiasta kertoi Lääkärilehti 20. lokakuuta.

Kansanedustaja Bella Forsgrénin mukaan ministerin on kerrottava, pitääkö tieto paikkansa ja millä perusteilla rahoitusta ollaan lopettamassa.

"Ministerin henkilökohtaiset mieltymykset eivät saa ratkaista, ketä Suomessa autetaan", Forsgrén sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

LSV on lähes kymmenen vuoden ajan ohjannut paperittomia ihmisiä terveydenhuollon piiriin, neuvonut heitä hoito-oikeuksista ja kouluttanut terveydenhuollon ammattilaisia. Järjestön mukaan kahden asiantuntijan työ maksaa 140 000 euroa vuodessa. Ilman rahoitusta neuvonta ja kohtaava työ loppuvat.

"Olen järkyttynyt. Puhumme työstä, jonka ansiosta diabeetikko saa insuliinireseptinsä, toistuvasti kouristeleva lapsi pääsee tutkimuksiin ja odottava äiti neuvolaan. Hinnan maksavat ihmisten terveys ja päivystykset, joihin hoitamattomat sairaudet lopulta päätyvät", Forsgrén sanoo.

title: What does the C say about your yoghurt?
content: Let's say you're in a shop looking for yoghurt. You're standing at the fridge, choosing between strawberry and plain. The pots show five letters, running from a dark-green A to a red E. The one you're holding has a C. Hmmm. Those letters are the Nutri-Score, a label weighing sugars, saturated fat, salt, and calories against fibre, protein, and the content of fruit, vegetables and legumes in products per 100 g or 100 ml. The label was first adopted in France in 2017 and has since been picked up in Germany, Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and Spain. International supermarkets have also brought it elsewhere, which is why you'll see the label on Lidl shelves in Latvia, for example. Using it is voluntary for producers. We analysed nearly one million EU-listed packaged products with a Nutri-Score in the Open Food Facts database from all over Europe, and found that nearly three-quarters (73.9%) were rated C, D, or E. Does that mean nearly three-quarters of these products are unhealthy? The answer isn't straightforward. title: Russia’s Ominous Migrant Weaponization
content:
Russia’s shadow war against Europe is a multiple pronged attack on NATO and other countries. In the northeastern sector of this front line, shoving developing world migrants through border fences has long played a role. In October, this campaign took a new and ominous turn.

On October 6, masked and armed individuals tried to drive at least 20 migrants from Belarus into Latvia, threatening the Latvian soldiers confronting them, according to the public media account. Hours later, masked people again crossed into Latvia, damaged an electricity distribution box, stole surveillance cameras and returned to Belarus before border guards arrived.

Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava warned that Belarus should expect serious consequences. This was not another episode of migration pressure but an armed intimidation and sabotage to a route already being used to pressure Latvia’s border. About 1,000 migrants monthly attempt to cross the frontier with Belarusian assistance.

title: Ohio Governor's Race: Trump Backs Ramaswamy Ad Siding with Opponent's Indicted Childhood Rapist
content:
President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both defended Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy after his campaign released a TV ad that appears to accuse Democratic nominee Amy Acton of lying about being sexually abused as a child. Acton’s stepfather was indicted in 1978 on charges of sexually assaulting her when she was between 10 and 12 years old, though he fled before he could be convicted. Acton’s mother, who lost custody of her two children, sided with her husband and remained with him as a fugitive until his death in 2004. In the controversial campaign ad, the elderly Donna Arthur says her daughter Amy has “lied her entire life” and can’t be trusted as governor, which has been widely interpreted as casting doubt on what Acton has said about being abused as a minor.

“Vivek Ramaswamy is now using that personal trauma as an effort to exploit what she went through and win this race,” says Abby Vesoulis, a reporter for Mother Jones. “He’s currently polling beneath Amy Acton, which shows, I think, that this ad is a desperate attempt to somehow pull off a victory despite poor odds.”
