title: Työeläkeindeksiin korotus – tätä se tarkoittaa
content:
Maksussa oleviin työeläkkeisiin vaikuttavaan työeläkeindeksiin tulee ensi vuonna noin 2,6 prosentin korotus. Indeksi nostaa esimerkiksi 2 000 euron työeläkettä noin 52 eurolla kuukaudessa.

Sosiaali- ja terveysministeriö on vahvistanut työeläketurvaa koskevat indeksit ensi vuodelle.

Työeläkeindeksillä tarkistetaan maksussa olevat työeläkkeet. Palkkakertoimella taas korotetaan työuran aikaiset palkat ja työtulot eläkkeelle jäämisen ajankohdan tasoon. Palkkakerroin nousee lähes 3,6 prosenttia.

Sosiaaliturvaetuuksien säilyminen on pyritty Suomessa turvaamaan siten, että etuudet tarkistetaan vuosittain indeksillä. Palkka- ja kuluttajahintatasossa tapahtuvat muutokset huomioidaan laskettaessa indeksiä.

Vuosi sitten työeläkeindeksiä korotettiin noin 0,9 ja palkkakerrointa noin 2,3 prosenttia.

Syksyn mittaan on keskusteltu siitä, puututaanko talouden tasapainottamisen nimissä myös eläkkeisiin.

Perussuomalaiset esitti tällä viikolla, että eläkkeisiin asetettaisiin vuosiksi 2028-2031 indeksijarru. Alle 2 000 euron kuukausittaiset eläkkeet saisivat kuitenkin täyden indeksikorotuksen.

title: Two States Can Now Restrict Social Media Access—Here’s What To Do Next
content:
Last week, two federal appeals courts issued opinions that will allow Florida and Georgia to start enforcing laws that will age-gate and block young people from accessing social media. The laws do not adequately respect minors’ rights to play, speak, and learn online. More fundamentally, these laws don’t help young people stay safe online—a goal that lawmakers should pursue.

Age-Gated? Email EFF at agegates@eff.org. 

Because of the new laws, some young people will lose their ability to access lawful information, find their online communities, and even engage with school board members. Others will need parental permission to stay online. And adults will face increased demands to prove their age, which will put their privacy at increased risk simply to continue to use the services they already use. 

We opposed these laws because they threaten the free expression and privacy of both minors and adults.  Even though these lawsuits are not over, the injunctions that paused enforcement have been lifted, and the states of Florida and Georgia will now be able to enforce broad restrictions on social media use.

content:

title: Marraskuussa Huittisten museolla sateenkaarihistoriaa ja runonlausuntaa
content:
Huittisten museon maksuttomat tiistaitapaamiset johdattavat marraskuussa sateenkaarihistorian ja runoustaiteen äärelle tuttuja neulontatiistaita ja valokuvakeruuta unohtamatta.

Kuukauden ensimmäisenä tiistaina 3.11. klo 17–19 museon tiistaitapaamista vietetään sateenkaarihistoriakuukauden merkeissä. Museolla pääsee tekemään itse pinssejä ja samalla jutustellaan siitä, mitä sateenkaarihistorialla tarkoitetaan. Tapahtuma järjestetään yhteistyössä Huittisten nuorisopalveluiden kanssa.

Seksuaali- ja sukupuolivähemmistöjä on aina ollut olemassa, mutta monesti heidän historiansa on pitänyt piilottaa. Sateenkaarihistoriakuukauden tarkoituksena on nostaa esiin tätä vaiettua historiaa osana yhteistä kulttuuriperintöämme. Suomalaisen sukupuoli- ja seksuaalivähemmistöjen historian tallentamisesta vastaa valtakunnallisesti Tampereella sijaitseva Työväenmuseo Werstas. Pinssipajassa pääsee tekemään rintamerkkejä Werstaan LHBTIQ+-kokoelman aitojen mallien mukaan.

title: Sanctioned Investor in Cambodian Scam Compound Owns California Mansion
content:
Brendon Luo was sanctioned in June by the U.S. Treasury Department, which alleged he was an investor in a cyber-scam compound operated by Cambodia's Prince Group. Property records show he still owns a mansion in a gated community in southern California.

The Prince Group is widely accused of involvement in compounds in Cambodia where thousands of trafficked workers were forced to commit industrial-scale cyberfraud. The Prince Group has strongly denied the accusations, but the U.S. has sanctioned more than 140 allegedly-associated entities and individuals, including Luo.

The sanctions have not disrupted Luo’s ownership of a five bedroom mansion in Yorba Linda, a city of about 68,000 people that is part of the Los Angeles metropolitan area. Although no sale price was identified in property records, online real estate portals value the property at roughly $5 million.

Luo was born in China and acquired passports from Cambodia, Vanuatu and Cyprus, according to information from sanctions notices as well as immigration records obtained by OCCRP.

title: Bird Flu Is Raging on a Mink Farm. It Could Spark a Human Pandemic, Experts Say, but Officials Won’t Act.
content:
The strain of bird flu that’s ripped through American barns for the last four years has killed two people who caught it from sick animals. But as far as anyone can tell, humans can’t spread it. The virus has remained a true “bird” flu, tailored to attach to avian cells, not invade human throats and noses, where coughing and sneezing reliably spew droplets. 

Under the right conditions, however, that could change. A single mutation could give the bird flu a foothold in people and spark a pandemic that experts fear could be deadlier than COVID-19. 

For that to happen, this bird flu would likely need to find an intermediate host — an animal vulnerable to viruses that infect both birds and humans. These animals would be crowded together, each infection raising the odds that a new strain could arise through mutation. Then, for that strain to jump across species, it would have to have access to humans and time to spread among them undetected.

Last year, the Anthropic CEO, Dario Amodei, warned that artificial intelligence could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs and that in six months it would be writing 90% of code. Neither of those predictions came to pass.

Now, in a report Anthropic published on Thursday, the company said it was hiring fewer junior technical workers and that human attention has become the new “bottleneck” as it increasingly relies on its Claude AI agents.

title: Sisävesien kaupallinen kalansaalis väheni miljoonalla kilolla vuonna 2025
content:
Sisävesiltä saatiin vuonna 2025 yhteensä neljä miljoonaa kiloa kaupallisesti kalastettua kalaa ja lähes 700 000 rapua. Saalis väheni edellisvuodesta miljoonalla kilolla eli viidenneksen. Saaliin arvo laski lähes neljänneksen ja oli yhteensä 12 miljoonaa euroa. Muikku oli edelleen määrältään ja kuha arvoltaan tärkein saalislaji.

Tiedot perustuvat Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) vuoden 2025 saalistilastoon.

Muikku säilyi määrältään sisävesien tärkeimpänä kaupallisena saalislajina. Muikkua pyydettiin 1,7 miljoonaa kiloa. Saalis oli koko 2020-luvun noin kaksi miljoonaa kiloa, kun 2010-luvulla sitä saatiin vuosittain noin 2,5–3 miljoonaa kiloa.

Muikkusaaliin arvo laski 3,5 miljoonaan euroon. Vähennystä edellisvuoteen oli yli miljoona euroa. Arvon laskuun vaikuttivat sekä aiempaa pienempi saalismäärä että tuottajahinnan aleneminen.

”Kalojen tuottajahinnat ovat kauttaaltaan laskeneet hieman, joskin tulos voi johtua uudistetusta hintatietojen keruumenetelmästä. Vain täpläravun hinta on noussut vähän. Se voi johtua rapuyksilöiden keskikoon suurenemisesta, mikä vaikuttaa ravusta maksettavaan hintaan voimakkaasti”, kertoo yliaktuaari Mika Rahikainen Lukesta.

title: Spheres of Influence Won’t Help the US
content:
In February 1991, officials of the Warsaw Pact gathered for a final meeting in Budapest.

When the doors opened and Soviet officials and officers emerged with delegates from the five other member states, there was an expression of barely suppressed hilarity on the faces of many. A journalist approached one Central European delegation to ask why.

The officials could barely contain themselves. “As the meeting was ending,” one said, “the Russians said there was one final thing – no one had said thank you.”

“Thank you? Asked one delegate. “What for”

“A thank you for keeping the peace all these years.”

Czechs, Slovaks and Hungarians, whose countries had been invaded by Russian tanks, were said to have led the snorts of derision and suppressed laughter. This was too much for the Russians, who packed up their papers and left.

title: Ranska varautuu viikonloppuun: 70 000 poliisia ja santarmia kaduille hillitsemään protesteja
content:
Ranska marssittaa ensi viikonloppuna kaduille noin 70 000 poliisia ja santarmia hillitsemään protesteja, kertoi sisäministeri Laurent Nunez perjantaina lehdistötilaisuudessa Pariisissa.

Hänen mukaansa sosiaalisessa mediassa oli jo yllytetty väkivaltaan ja ryöstelyyn mielenosoitusten yhteydessä.

Nunezin mukaan osa partioivista poliiseista kuuluu eliittiyksiköihin, minkä lisäksi viranomaisten käytössä on noin 20 panssariajoneuvoa ja 15 vesitykkiajoneuvoa.

Ranskan korkeita elinkustannuksia vastustaneet protestit viime viikonloppuna yltyivät osin väkivaltaisiksi.

Tämän viikonlopun mielenosoituksia on rajoitettu. Esimerkiksi Lyonissa mielenosoitukset on kielletty kaupungin keskustassa, ja Pariisissakin niiden reittejä on rajoitettu.

content:
Company Humanimaliksen nykysirkus- ja nukketeatteriteos Luonnon lähettiläs? saa kantaesityksensä Turun Kaupunginteatterin Sopukka-näyttämöllä 29.10.2026.

Sirkus- ja tanssitaitelija Sara Nurmisen konseptoima ja ohjaama teos herättää sirkuseläimet henkiin lavalla uniikilla yhdistelmällä nukketeatteria, nykysirkusta sekä videotaidetta. Perinteisen sirkuksen estetiikalla leikittelevä surrealistinen satiiri kuljettaa katsojan tuotantoeläimen silmin absurdiin todellisuuteen, jossa sekoittuvat arkirealismi ja abstrakti liike.

Teosprosessissa olemme tarkastelleet eläinsirkuksen historiaa kriittisesti ja syventyneet siihen, miten toislajiset voisivat jäädä osaksi sirkusta
niin että se hyödyttäisi heitä hyväksikäytön sijaan”, Nurminen kertoo.

title: US Court Orders Lebanese Ex-Minister to Pay $35M in Torture and Fraud Case
content:
A U.S. district court has ruled against four Lebanese individuals, including a former minister, finding them liable for fraud, torture and civil conspiracy and ordering them to pay $35 million in damages, for orchestrating the kidnapping and torture of a Lebanese-American couple.

Speaking to OCCRP about the verdict from the Florida court, Lara Samaha, a U.S. green card holder, said the couple filed in the U.S. because “the justice system in Lebanon is so corrupt it is impossible to obtain justice.”

According to the default final judgment seen by OCCRP, a binding court order issued when defendants fail to respond to a lawsuit, the court ordered Gebran Bassil—a sitting member of parliament, Lebanon’s former foreign minister, and the son-in-law of former President Michel Aoun—to pay millions in damages, along with three co-defendants.

“⁠I feel justice has been served after 7 years in court and more than 300 court filings,” Lara Samaha told OCCRP. She confirmed that there will be a follow up on a related lawsuit in Lebanon, though she declined to detail the next steps.

title: The young Americans choosing Y2K cars over shiny new SUVs: ‘I get so much crap from people’
content:
People under 35 are hunting for no-frills rides they can pay for in cash and fix themselves – defying expectations to take on steep loans

Jack Price joined the marines in fall 2021 knowing he would need a car to get around base and that he couldn’t afford a new one. A joyless, month-long search through dealer classifieds and Facebook Marketplace listings ended when his mother spotted a 2010 Volkswagen Jetta posted on her office listserv by a co-worker moving abroad. With just 60,000 miles (96,560km) on the meter, the car (a manual!) was mechanically sound, and the air conditioning, sunroof and Bluetooth radio worked too. At $6,000, it was a steal. Price paid in cash.

Five years on, the Jetta, which he called the Pewter Pebble, is still carting him from A to B in unassuming style. “I’ve completely driven it into the ground,” says the 30-year-old, who lives in Los Angeles. “All over bases, cross-country a couple times, not really lovingly. I get so much crap from people, but not people my age.”

title: Den kommersiella fiskfångsten i insjöarna minskade med en miljon kilo 2025
content:
År 2025 uppgick den kommersiella insjöfångsten till sammanlagt fyra miljoner kilo fisk och nästan 700 000 kräftor. Fångsten minskade med en miljon kilo från året innan, det vill säga med en femtedel. Fångstens värde minskade med nästan en fjärdedel och uppgick till sammanlagt 12 miljoner euro. Siklöja var fortfarande den viktigaste fångstarten sett till mängden och gös den viktigaste till fångstvärdet.

Uppgifterna baserar sig på Naturresursinstitutets (Luke) fångststatistik för 2025.

Siklöja förblev den viktigaste kommersiella fångstarten i insjöarna sett till fångstmängden. Fångsten av siklöja uppgick till 1,7 miljoner kilo. Under 2020-talet har fångsten varit cirka två miljoner kilo, medan den under 2010-talet uppgick till cirka 2,5–3 miljoner kilo per år.

Värdet på siklöjafångsten minskade till 3,5 miljoner euro. Det var en minskning med mer än en miljon euro från året innan. Värdeminskningen berodde både på en mindre fångstmängd än tidigare och på ett lägre producentpris.

title: Netanjahu: Länsirannalla käyntiin laaja sotilasoperaatio – osa Hebronin asukkaista siirretään
content:
Israelin pääministeri Benjamin Netanjahu sanoi perjantaina käynnistäneensä laajan sotilasoperaation Israelin miehittämällä Länsirannalla. Palestiinalaistaistelijoiden kerrottiin tehneen Hebronissa perjantaiaamuna aseellisen hyökkäyksen, jossa haavoittui viisi ihmistä.

Netanjahu määräsi jo aiemmin Länsirannan suljettavaksi hyökkäyksen vuoksi. Hänen mukaansa osa Hebronin asukkaista sijoitetaan muualle.

Netanjahu sanoi harkitsevansa puolustusministeri Israel Katzin kanssa Länsirannan-operaatiota, joka olisi laajempi kuin mikään sitten vuoden 1967 kuuden päivän sodan.

title: Kuunteluklubi Hämeenlinnan pääkirjastossa
content:
Kuunnellaan Ylen Radioateljeen emeritus tuottajan Harri Huhtamäen ateljee-ohjelma Äiti, Alzheimer ja Americana - elämä laillisessa laittomuudessa. Kuuntelun jälkeen keskustelua ja Huhtamäki kertoo miten ohjelma on tehty. Tilaisuuteen on vapaa pääsy.

Muistisairauksista ja erityisesti Alzheimerin taudista on tulossa vakava kansansairaus, väittävät asiantuntijat, jotka ovat huolissaan suurista ikäluokista. Huoli on ennen kaikkea taloudellinen. Muita huolia ei juuri yhteiskunnallisessa keskustelussa tunneta. Radioateljeen ohjelma Äiti, Alzheimer ja Americana tutkailee asioita hieman toisista kuulokulmista.

Nykyistä vanhustenhoitoa voi pitää eräänlaisena laillisena laittomuuden tilana – leirinä. Leiri on periaate, jolle poliittinen tila ja järjestys nykyään muodostuu. Ajatus leiristä on italialaisen filosofin Giorgio Agamben. Kontekstina on suvereeni valtio, joka päättää elämästä ja kuolemasta. Suvereenin hallitsema laillisen laittomuuden tila merkitsee vanhusten hoidossa mielivaltaa – heitteillejättöä, laillisesti.

title: Cambodia Cracked Down on Banks Allegedly Linked to Cyber-Scams. The IMF Says the Problem Persists.
content:
Amid mounting international pressure to clean up its financial system, Cambodia’s central bank published a statement earlier this month accusing unnamed actors of waging a campaign of “economic sabotage” against the country.

“Rumors and unverified information have been circulating on social media, claiming that a number of banking and financial institutions are facing issues or heading toward collapse in the near future,” the National Bank of Cambodia (NBC) said.

The NBC did not clarify who might be behind such a campaign, or which institutions were targeted. But the regulator warned that such “baseless” information could undermine “trust in the overall banking system.”

The banking system has taken a beating recently, as international attention turned to Cambodia’s role as a major hub for cyber-scams targeting victims around the world. Proceeds from scams have allegedly flooded into financial institutions.

title: Is a job guarantee the solution to mass AI unemployment?
content:
An old idea springs anew as a chorus of influential voices predicts that AI may trigger crises of vast magnitude

In a preface to his book Capitalism and Freedom, the American economist Milton Friedman famously observed that a crisis can propel once-fringe ideas into the political mainstream.

“Only a crisis – actual or perceived – produces real change. When that crisis occurs, the actions that are taken depend on the ideas that are lying around,” he wrote. The job of intellectuals, thinktanks and economists, he argued, is to refine the quality of these ambient ideas, so that good ones are ready when disaster strikes.

title: Portal Texas Used to ‘Rubber Stamp’ Data Centers Down After 404 Media Reporting
content:
Texas has shut down the web portal for its automated construction permit filing system and suspended construction permits of 17 data center projects. The change came after 404 Media reported that a group of Texans discovered the state had continued to issue construction permits related to data centers despite Governor Greg Abbott calling for a pause in September.

On Monday, the watchdog groups FracTracker Alliance and Public Citizen published reports detailing more than two dozen permits issued to Texas data center projects. On Tuesday, the website for STEERS – an application filing system for construction projects run by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) – returned a 404 error.

By Wednesday, the site had this message on it: “TCEQ’s electronic filing application used for automatic authorizations has been temporarily shut down to ensure all applications are reviewed by agency staff to determine if they are related to data centers.”

Before TCEQ shut the portal down, 404 Media viewed 17 different permits related to data center projects and saw that they’d been moved from “active” to “suspended” in the TCEQ central registry.

title: Sudan: El Fasher civilians suffer unlawful killings, detention and torture one year after city’s capture by the RSF – new testimony
content:
• Surveillance and detentions rife in city
  • With limited humanitarian aid, risks of child malnutrition remain high
  • “A pervasive pall of fear hangs over El Fasher today” – Agnès Callamard

    • Civilians in El Fasher in North Darfur, Sudan, are still suffering detention, torture and limited access to humanitarian aid one year after the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) captured the city and committed brutalities against civilians, Amnesty International said today.

    In new testimony, residents who recently escaped the city told Amnesty International how schools had been turned into detention centres, how their movement was strictly controlled, and that unlawful killings were rife.

    According to figures gathered by humanitarian organizations working in the city, fewer than 70,000 people are present in El Fasher, compared to its pre-war population of more than one million. Humanitarian access remains limited, and humanitarian workers and other civilians in the city are constantly surveilled or monitored. Arbitrary detention risks, for both civilians and humanitarian workers, remain extremely high.

    A pervasive pall of fear hangs over El Fasher today

    Agnès Callamard, Amnesty International’s Secretary General

title: Can LLMs Supercharge Geolocations? Our Tests Show Big Improvements But Humans Remain Key
content:
Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published.

In September, the AI company Anthropic published a blog post that claimed its models were approaching “superhuman capabilities for geolocating outdoor photos”. Anthropic made this claim by comparing its models’ performance to that of players of the popular online game GeoGuessr, which challenges users to geolocate Google Street View images. 

Bellingcat has been running its own benchmark tests on AI models since June 2025, right around the time when Large Language Models (LLMs) began to challenge reverse image searches for assisting with geolocation tasks. title: Experts: How are climate scientists using artificial intelligence?
content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is developing at a rapid pace and is increasingly being used by scientists to better understand climate change.

AI is perhaps best-known for its use in “large language models”, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

However, the field is vast. 

From weather forecasting to analysing satellite images, climate scientists are using various types of AI to develop faster and more efficient ways to study the warming planet. 

However, the technology comes with no shortage of risks and challenges, including overreliance on unverified results, intensive energy use and exacerbating existing inequalities in climate science.

Carbon Brief spoke to 10 experts working across a range of climate-related fields – from developing climate forecasts to analysing changes in the energy grid – about how AI is being used.

Their answers are set out below, grouped by theme.

  • What are the benefits and challenges of using AI in weather and climate forecasting?
  • What are some other current uses of AI in climate science research?
  • How is AI being used to advance climate policy and action?
  • How could AI be used in climate research over the coming years?

title: Western Embassies Must Stay in Bomb-Blasted Kyiv
content:
Some Western diplomats in Kyiv have reportedly begun contingency planning to relocate to Lviv or eastern Poland if Russian attacks on the capital intensify further. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry later said that no diplomatic mission had formally notified it of plans to leave Kyiv.

The reports may never translate into actual relocation, but they highlight a potentially much bigger problem: what happens if Russia’s growing pressure on the capital succeeds in persuading Ukraine’s international partners to abandon Kyiv, as many did in 2022?

That question has become more urgent as Moscow’s campaign against Kyiv grows increasingly disruptive. Recent strikes have hit energy infrastructure and the bridges connecting the two banks of the Dnipro. More than a third of Kyiv’s residents live on the left bank while many work on the right, making these crossings central to the city’s daily functioning.

title: Six years on from her unjust imprisonment: Freedom for Kenia Now!
content:
October 18th marked six years since lawyer, feminist and Amuzga indigenous woman human rights defender, Kenia Inés Hernández Montalván, was arbitrarily detained, criminalised and unjustly sentenced to a total of more than 20 years in prison on eleven charges.

Kenia is an Amuzga woman and defender of land, territory, the rights of indigenous peoples and women’s rights. She is the Coordinator of the Zapata Vive Libertarian Collective, which promotes different forms of peaceful resistance against the implementation of capitalist development models.

The reason for her imprisonment? Exercising her legitimate right to protest and to defend human rights. Six years later, despite the fact that in April 2026 she was cleared of the eight federal charges against her, and despite warnings regarding the injustice of her case, from international organisations, human rights bodies and mechanisms, including the IACHR, the UN, as well as Mexican and European parliamentarians, Kenia remains in detention.

title: "A Spark from the Cockroaches": Arundhati Roy on India's Youth Protests & Modi's Crackdown
content:
A court in India on Wednesday ordered the release of two leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party, the youth-led movement that has led historic waves of protests in India since the summer. Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained amid massive protests last week after they scaled a barricade to enter a site popular for protest, unfurled the national flag and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Kumar oversaw the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls in India since June of last year. Opposition parties say those impacted are primarily Muslims and other minorities less likely to support the BJP, the Hindu nationalist ruling party of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

“You have a deep and wide — an ideologically wide — historical culture of resistance in India,” says acclaimed writer and activist Arundhati Roy. At the same time, the Modi government “has three things in its playbook: One is false-flag attacks, two is engineering communal riots, and the third is massive repression. And I don’t think we’ve seen its hand yet.”

title: Trump wants to financially cripple the Hague tribunal that issued arrest warrants for Putin and Netanyahu. The EU threatens retaliation
content:
The United States has imposed retaliatory sanctions not only on individual judges and prosecutors but, most recently, on the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague as an institution.

Washington is responding to the actions of the Hague judges, who are investigating suspected war crimes in the Gaza Strip and have issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The Hague court serves as the court of last resort for international justice. It prosecutes individuals, including heads of state and military commanders, for war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity. More than 120 countries recognise its authority. The United States, Russia, China and Israel, however, are not members and reject its jurisdiction.

Washington’s order came on Friday, 9 October 2026, just hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for a UN report concluding that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.

title: ECHOES at the NEMO European Museum Conference
content:
Last week, ECHOES partners attended the NEMO European Museum Conference entitled Human after all – Museums in the wake of AI in Vilnius (11th-13th October), Lithuania, and organised a workshop dedicated to Nordic and Baltic cultural heritage professionals on the 14th October. This session invited museum professionals, researchers and policy makers to present their national and regional landscapes, and explore new opportunities for knowledge exchange and collaboration in a complex political and technological context.

During the first half of the workshop, the audience was introduced to the ECHOES project and the Cloud, including detailed presentations of the community engagement activities by FSP and a demonstration of the Cloud’s features and infrastructure design by PCSS. The second half of the session was dedicated to a round table gathering museum professionals from Northen Europe. They were invited to present their national cultural and policy landscape and discuss how the Cloud could support better collaboration beyond national and regional frameworks.

An important output from the NEMO Conference was their statement on AI and Museums, download the PDF here.

title: Canadians Are Running Out Of Time To Oppose The Dangerous C-22 Surveillance Bill
content:
Canada’s Parliament is debating a massive expansion of surveillance powers that will threaten the privacy and security of millions of people. Bill C-22, also called the Lawful Access Act, has already passed the House of Commons, and is now before the Canadian Senate. 

Canadians still have an opportunity to speak out and stop this dangerous legislation. The Canadian Civil Liberties Association (CCLA) is urging all Canadians to sign its petition opposing the bill. (The petition on CCLA’s website is governed by CCLA’s privacy policy.) 

Take action

Tell the canadian senate to stop C-22

As we wrote earlier this year, Bill C-22 gives the government new powers to force digital services—including telecom companies, messaging apps, and more—to help with government surveillance. Worse, it allows Canada’s Minister of Public Safety to order companies to create a backdoor to their services for law enforcement, as long as it doesn’t lead to a “systemic insecurity.” That’s a clear recipe for weakening the encryption we all rely on.

title: Juhlavuoden infografiikat esittelivät laitoksen kehitystä
content:
Etlan juhlavuoden kunniaksi julkaistiin kolme infograafia laitoksen kehityksestä vuosien varrella. Infografiikat julkaistiin Etlan Instagram-tilillä ja nyt ne ovat nähtävillä myös tässä uutisessa.

Ensimmäisessä infograafissa sukellettiin Etlan toimitusjohtajien historiaan. Etlalla on ollut yhteensä 13 eri toimitusjohtajaa, joista yksi on toiminut tehtävässä kahdessa eri otteessa. Saat kuvat suuremmaksi klikkaamalla.

Toisessa osassa tarkasteltiin henkilöstön, muistioiden ja raporttien määrää vuosina 2012–2025 välisenä aikana. Vuonna 2025 Etla julkaisi 57 raporttia, muistiota, työpaperia, kirjaa ja ennustetta. Erityisesti muistioiden määrä on kasvanut viime vuosina, ja ne tuovat tutkimustiedon nopeasti ajankohtaiseen keskusteluun.

Mediajulkisuuden määrää esiteltiin puolestaan alla olevassa infograafissa. Etla näkyi mediassa viime vuonna yli 2500 kertaa.

Viimeisenä sukellettiin hieman kevyemmän sisällön dataan. Taloustutkimus on tarkaka työtä, ja nesteytys kuuluu asiaan. Vuoden 2025 aikana Etlassa juotiin 10 780 kupillista kahvia, 4 422 pulloa kivennäisvettä ja 2 442 pulloa lähdevettä. Yhteensä siis yli 17 600 kuppia ja pulloa.

title: UNICEFin analyysi: Suomen kehitysyhteistyörahoitus vähenee, eikä humanitaarinen apu kohdennu lapsille
content:
Suomen virallinen kehitysapu on vähentynyt noin 23 prosenttia vuoden 2022 tasosta. Kehitysrahoituksen suunta on kansainvälisestikin laskeva, monet suuret rahoittajamaat kuten Yhdysvallat, Iso-Britannia, Ranska ja Saksa ovat leikanneet avustuksiaan.

UNICEFin tuottaman analyysin mukaan Suomen kehitysavusta viidennes kohdistuu lapsille. Kansainvälisesti vertailtuna Suomen prosentti on melko korkea, euromääräisesti kuitenkin vähäinen. Suomen valtion humanitaarisesta rahoituksesta lapsille kohdistuu vain 14 prosenttia.

– Lapset muodostavat kolmanneksen maailman väestöstä ja he kärsivät kriiseissä ja konflikteissa kaikkein eniten. Tästä huolimatta Suomi kohdistaa humanitaarisesta rahoituksestaan vain 14 prosenttia lapsille, kun luku on muissa Pohjoismaissa vähintään kaksinkertainen, sanoo Suomen UNICEFin lapsen oikeuksien ja kehityspolitiikan erityisasiantuntija Mirkka Mattila.

Suomen koulutus- ja terveysrahoituksesta suurin osa menee lapsille. Rahoituksen kehitys on kuitenkin laskeva. Lapsiin kohdistuva koulutusrahoitus on vähentynyt 57 prosenttia vuoden 2021 huipputasosta.

title: Lessons from Maricarmen
content:
The case of Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman from Madrid who passed away just days after being evicted from the apartment where she had lived – and for which she had paid – for decades, has resonated far beyond Spain’s borders. It has become a powerful symbol of a deeper crisis affecting our societies. For too long, housing has been treated primarily as a commodity rather than as a fundamental human right. For too long, we have been told that markets would regulate themselves and that public intervention would do more harm than good. Today, the evidence is undeniable: that approach has failed.

The question we must now confront is straightforward: what must we do to ensure that housing is guaranteed as a right, and not merely traded as an asset?

title: TNR Watch: The Enduring Problem of Transnational Repression in Southeast Asia
content:
Déjà vu: Two apparent incidents of transnational repression (TNR) endangered several diaspora activists in Southeast Asia in mid-September. On September 15, Khieo Lapchanh, a Thailand-based Laotian asylum seeker known for his online criticism of Laos’s government, went missing outside Bangkok. The 26-year-old, who was set to attend an asylum interview at the UN Refugee agency office in Bangkok a day later, reportedly was the target of an $8,000 bounty circulating online.

Three days after Lapchanh’s disappearance, three Vietnamese activists—Nguyen Duc Thuan, Ho Pham Hiep Huy, and Thai Cong Truong Son—were abducted from Cambodia and returned to Vietnam, where they are under investigation for “terrorism” and forging documents. Australian resident Hiep and dual Norwegian-Vietnamese citizen Thuan went to Cambodia to meet and train other Vietnamese human rights defenders. According to the prodemocracy organization Viet Tan, which Hiep and Thuan belong to, Vietnamese authorities initially prevented consular visits by Australian and Norwegian representatives to the two while they were in detention.

title: Riddims against copyright
content:
The Caribbean has long been exploited on the world stage, and copyright law is no exception

Originally published on Global Voices

Copyright chaser from eff.org. Fair use.

By Alexis Hancock

“Oh! Bob Marley, right?” Jamaican culture has been popularised by the mainstream, and as a Jamaican-American, I often get a glimpse into how others have consumed it and from what point of view. I would not call myself an ardent Marley fan, but I know the kind of people who are most likely attached to his music outside of Jamaica — for example, the potential counterculture student of the 1970s at UCLA who found connection to his messages of resistance. 

My personal fascination with Jamaican music is the “riddim” — the Jamaican patois spelling of “rhythm” — an instrumental beat or tune constructed not for a single artist, but to be used by the collective of the time and to be both enjoyed and critiqued by the culture makers of Jamaican art: the disenfranchised masses.

title: 17-Year-Old Teenager Mohammad Lotfi Arrested by Security Forces in Baneh
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Mohammad Lotfi, a 17-year-old teenager, was arrested. Security forces reportedly arrested the teenager at his workplace in Baneh on Tuesday, October 20, without presenting a judicial warrant.

Efforts by Mohammad Lotfi’s family to obtain information about his current situation through judicial authorities have so far been unsuccessful.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the reasons for his arrest, his whereabouts, or the charges brought against him.

title: ICC Wins EU Parliament’s Sakharov Prize
content:
(Brussels) – The European Parliament on October 22, 2026, awarded the Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and its officials. 

The following quote can be attributed to Philippe Dam, EU advocacy director at Human Rights Watch:

“By awarding the Sakharov Prize to the ICC, the European Parliament recognizes the court’s vital role for victims of the gravest crimes around the world, at a time of unprecedented attack from the Trump administration and others. This prize should be a rallying cry for ICC members to stand up for the court and for the EU Commission to urgently activate the EU’s ‘blocking statute’ to protect the court and those supporting its work from effects of US sanctions.”

title: Taide on yhteiskunnan ajattelun infrastruktuuria
content:
Kun yhteiskunnan kyky hahmottaa kokonaisuuksia heikkenee, menetämme jotakin olennaista: yhteisen tavan ymmärtää maailmaa. Taide ei ole irrallinen saareke, vaan osa sitä sivistyksen rakennetta, jonka varassa pystymme näkemään toisemme ja toimimaan yhdessä. Se ylläpitää kykyä ymmärtää maailmaa silloin, kun muutos etenee nopeammin kuin ehdimme sitä jäsentää.

”Suomen ja Euroopan tämänhetkinen haaste ei ole vain taloudellinen tai teknologinen. Se on ajattelun kaventuminen.”

– Nana Salin (Kuva: Heli Sorjonen)

Suomen ja Euroopan tämänhetkinen haaste ei ole vain taloudellinen tai teknologinen. Se on ajattelun kaventuminen. Kun maailma monimutkaistuu, yhteiskunta alkaa helposti nojata siihen, mikä on nopeaa, mitattavaa ja varmaa. Samalla menetämme jotakin olennaista: kyvyn hahmottaa kokonaisuuksia, jotka eivät mahdu Exceliin ja kyvyn nähdä toisemme yli omien kokemusten.

Taide on osa sitä peruslukutaitoa, jonka varassa yhteiskunta ylipäätään kykenee ymmärtämään itseään. Ei irrallisena sektorina, vaan osana sivistystä, kieltä ja yhteistä kokemusta. Taide on tapa oppia näkemään ja tapa oppia näkemään toisin.

title: Valon sillat -viikonloppu tuo valotaide-elämykset Savonlinnan marraskuuhun
content:
Savonlinna loistaa marraskuussa: valotaide ja elämykset valaisevat syksyn pimeyttä – Valon sillat -tehoviikonloppu 13.–15.11. kokoaa yhteen upean ohjelmakokonaisuuden.

Toimijat rakentavat tänä syksynä uutta valotapahtumaa osana Savonlinnan Kulttuurin unelmavuotta. Valon sillat –viikonloppu aloittaa kuukauden kestävän Savonlinna loistaa –kokonaisuuden, joka tuo elämyksiä ja kohtaamisia vuoden pimeimpään aikaan kokoamalla yhteen valotaidetta, valaistuja kulttuurikohteita sekä monipuolista ohjelmaa marras-joulukuun aikana.

Valon sillat –viikonloppuna 13.-15.11. kaupunkilaiset ja matkailijat voivat kokea valotaidetta, valaistuja kulttuurikohteita sekä uudenlaisia tapoja nähdä ja kokea Savonlinna pimeän aikaan. Esillä on osallistavaa valotaidetta, projisointeja sekä elämyksiä sekä vesiltä että maalta käsin.

Tapahtumakokonaisuus syntyy laajassa yhteistyössä yritysten, Kulttuurin unelmavuosi 2026 -hankkeen, Riihisaaren, Olavinlinnan sekä Sakke ry:n kesken. Yhteisenä tavoitteena on vahvistaa Savonlinnan ympärivuotista tapahtumatarjontaa ja matkailuvetovoimaa sekä tarjota paikallisille uudenlaisia elämyksiä ja kohtaamispaikkoja.

title: Tanssia taiteen alttarille
content:
”Taiteella on omat lakinsa, sen on kuljettava määrättyjen kehitysvaiheiden kautta, sitä ei tekemällä tehdä. Balettimme on kärsinyt melkoisia vaurioita viime vuosina eikä vähiten siksi, että sitä käsitellään kuin olisi kysymyksessä jokin käsityöläisammattiryhmä eikä taiteenhaara.”

Lokakuussa 1955 nimimerkki Attitude kirjoitti Uudessa Suomessa katsauksen Suomen kansallisoopperan baletin nykytilanteeseen. Vaurioilla kirjoittaja viittasi saman vuoden keväällä alkaneeseen kuohuntaan kansallisoopperan baletin ympärillä.

Taiteilijakunnan ja johtokunnan välille syntynyttä, niin balettiriidaksi kuin oopperaskandaaliksi kutsuttua konfliktia, käytiin ja puitiin lehdistössä laajalti molempien osapuolien vuorottaisilla kommenteilla – siitä huolimatta, että johtokunta kuvaili lehdistön välityksellä käytyä keskustelua vastenmieliseksi. Lehdistöllä oli ilmeisen tärkeä rooli sekä tiedonkulun että oopperan maineen ylläpitämisen saralla.

title: Istuimme taiteilijan kanssa bensiininhajun epämukavuudessa pohtimassa nykypäivän kolonialistista väkivaltaa – Uusi näyttely kysyy, voisiko maailmaa ymmärtää eri tavalla
content:
”Oletko sä tehnyt tämän? Tää on niin kaunis!” nuori tyttö sanoo varovasti.

Seisomme suomalaiskongolaisen taiteilijan Liisa-Irmelen Liwatan kanssa ihmettelemässä hänen Oloseutu-teostaan Amos Rex -museossa Helsingin keskustassa.

Vuoren toisella puolen -näyttely esittelee yksitoista nykytaiteilijaa, jotka työskentelevät Afrikan mantereella ja afropohjoismaisessa diasporassa Suomessa ja Pohjoismaissa. 

Näyttely on saanut nimensä suomalaisnigerialaisen Minna Salamin kirjasta Aistien viisaus. Inspiraationa on tarina vuoresta, jonka kaksi tutkimusmatkailijaa kokee hyvin eri tavalla. Tarina symboloi sitä, että todellisuus voi näyttäytyä erilaisena riippuen siitä, kenen näkemys siitä on esillä ja kenen tarinaan uskotaan.

Oloseutu-teoksessaan Liwata tutkii kansallismaisemia, sekä suomalaisia että kongolaisia.

Liwatan isä on kotoisin Kongo-joen varrella sijaitsevasta kalastajakylästä, jossa liikutaan saarten välillä elantoa etsimässä.

Kongossa hän on käynyt vain yhden kerran kolmevuotiaana, joten muistot sieltä ovat lähinnä sukulaisten kertomusten ja valokuvien varassa.

title: Suomelta 8 miljoonaa euroa humanitaarista apua ruokaturvattomuuteen ja Ukrainan talveen
content:
Suomi myöntää loppuvuonna yhteensä 8 miljoonaa euroa humanitaarista apua Ukrainan, Etelä-Sudanin, Afganistanin sekä Afrikan sarven ja Suurten järvien alueen humanitaarisiin kriiseihin. Tämän myötä Suomen humanitaarisen avun kokonaisrahoitus on vuonna 2026 tähän mennessä noin 124 miljoonaa euroa eli suunnilleen samalla tasolla kuin kahden edeltävän vuoden keskiarvo.

Suomi painottaa ihmishenkiä pelastavan humanitaarisen avun myönnöissä kaikkein haavoittuvimpien auttamista.

Humanitaarista apua kanavoidaan Ukrainaan tässä myöntöerässä kaksi miljoonaa euroa. Maailman ruokaohjelma WFP:n kautta Ukrainaan myönnetään miljoona euroa. WFP työskentelee paikallisten kumppaneiden kanssa ja toimittaa mm. ruokapakkauksia etulinjassa sijaitseville alueille. YK:n pakolaisjärjestö UNHCR:n kautta kanavoidaan miljoona euroa erityisesti maan sisällä siirtymään joutuneiden ja evakuoitujen ihmisten auttamiseksi. Molemmat järjestöt tarjoavat myös talveen varautumisen apua. Ukrainan siviilien tilanne on entisestään vaikeutunut Venäjän kiihtyvien iskujen seurauksena.

title: EU Sanctions Envoy Pushes for Action Against Rusal’s Irish Alumina Refinery
content:
Material produced in a major metals refinery in Ireland is “undoubtedly” going into Russia’s weapons supply chain, the European Union’s Sanctions Envoy David O’Sullivan said on Thursday, adding that “there is a very real issue to be addressed.”

The comments, made at the Institute for International and European Affairs (IIEA) in Dublin, come seven months after OCCRP and partners published an investigation showing that the Aughinish Alumina refinery in western Ireland was indirectly supplying Russian weapons producers.

As much as half of the alumina from the Aughinish refinery was shipped to smelters owned by its parent company, United Company Rusal, and used to produce aluminum. The metal was then sold to a trading company supplying dozens of EU-sanctioned Russian weapons manufacturers, OCCRP’s investigation showed. 

Weapons made by these firms have leveled entire city blocks in Mariupol, struck a children’s hospital in Kyiv, and blown open an apartment building in western Ukraine, according to EU sanctions listings, Ukraine’s military intelligence, and the London-based Royal United Services Institute (RUSI).

title: Christopher Lee Reads Edgar Allan Poe: “The Raven,” “The Fall of the House of Usher,” “The Murders in the Rue Morgue” & More
content: Sir Christopher Lee and Edgar Allan Poe went way back. Or at least they went as far back as 1969, the year of The Oblong Box, a loose and lurid film adaptation of the eponymous story starring Lee and the also Poe-associated Vincent Price. Lee plays the doctor to whom a gang of grave-robbers delivers Price’s character, an Englishman disfigured in a voodoo ceremony who fakes his own death in order to escape the captivity of his brother. Whatever its entertainment value, the picture doesn’t rank especially high in the canon of Poe adaptations. Nor, for that matter, does the original story rank alongside works like “The Pit and the Pendulum,” “The Fall of the House of Usher,” “The Cask of Amontillado,” or “The Black Cat.”

title: Digital Commons Policy Summit 2026
content:
On 12 November, the NGI Commons Initiative is organising the Digital Commons Policy Summit 2026 in Brussels. Building on the previous year’s edition, this year’s summit will focus on ‘Digital commons and the Open Internet Stack for a competitive Europe’. The summit’s goal is to advance and discuss strategies to achieve European digital sovereignty and to ensure that Digital Commons have a role in the new European Open Internet Stack.

The gathering will bring together policymakers, regulators, funders and practitioners to discuss tech sovereignty and open source.

As part of the NGI Commons consortium, Open Future will lead session 2, which will be moderated by Paul Keller (Director of Policy) and titled ‘The Digital Commons Strategic Agenda’. Confirmed speakers include Henri Verdier (Director, Fondation INRIA) and Jan Penfrat (EDRi, Senior Policy Advisor).

Our Director of Research, Zuzanna Warso, will also speak at the summit to discuss the Tech Sovereignty Package and the Digital Commons.

title: Nuclear Weapons Waste Made Workers Sick. Despite a Law Meant to Help, the DOE Keeps Fighting Their Claims.
content:
Lonnie Rouse shuffled into a wood-paneled conference room at the Washington state Capitol in March 2018. It had been nearly a decade since medical experts diagnosed him with a neurological disease they attributed to his exposure to chemicals at work. In the time since, he had acquired a stutter, begun limping and lost several teeth biting into a banana.

For nearly 20 years, Rouse had packaged plutonium and monitored radioactive waste at the Hanford Site, a now-decommissioned Department of Energy nuclear weapons production plant in south-central Washington and one of the most contaminated nuclear sites in the country. Tanks full of radioactive sludge exposed him to at least 48 potentially hazardous chemicals. The worksite was so toxic, he said, that the floor once melted the rubber off his boots. 

Rouse was among the thousands of workers responsible for the ongoing environmental cleanup at Hanford, which has been underway since the DOE shut down the last reactor in the late 1980s. Congress has acknowledged, based on voluminous studies, that radiation at DOE sites poses health risks to workers.

title: Erik Bergman 115 – välkommen på konsert
content:
I år skulle den finländska tonsättaren och dirigenten Erik Bergman ha fyllt 115 år. Det uppmärksammar vi med en konsert och prisutdelning på hans födelsedag den 24 november.

Erik Bergman (24.11.1911 – 24.4.2006) är inte bara en känd tonsättare och dirigent som aldrig drog sig för det nya och okända. Erik Bergman är också en av Kulturfondens donatorer.

I år skulle Erik Bergman ha fyllt 115 år och det firar vi med en konsert i samarbete med Helsingfors kammarkör och Akademiska Sångföreningen.

Konserten är öppen för alla och inträdet är gratis.

Välkommen!

Tisdagen den 24 november 2026 kl. 19.

Programmet räcker ungefär två timmar.

Paulus kyrka, Sammattivägen 5, Helsingfors

Läs mer aom kyrkan här: https://www.helsinginseurakunnat.fi/artikkelit/mttqp96e3

Vi riktar ett varmt tack till Paulus kyrka i Helsingfors för möjligheten att ge konserten en fin inramning i kyrkan.

Inträdet är fritt, men för att vara säker på att du får en plats ska du anmäla dig på förhand via Kulturfondens formulär.

Om du inte anmält dig på förhand, är du välkommen till konserten i den mån det finns sittplatser.

  • Helsingfors Kammarkör
  • Akademiska Sångföreningen
  • Elisa Huovinen, dirigent
  • Susanne Kujala, orgel

title: European CEOs warn against surrendering frontier AI to US and China
content:
BRUSSELS — Top tech entrepreneurs are lining up to denounce calls by European leaders to pull out of the race to build AI frontier models.

POLITICO last week reported that key leaders, including European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and prominent tech founders, believe Europe should shift away from trying to catch U.S. frontrunners in developing the most advanced AI models, and focus instead on deriving value from the technology through applications.

“We need our own models, and we need the whole value chain of AI,” Jarek Kutylowski, CEO of German AI translation-focused research lab DeepL, told POLITICO in an exclusive interview. “We also need to capture the value that lies in the technology and in AI itself … Otherwise we’re just going to be leaving a large part of the value creation [to others].”

The rift exposes how Europe is struggling to find its feet in the global AI race. The continent trails the U.S. and China in developing the most complex and advanced models, which have become a security concern because they can exploit software vulnerabilities.

title: Brazil’s election puts at risk country’s role as a bulwark against Trump interventionism in the Americas
content:
On Oct. 25, Brazilians will return to the polls for the second round of the presidential election. The results will matter not only for the future of country itself, but also for the region and the world. Alongside Canada and Mexico, Brazil, under the leadership of current President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is one of the few countries in the region that has stood up to Donald Trump’s meddling and interference attempts.

Under Lula, Brazil still serves as a bulwark against the imposition of right-wing populist agendas critics say run counter to the broader interests of local societies, but cater to the interests of certain domestic elites. It is within this context that we must consider the Brazilian election alongside other electoral processes in the democratic world.

title: Preserving More Than the Web: Building an Archive of Online Resources for Preservation and Conservation
content:
In this interview, Jon Sweitzer-Lamme explains how web archiving is supporting the work of conservators and preservation scientists at the Library. He describes the process of creating the Preservation and Conservation Web Archive, what it preserves and why, the challenges of expanding the collection internationally, and how the archive can help future researchers understand the history of the field. 

What is your job at The Library of Congress and what was your role in creating this collection? 

I am a Preservation Librarian in the Conservation Division. Part of my role is ensuring that conservators and preservation scientists have access to the resources they need for their work, including new scholarly publications. As more of those resources became available only online, I realized we needed to preserve access for the future, which led to creating the Preservation and Conservation Web Archive. I am the Collection Leader, and I’ve researched the field and worked with colleagues across the Conservation Division to identify resources to include in the collection.

title: Taking the Long View: Man City Verdict Shows Whistleblowers’ Impact Spans Years
content:
By Sandrine Rastello

The independent commission that recently found Manchester City guilty on nearly all charges of breaking Premier League rules sent shock waves through international football, threatening the future of one of the biggest clubs and straining diplomatic relations between the UK and the United Arab Emirates.

For The Signals Network, which has supported the whistleblower behind the Football Leaks that sparked the lengthy probe, it was yet another reminder that the impact of speaking up can often take years.

“Speaking up against wrongdoing can lead to major societal gains but those usually aren’t seen right away as investigations, prosecutions and legislation follow their own pace,” TSN’s Founding Executive Director Delphine Halgand-Mishra said. “The impact on the life of whistleblowers can last years, too. That’s why we must take a long view when supporting them.”

title: Päivitä verkkosivut heti – seuraava suuri haavoittuvuus voi iskeä nopeammin kuin yritys ehtii reagoida
content:
TIEDOKSI MEDIALLE – JULKAISUVAPAA

PHP2Shell-nimellä tunnetut CVE-2026-109618- ja CVE-2026-109619-haavoittuvuudet voivat mahdollistaa hyökkääjälle koodin suorittamisen haavoittuvalla palvelimella ilman kirjautumista. Molempien haavoittuvuuksien vakavuusluokitus on 9,2/10, ja korjatut PHP-versiot julkaistiin keskiviikkona 21. lokakuuta. Viranomaiset kehottavat organisaatioita päivittämään haavoittuvat järjestelmät välittömästi.

Arviolta 70 prosenttia maailman verkkosivustoista käyttää PHP-ohjelmointikieltä.

Fortinetin kyberturvallisuuslaboratorio FortiGuard Labs suosittelee priorisoimaan erityisesti internetiin avoimien PHP-palvelinten päivittämistä. Jos korjausta ei voida tehdä heti, internetiin avoimien sovellusten eristämistä julkisista verkoista on syytä harkita korjauksen asentamiseen asti.

”Jos yrityksen verkkosivusto tai muu verkkoon avoin palvelu käyttää PHP:tä, nyt ei kannata odottaa seuraavaa normaalia huoltoikkunaa. Ensin pitää selvittää, mitä PHP-versiota palvelu käyttää ja asentaa saatavilla oleva korjaus mahdollisimman nopeasti”, sanoo Suomen Fortinetin tietoturva-asiantuntija Timo Lohenoja.

title: Järjestöt luovuttivat vetoomuksen ministeri Karoliina Partaselle – 15 520 suomalaista vaatii konkreettisia tekoja naisiin kohdistuvan väkivallan lopettamiseksi
content:
Suomi on yksi Euroopan unionin vaarallisimmista maista naisille. Yli puolet Suomessa asuvista naisista on kokenut fyysistä väkivaltaa, seksuaaliväkivaltaa tai uhkailua 15 vuotta täytettyään. Naisiin kohdistuva väkivalta ei ole vähentynyt viimeisen vuosikymmenen aikana, ja lähisuhdeväkivalta on edelleen vakava yhteiskunnallinen ongelma.

Naistenpäivän marssin yhteydessä käynnistetyllä vetoomuksella järjestöt vaativat, että naisiin kohdistuvan väkivallan ehkäiseminen nostetaan Suomessa poliittiseksi painopisteeksi ja että tavoitteiden saavuttamiseksi osoitetaan riittävät resurssit.

Yli 15 200 allekirjoitusta osoittaa, että suomalaiset vaativat muutosta ja ovat valmiita asettumaan naisiin kohdistuvaa väkivaltaa vastaan. Vetoomuksen saama laaja tuki lähettää päättäjille selkeän viestin: naisten oikeus väkivallattomaan elämään on turvattava konkreettisilla päätöksillä ja teoilla.

title: Big pharma accused of ‘free-riding on nature’ as global fund attracts just $7,000
content:
The Cali Fund, set up to raise $1bn a year for biodiversity from drug companies, remains near empty

Big pharmaceutical companies have been accused of “free-riding on nature”, after a landmark biodiversity fund that invites businesses to put some of their profits back into conservation was left virtually empty.

The Cali Fund set out to raise $1bn (£750m) annually, by asking companies that profit from nature’s genetics to contribute towards conservation in low-income countries. But more than 18 months after the fund was launched, it remains far below this target.

title: Polly Fields joins WITNESS as Interim Executive Director
content:
Polly Fields joins WITNESS in the role of Interim Executive Director following  Sam Gregory’s decision to step down. She will lead the organization while the Board conducts its search for a permanent Executive Director. 

Polly has deep knowledge of WITNESS having served on its Board for the past seven years, including as co-Chair from 2021 to 2024 and most recently as Board Secretary. She stepped down from the Board on taking up her new role.

In this role, Polly will work closely with WITNESS’s Senior Leadership Team to deliver on our existing strategy and priorities. She will also strengthen our relationships with the communities we serve, our allies and our funders, and help prepare the way for WITNESS’s next permanent leader.

Polly brings over 30 years of leadership in philanthropy, global health and human rights. At Dropbox, she founded the Dropbox Foundation and built its human rights portfolio, providing trust-based, unrestricted support to human rights organizations worldwide. Earlier in her career, she worked to expand access to treatment for life-threatening diseases across the Global South and was the first Chief of Staff for President Clinton’s HIV/AIDS Initiative.

title: ”Opiskelijat eivät ole vain sisällöntuottajia vaan itse Ylioppilaslehti” – Ysälli voitti Ylkkärin ideakilpailun
content:
Ylioppilaslehden ideakilpailun voittajaksi on valittu Lumia Lammin ehdotus Ysälli. Voittanut työ rakentuu ajatukselle, että Ylioppilaslehden tärkein voimavara eivät ole sen verkkosivut, sosiaalisen median kanavat tai edes yksittäiset jutut, vaan opiskelijat itse.

Lammin mukaan opiskelijoita ei pitäisi nähdä vain lehden yleisönä tai satunnaisina avustajina. He ovat Ylioppilaslehden syy olla olemassa. Siksi Ysälli ehdottaa vuosittain järjestettävää ohjelmaa, jonka kautta opiskelijat pääsisivät mukaan tekemään journalismia, kehittämään uusia sisältöjä ja osallistumaan lehden toimintaan kokeneiden journalistien ohjauksessa. Ajatuksena ei ole perustaa pelkästään toimittajakoulua, vaan rakentaa yhteisöä lehden ympärille.

Ehdotus keskittyy kysymykseen, joka nousi esiin monessa kilpailutyössä: miten opiskelijamedia voi säilyä merkityksellisenä aikana, jolloin opiskelijoiden aika, huomio ja yhteisöt ovat hajautuneet yhä useampiin kanaviin? Ysällin vastaus on yksinkertainen: jos ihmiset kokevat lehden omakseen, he myös lukevat sitä, osallistuvat sen tekemiseen ja kertovat siitä eteenpäin.

title: Your home is their asset
content: Let’s be realistic, housing has always been a business. What has changed however, is its scale. By the end of 2024, the value of global real estate had reached 393 trillion USD (€379 trillion) according to Savills Research real estate analysis. Most of this value came from residential property. This is more than the combined value of all global stocks and debt, and 20 times the value of all the gold ever mined. The market is not driven by what Barbara Steenbergen, the EU representative of the International Union of Tenants (IUT), calls “small amateur landlords”, but by large investment and pension funds. These funds are often registered in one country but source capital globally, Manuel Aalbers, professor of human geography at KU Leuven, told The European Correspondent (TEC). “They might have Spanish or German names, yet the money they invest comes from the City of London or Wall Street.” Listed real estate funds, which account for only a fraction of the market, owned €199 billion worth of property in the EU in 2024, up from just €5 billion in 2004. title: Convention on Biological Diversity. What you need to know and why it matters
content:
You have probably heard of the UN Convention on Climate Change, which emerged from the Rio Earth Summit in 1992. What is less well known is that two further conventions were also born at the summit: the Convention to Combat Desertification, and the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). The three were always intended to be implemented together as humankind’s response to the global environmental crisis. The aims of the CBD, which has been ratified by almost every country on the planet, are the conservation of nature, the sustainable use of its products (for example timber from rainforests) and the sharing of benefits fairly by everyone.  

Every two years, states that have joined the CBD meet in a “Conference of the Parties” (COP), the global decision-making body that oversees implementation of the convention. This year’s meeting is the 17th – known as COP17. In 2022, in response to challenges including massive-scale deforestation and extinction-level declines in the populations of many species, CBD’s COP15 agreed the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework which sets out 23 targets for nature conservation.

title: Turkey and Azerbaijan: Old Allies Fall Out
content:
The close relationship between Turkey and Azerbaijan has been a reliable and longstanding feature of geopolitics at the often-disputatious junction of Europe and Asia.

The 2021 Shusha Declaration formalized a relationship that had provided Azerbaijan with the drones and other equipment to defeat Armenian forces in Nagorno-Karabakh the previous year. It extended Turkish influence into the South Caucasus and crowned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan as a powerful figure in the region.

Is that really now at risk from a dispute over girls’ schoolwear?

On 12 October, the Azerbaijani government introduced new school uniform regulations that effectively barred hijab-wearing female students from attending classes, triggering public criticism and protests in several schools. While authorities cited Azerbaijan’s constitutional commitment to secularism and its long-standing secular traditions, the decision has exposed deep societal divisions, with some segments of the public supporting the policy and others viewing it as a restriction on religious freedom.

title: DCA-sopimus etenee käytännön toimeenpanoon tavoitteiden mukaisesti
content:
Suomen ja Yhdysvaltojen välinen puolustusyhteistyösopimus, Defence Cooperation Agreement eli DCA, on siirtynyt sopimusvaiheesta määrätietoiseen käytännön toimeenpanoon. Sopimus tuli voimaan 1. syyskuuta 2024, ja sitä on jo sovellettu Suomen ja Yhdysvaltojen välisessä puolustusyhteistyössä. Samalla jatkuu yksityiskohtaisten menettelyjen valmistelu, jolla sopimuksen määräykset viedään osaksi viranomaisten normaalia toimintaa.

DCA on Suomea sitova kansainvälinen sopimus, joka luo ajantasaiset oikeudelliset ja hallinnolliset puitteet Suomen ja Yhdysvaltojen puolustusyhteistyölle kaikissa turvallisuustilanteissa. Se täydentää Naton joukkojen asemaa koskevaa Nato SOFA -sopimusta ja tukee Suomen Nato-jäsenyyteen liittyvien velvoitteiden toimeenpanoa. Sopimus ei korvaa Nato-jäsenyyttä, vaan vahvistaa sitä kahdenvälisillä järjestelyillä, jotka mahdollistavat yhteistoiminnan suunnittelun ja toteuttamisen aiempaa sujuvammin.

title: Should AIPAC Register as a Foreign Agent? Zeteo Examines Pro-Israel Lobby's Influence on Elections
content:
The growing controversy over AIPAC’s impact on U.S. politics is the subject of a new Zeteo documentary titled Night Flower: Inside AIPAC’s Fight for Influence. The film examines AIPAC’s history and its role in shaping U.S. policy toward Israel, and questions whether its activities warrant further scrutiny under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, or FARA. “It says that you have to register under this law if you are acting at the request of a foreign government,” says Dion Nissenbaum, the filmmaker behind Night Flower: Inside AIPAC’s Fight for Influence. “And we talked to numerous people who showed us several examples of how AIPAC is acting at the request of Israel.”

Referencing the title of the film, Night Flower, Zeteo editor-in-chief Mehdi Hasan says AIPAC “blossoms in the dark, shrivels in the light. We’re trying to put some sunlight onto AIPAC.”

title: Preparing for the worst: a single attack could leave us without electricity or heating
content:
Delfi looks at the cyber threats already facing Lithuania’s energy sector and how it is preparing for possible attacks. On 29 December 2025, coordinated cyberattacks targeted more than 30 wind and solar power plants and two combined heat and power plants in Poland. According to CERT Polska, the country’s computer security incident response team, hackers managed to stop a steam turbine and a water treatment system at one of the plants. However, the heat supply to residents was not interrupted. The attacks on the wind and solar plants disrupted their communications with electricity distribution network operators, but power generation continued.

In July 2026, a cyberattack also affected the UK energy sector. According to British media reports, a small electricity generation facility was shut down for four days following the attack. On 7 September, the country’s Energy Minister, Michael Shanks, confirmed that the incident had affected a very small amount of electricity generation, but posed no threat to the wider UK energy system.

title: Housing: the basis of dignity and opportunities for all
content:
Housing is no longer just a local or national policy issue. Across Europe, housing costs increasingly shape people’s opportunities and influence the development of local economies. When people cannot afford to live where jobs are available, or young families struggle to find a home, the consequences extend well beyond the housing market. 

The scale of the problem is clear. Between 2010 and 2025, house prices in the EU increased by more than 60 per cent, while rents rose by almost 30 per cent. But the problem is not simply that housing has become more expensive. Across much of Europe, there is a structural shortage of affordable housing, alongside limited availability of social housing. 

The effects are visible across the economy. Workers find it harder to move to areas where their skills are needed. Young people are postponing leaving home, and families face growing difficulties staying in the communities where they have established their lives. What was once regarded mainly as a problem for low-income households increasingly affects the middle class.

title: NEW REPORT: Authoritarian Internet Controls Drive 16th Consecutive Year of Decline in Global Internet Freedom
content:
WASHINGTON, DC—Global internet freedom declined for the 16th consecutive year, with conditions deteriorating in 16 of the 38 countries assessed and improving in only 8, according to Freedom on the Net 2026: Seismic Shifts on the Global Internet, a new report released today by Freedom House. Authoritarian efforts to isolate populations from the global internet, expanding age checks for online access, and the weaponization of laws governing AI-generated content created new barriers to free expression and access to information. 

“Agentic AI promises to transform the internet,” said Freedom House Chief Executive Officer Jamie Fly. “Authoritarian actors are already weaponizing AI. We need to ensure that frontline activists and freedom fighters have access to cutting-edge technologies to counter these threats and to accelerate freedom in repressive societies. Democracies need to ensure that efforts to secure democracy and fundamental rights in the AI era do not restrict legitimate expression.”

title: Mohammad Azizi Remains in Detention and Legal Limbo at Choobindar Prison in Qazvin
content:
According to HRANA, Mohammad Azizi remains in detention.

A source close to his family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “Despite the passage of 30 days since Mr. Azizi’s arrest, he remains in legal limbo at Choobindar Prison in Qazvin. Some time ago, he was formally charged with propaganda against the regime on social media, disrupting public order and peace, insulting the Supreme Leader, and insulting religious sanctities.”

According to the source, despite his family’s efforts to secure his temporary release on bail, they have so far been unsuccessful.

On Wednesday, September 23, IRGC Intelligence agents arrested Mohammad Azizi at his residence in Alvand and transferred him to Choobindar Prison in Qazvin.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the specific actions underlying the charges against him.

Mohammad Azizi, a resident of Alvand, has previously faced arrest and judicial proceedings in connection with his activities.

title: Tajik Activist Given Lengthy Prison Sentence
content:
A court in Tajikistan has sentenced Asadullo Boboev, an opposition activist deported from Germany in June, to 17 years in jail. Human Rights Watch and other groups previously warned the German authorities that activists like Boboev could face mistreatment and criminal prosecution on politically motivated charges if returned to Tajikistan.

Boboev, 54, had lived in Germany with his family since 2017. He was involved in the Reforms and Development of Tajikistan movement, an opposition group critical of President Emomali Rahmon’s government. After Boboev was convicted under three articles of the criminal code, including “extremism through the internet,” a court sentenced Boboev on September 21, according to a media report. Tajik authorities have not published information on the case.

Boboev, who was deported from Germany on June 20, previously told media that Tajik authorities had opened a criminal extremism case against him because of social media posts criticizing the Tajik authorities. He said that the German court gave him until July 1 to prove that such a case exists, but he was deported before this deadline.

title: Smugglers Collected Up to $509M on Europe Routes in 2025
content:
Smugglers netted an estimated $388 million to $509 million from sea crossings to Europe in 2025, according to new research by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC). The agency estimated that between 190,000 and 209,000 people were smuggled along four major Mediterranean and Atlantic routes, with criminal networks facilitating between 57 percent and 90 percent of departures. Fees varied widely depending on the journey, ranging from $170 for crossing to Spain’s Canary Islands to more than $7,500 for routes toward Italy and Malta, according to the International Organization for Migration.

The Central Mediterranean was the busiest route, with up to 100,400 people smuggled, followed by the Eastern Mediterranean with up to 51,300, the Northwest African Atlantic route with 33,000, and the Western Mediterranean with 24,500. These estimates, according to UNODC, reflect all smuggling attempts, including journeys that ended in interception or tragedy. The routes remained deadly: 3,404 people died or went missing in 2025, while another 104,200 were intercepted at sea and returned.

title: What Ancient Latin Sounded Like, And How We Know It
content:
Latin is a language

As dead as dead can be; 

It killed the Romans long ago, 

And now it’s killing me.

Latin is a language

As dead as dead can be; 

It killed the Romans long ago, 

And now it’s killing me.

That famed ditty isn’t likely to resonate with many modern school children, but interest in ancient Rome remains fairly robust. 

We’ve come to accept that those stately ruins were once covered in graffiti.

We can recreate their meals from hors d’oeuvres (Boiled Eggs with Pine Nut Sauce) to dessert (Pear Patina).

Thermae Romae, a popular Japanese manga-cum-feature-film, took us inside Emperor Hadrian’s bathhouse.

But what did the Romans sound like?

Kirk Douglas’ Spartacus? Or Laurence Olivier’s Crassus?

The HBO series Rome upheld the tradition of British accents.

Animator Josh Rudder of NativLang did a fair amount of digging in service of finding out What Latin Sounded Like, above.

(And he seems to have done so without the help of Derek Jarman’s NSFW Sebastiane, the only feature film to be filmed entirely in sermo vulgaris or vulgar Latin.)

title: Ballot Rejections Soared in Rural Counties After USPS Reduced Mail Service
content:
In early August, election workers north of Spokane, Washington, went across the street to the post office to check for late mail-in ballots. It was three days after the primary and they were expecting no more than a few dozen.

Instead, their mailbox was brimming with envelopes — more than 500 of them, each a vote that wouldn’t count. The sight was “jarring,” said Auditor Lori Larsen, a Republican who oversees voting in Stevens County.

Across the region, other election officials were getting similar jolts. In the 11 predominately rural counties in eastern Washington, nearly 2,000 ballots came in late, compared to about 600 in 2022, the previous midterm primary.

In recent weeks, concerns about mail-in voting disruptions have focused almost entirely on President Donald Trump’s now-shelved plan to sharply restrict who can vote by mail. 

But a ProPublica data analysis shows that delays resulting from the U.S. Postal Service’s cost-cutting measures have endangered the validity of ballots cast in rural areas, not only in Washington, but across the country.

title: Studiefonden delade ut drygt 1,2 miljoner euro
content:
Antalet ansökningar till Svenska studiefonden fortsätter att öka. Den här hösten har nästan 1 000 högskole- och universitetsstuderande inlett sitt läsår med hjälp av ett stipendium från fonden. Axel Österlund som studerar lantbruksvetenskap är en av dem.  Sammanlagt går drygt en miljon euro till studerande med svenska som modersmål eller studiespråk.

– Stipendiet från Studiefonden betyder för mig att jag kunnat fokusera på min praktik till hundra procent utan att behöva bekymra mig över min ekonomi, säger Axel Österlund.

Axel studerar lantbruksvetenskap vid Helsingfors universitet och fick ett stipendium för sin utlandspraktik i Kanada.

–  Jag valde att åka på praktik till Kanada för att få se hur en mjölkgård i Kanada skiljer sig från en mjölkgård i Finland. Mitt arbete består främst av att sköta om korna på gården, det vill säga ladugårdsarbete, säger Axel.

Axel är själv uppvuxen på en mjölkgård i Tenala, Raseborg, och har under 2026 tillbringat sju månader i Kanada. En av målsättningarna med praktiken var att lära sig nya saker inom branschen som han förhoppningsvis kan dra nytta av när han återvänder till Finland.

–  Till en sådan här grej underlättar ett stipendium massor.

title: US renews push for EU to soften Big Tech rules
content:
BRUSSELS — The United States has renewed a warning that it will not lower tariffs on EU steel products and a range of other goods unless Brussels softens its enforcement of the Digital Markets Act, the bloc’s rulebook for Big Tech.

The European Commission relayed the message from the Trump administration to EU capitals at a meeting last week, two people with knowledge of the matter told POLITICO. They were granted anonymity to discuss the closed-door conversation.

The warning risks reigniting transatlantic trade tensions ahead of U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3, after a spell of calm following the EU’s implementation of the trade agreement struck at President Donald Trump’s golf resort in Turnberry, Scotland, last year.

Under the EU regulation enacting the trade deal, the Commission must report to the European Parliament and EU governments before the end of the year on whether Washington is keeping its side of the bargain on steel tariffs.

title: How K-dramas use Africa as a backdrop to boost South Korea’s image
content:
The success of South Korean popular music or K-pop continues to power the Hallyu Wave, a term that describes the global obsession with the country’s pop culture production.

But before K-pop came the spread of K-drama, TV series from the country, starting in the late 1990s. By 2024 the melodrama Queen of Tears ranked as the most watched Korean series on Netflix, becoming the 14th most watched show of all time on the streaming service. It followed on the success of many other hits like Crash Landing on You and Marry My Husband.

K-drama has led to the development of another trend: Africa repeatedly appears as a homogeneous place full of savage danger or childish immaturity, and in need of a Korean saviour.

As a scholar of film and media, with a specific interest in global Black art and film practices, I recently studied how and why Africa became this trope in K-drama. This is particularly true in rags-to-riches romance stories and melodramas.

I traced Africa’s presence in three K-dramas – Shooting Stars (2022), Marry My Husband (2024) and Queen of Tears (2024). In them, Africa appears in three different negative ways:

  • in need of charity

    • in need of charity

  • a place of rebellion and savagery

title: HELDIG Summit 2026 Methodological encounters: Application deadline for talks and posters extended
content:
Dear reader,

We are gathering speakers and poster proposals for the next HELDIG Summit that aims to provide a snapshot of digital research in Social Sciences and Humanities today. To bring about discussion, we are planning three themes: digital history, digital social sciences and digital heritage. We invite you to contribute to this event with a 5-minute flash-talk or poster from recent or ongoing project(s). The Summit is a good opportunity to give visibility to your latest research and tools, get inspired by methodological innovations in similar fields, and make new connections.  

The HELDIG Summit brings together social sciences and humanities in a day that takes a snapshot at the state of the art in digital research. This year, we bring discussion around methodological and infrastructure encounters beyond disciplines. What challenges in data processing new methods enable us to overcome? How to maintain and adapt our research tools to fast-changing technological landscape? How to target the use of AI responsibly in the research cycle?  

The Summit will take place on December 4 (10:00-18:00), including a cocktail reception.

title: AI Is Changing Everything About Hacking. No One Knows What Happens Next
content:
For much of the last month, many of the cybersecurity experts I talk to and follow have been posting like they are very scared. Many have been warning of an AI-powered “Black Swan” event, have been alarmed by the number of vulnerabilities suddenly discovered, and of the apparent power of AI agents and large language models more broadly to find and exploit previously unknown bugs. 

The rhetoric has ranged from worried-but-measured (things are about to get weird), to run-of-the-mill advice like update your software and make sure you have two-factor authentication on, to vagueposting about AI-powered attacks, to things like ‘the internet was nice while it lasted,’ to outright prepper-level terror.

title: Yemen: Huthis must open Ta’iz roads immediately as thousands of civilians’ lives are at risk
content:
The Huthi de facto authorities must immediately open vital roads in and around Ta’iz city, as fighting intensifies between the Huthis and government forces and moves closer to densely populated areas of the city, Amnesty International said today.  

The Huthis have tightened their control around Ta’iz city after they cut off the main road connecting Ta’iz to Aden in October, pushing the city to the brink of a severe humanitarian disaster. They have blocked humanitarian aid, putting access to food, water, and healthcare for hundreds of thousands at grave risk as per UN agencies. 

“The residents of Ta’iz, Yemen’s third largest city, have endured years of hardship due to the conflict, while hosting the country’s largest number of internally displaced people. At various points since 2015, Huthi forces have surrounded the city, blocking access to major roads connecting it  to other towns and cities and forcing civilians to use dangerous and poorly maintained mountained roads,” said Heba Morayef, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for Middle East and North Africa.

title: Ukraine’s Medical Evacuations Go Airborne
content:
A recent video released by Ukraine’s 92nd Assault Brigade reportedly showed a heavy bomber drone helping to evacuate a soldier, in what was the world’s first attempt to use a drone for the mission. “Due to high enemy drone activity and mined terrain, evacuating him using traditional unmanned ground systems was impossible,” said the brigade.

The soldier, Kostiantyn Vlasenko, had been cut off for months and had lost a leg. In the end, alone and fearing gangrene, he decided to amputate the other. Earlier attempts to reach him had failed.

Ukraine has been testing medical evacuations with aerial drones throughout this year and had previously used ground robots.

“This is the first time in human history that such an operation has been carried out,” says Anatolii, a commander of a mortar battery unit from the unit. “I think we’ll see it happen more often, but everything will depend on the conditions . . . [it works best] in rain or fog.”

The widespread use of drones across the front, and the expansion of the kill zone, moving in and out and getting the wounded evacuated from the front has become a very dangerous job.

title: Mehdi Hasan on AIPAC's Role in El-Sayed vs. Rogers Race in Michigan & Trump's Targeting of Ilhan Omar
content:
One of the most closely watched races in the midterm elections is in Michigan between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers. El-Sayed is a former public health official who is campaigning on a platform of Medicare for All, ending military aid to Israel, and getting corporate money out of politics. Rogers is a former Republican congressman backed by President Trump.

If elected, El-Sayed would become the first Muslim to serve in the U.S. Senate. During Wednesday’s debate in Michigan, Rogers repeated the claim, without providing evidence, that El-Sayed has ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed has repeatedly denied the accusation.

“If Abdul El-Sayed wins, it will be a reminder that the left can win in a swing state like Michigan,” says Mehdi Hasan, editor-in-chief of Zeteo. “And it will be actually a moment to say, 'You know what? Americans rejected Islamophobia.'”
