    Seison kodinkoneliikkeen pakastinosastolla ja pohdin kiireen tuntu rinnassa, minkä laitteen ostaisin. Olen poiminut syksyn viimeiset mustikat talteen, ja edessä on kymmenen vuoden talvi. Seuraavasta sadosta ei ole mitään tietoa. Valtava, globaali päätös ilmastonmuokkauksesta on yhtäkkiä tiivistynyt yhteen pienenpieneen arjen kysymykseen: mitä teen näille mustikoille?

    En tietenkään oikeasti ollut kaupassa, vaan osallistuin tulevaisuussimulaatioon, jossa ihmiskunta oli päättänyt viilentää maapalloa suihkuttamalla stratosfääriin rikkidioksidia. Silti tämä kuviteltu hetki jäi mieleeni hämmästyttävän todentuntuisena.

    Nykyään aina, kun luen uutisia ilmastonmuokkauksesta, palaan hetkeksi pakastinosastolle ja niihin viimeisiin mustikoihin. Muistan, miltä tuntui yrittää ratkaista aivan tavallista arjen ongelmaa maailmassa, jossa ilmastonmuokkauksesta oli tullut todellisuutta.

title: The best Kindles in the UK for every bookworm and budget – tested
content:
Whether you want a colour screen, somewhere to scribble notes or a child-friendly model, here’s what we recommend from Amazon’s e-reader range

• The best e-readers

From that fresh paperback smell to the wrinkles in the spine, nothing beats a real book. But if you’re sick of the space they take up in your home, or the weight they steal from your holiday luggage allowance, it might be worth considering an Amazon Kindle. It can fit thousands of weighty reads into as little as 158g, and as tech goes, it’s almost immune to the sort of pathological time-wasting features that come with modern phones and tablets.

Amazon Kindles have been available in the UK for more than 15 years, so they’re an old-school gadget at this point. But in 2024, the biggest update yet arrived: colour, which added an important extra option to the existing Kindle lineup, alongside readers for children, for note-taking and for tighter budgets.

title: France’s ‘casseurs’: why the term fails to do justice to the extent of looting and spiralling unrest
content:
Following widespread looting sprees and acts of violence occurring on the sidelines of the October 17 student protests, so-called “casseurs” seem to be the centre of attention. But the term, which comes from the French verb casser or “to break”, poses more questions than answers. The sociologist Paolo Stuppia examines the unprecedented situation many cities across France are having to contend with, and the complex combination of collective action whose motivations are unclear and the social media’s extreme agility.

The Conversation: How unprecedented are the scenes of looting that we witnessed on the sidelines of the October 17 demonstrations?

Paolo Stuppia: What may be unprecedented is the extent of the destruction of private property and the goods that have been stolen. It should be clear, however, that not all the looters can necessarily be sorted into identifiable groups, at least politically.

title: Africa’s bats could survive climate change – if they can find somewhere to live
content:
Climate change and changes in the way land is used are the two biggest threats to wildlife because they change the environment in which animals survive and thrive. Knowing how species respond to these pressures is central to planning conservation actions.

A number of studies have modelled how climate change will affect vertebrate distributions. But little is known about bats from tropical and subtropical regions, especially in Africa.

Bats are particularly sensitive to changes to their environment because of their slow reproductive rates, dependence on stable roosts, and sensitivity to climatic extremes that shape insect availability – their main source of food.

They therefore need both suitable foraging landscapes and the availability of caves for roosting. Research has been done on how bats will be affected by the effects of climate change such as rising temperatures. What has been overlooked is the fact that cave-dependent bats can’t survive in climatically suitable areas without access to suitable roosts.

title: Good news, the robots trying to take your job are bad at it
content: A supermarket on the outskirts of Copenhagen has become the unlikely site of a futuristic labour experiment. Føtex is training humanoid robots to restock its shelves at night, a task it estimates currently takes 40-50% of its staff's time. One day, they hope to have two high-tech assistants in every store, not to replace employees but to speed up routine tasks, they say. But for now, the robots aren't exactly autonomous – trainers from the Danish start-up HIVE Robots still guide their every movement using VR goggles. Nor are they... good. Still much slower than humans, they're meant to improve as they accumulate and process data over time. Despite their awesome looks, even the most advanced humanoid robots have had some spectacular public mishaps recently, including face-planting during demonstrations. Stanford University’s 2026 AI Index Report estimated the top AI robotic systems could only complete 12% of household tasks when tested in realistic simulations. Part of the problem is hardware: rigid joints, tough materials, and limited sensors make movements stiff. title: EFF to Brazil’s ANPD: Data Privacy and Free Expression Must Underpin Platform Regulations
content:
The Brazilian National Data Protection Agency (ANPD) plays a pivotal role in the regulation of digital platforms according to new legislation approved in Brazil. Throughout this year, EFF has presented comments, filed submissions, and met with the agency to emphasize crucial guardrails that the enforcement of new regulations should ensure. 

ANPD is responsible for detailing and applying obligations set in Law n. 15.211/2025, which established rules for the protection of children and adolescents in the digital space. While some provisions establish important privacy safeguards, like prohibiting advertising based on profiling of underage users, the law created mandatory age assurance mechanisms for accessing digital products and services.

title: When Big Tech becomes a tool of state control in Kenya
content:
State censorship on information has moved from broadcasters to platforms and the laws that govern them

Originally published on Global Voices

Image of person using Telegram by Christian Wiediger via Unsplash (Free to use). Image of Kenyan flag by User:Pumbaa80 via Wikimedia Commons(Public domain). Illustration by Global Voices.

This post by Grace Kobare is part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” In this Spotlight, we explore how Big Tech facilitates and hinders authoritarian governments and practices, and how these choices influence the Global South. You can support this coverage by donating here.

On January 30, 2018, Raila Odinga held his symbolic “swearing-in” ceremony in Nairobi, and the government, through Kenya’s regulator, switched off the transmitters of KTN, NTV and Citizen TV while they were broadcasting live.

The Interior Ministry defended the move, saying the media had been given a security briefing in advance. The stations stayed off air for days and were only fully back by February 9, 2018.

title: Town Leaders Said They Were Prepared for Floods. First Responders Disagree.
content:
The man was nearly to his waist in a flooded river and couldn’t get out. A firefighter and a police officer didn’t have enough rope or manpower to lift him onto the temporary flood barrier that separated them from the debris-strewn water. The man, Jere Stark, had just been carried a quarter mile by a torrential flood and was covered in mud and extremely cold.

It was around 3:30 p.m. on July 8, 2025, and a flood in Ruidoso, New Mexico, had unleashed chaos at Paradise Canyon Drive, just a couple hundred yards from the headquarters of the village fire department.

Not far from Stark, a woman huddled on the ground, shielded from the floodwaters by the temporary barrier. It was Stephanie Trotter, a tourist from El Paso, Texas, who had been washed away with her young daughter. A civilian tended to her while a second firefighter hauled in a rope he had used to rescue her. “Is somebody coming for her?” asked the civilian.

title: ‘A difficult line’: meet the editors tackling Wikipedia’s arms trade pages
content:
Volunteers and new recruits come together for ‘wikithon’ to put more detail about industry into public domain

“Anyone can edit Wikipedia,” the adage goes. But, it turns out, a relatively small number actually do.

What is worthy of a digital page in the world’s largest and most-read encyclopedia is decided by roughly 270,000 active volunteers, enthusiasts who populate the online resource with information on anything from 19th-century medicine to TikTok trends. Inevitably, some subjects are sidelined – the global south, notable women – but a new batch of Wikipedian recruits are waging war on one neglected topic: the arms industry.

Last week, in a classroom in central London, two dozen volunteers huddled around laptops and free servings of vegan Ethiopian food for what is known as a “wikithon”, an event of collective and in-person Wikipedia editing. Some were veteran editors in their 70s, others young students who had never registered an account before. But their targets include subjects such as Palantir, Project Maven and Nitro-Chem.

title: Japan’s expensive funerals and declining birth rates are transforming ancestral traditions
content:
Whenever I drive amid the mazelike bustle of Tokyo’s Shuto Expressway, where approximately 1 million vehicles transit daily, I see billboard advertisements for all manner of businesses: dentists, hotels, car and tire companies, and affordable funerals. Lots and lots of funerals.

For generations, Japan’s funeral system rested on family and community networks and Buddhist temples. Together, they sustained the traditional system of burials into the 20th century.

Today, Japan is facing a crisis of funerals and burials. Funerals averaged approximately 1.2 million yen or about US$7,600, according to a 2024 national survey – approximately one-quarter of an average Japanese worker’s annual gross earnings.

Consequently, many Japanese are thinking about whether to continue burial traditions that will place on their children and grandchildren the financial, logistical and emotional costs associated with maintaining the family grave. Japan’s falling birthrate means there are fewer people to care for their ancestors’ graves, which has made the problem more urgent.

title: Priced out of Netflix
content: When Netflix raised my subscription price again to €17 per month, I paid and moved on. But it made me wonder what the same subscription costs everyone else. Netflix charges different prices in different countries, depending on local purchasing power. After all, not everyone can afford the €25 a month the Swiss pay. I found that Netflix's lower pricing in poorer countries is still far smaller than the gap in wages to richer countries. So while the average Dane earns their monthly subscription in the time it takes to watch an episode of Friends, the average Ukrainian has to work through the whole of Pulp Fiction.

title: The Chestnut Grove Caught in the Middle of A Years-Long Data Center Fight
content:
Near the bank of the Ohio River, a historic American chestnut grove in Mason County, West Virginia has become the epicenter of a fight against a planned 2,250 acre data center campus. Plans for the UK-based startup Nscale’s Monarch Compute Campus, with clients including Anthropic, Nvidia and Microsoft, encompass the former Clements State Nursery and the American chestnut trees still growing there. 

For thousands of years, the American chestnut tree was a staple of life. Its natural range spanned hundreds of millions of acres from Maine to Mississippi, centuries before those names existed. As many as four billion trees provided a hearty nut crop for humans and provided miraculously rot-resistant lumber for railroad ties and housing. It sustained black bears as they prepared to hibernate, fed white-tailed deer and turkey, and shed nutrient-dense leaves. The largest American chestnut trees once grew 100 feet tall and 13 feet wide and represented one-fourth of all hardwoods; a squirrel could scamper along their branches from New England to Georgia without touching the ground, as an old saying goes.

title: EFF’s State Legislative Agenda to End ALPR Mass Surveillance
content:
Police agencies across the U.S. have deployed Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) to capture images of passing vehicles along with time, date, and GPS coordinates. While the technology itself isn’t new (ALPRs have existed in various forms for more than 50 years, and in the U.S. since 1998), the surveillance landscape has shifted dramatically. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence and national data sharing have transformed police ALPRs into an interconnected, nationwide tracking network. It is pitched to city councils by law enforcement and private vendors like Flock Safety, Motorola Solutions (Vigilant), and Axon as an essential tool for solving violent crime.

In reality, it is an inherently dangerous infrastructure of mass surveillance.

title: The Secret Terms of Trump’s Venezuelan Oil Deal
content:
In late August, President Donald Trump announced what he called the “biggest oil deal in world history.” Since then, the full text of the accord — which grants the U.S. sweeping access to Venezuela’s oil reserves — has been one of the most sought-after secrets in Washington, D.C. 

ProPublica has reviewed a copy of the 18-page strategic partnership agreement signed for the United States by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The document reveals carefully constructed terms that favor U.S. interests at every turn and cements the power of a small group of people handpicked by the Trump administration to govern and profit from the deal. The role of the Venezuelan government and the potential benefits to its people are largely absent from the text.

One of the most criticized aspects of Trump’s announcement has been his choice of a partner: Alejandro Betancourt, a globe-trotting Venezuelan oligarch who has faced money-laundering investigations in three countries.

title: EFF Launches Guide to Help Parents and Youth Protect Privacy Online
content:
SAN FRANCISCO – The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) has published “Online Privacy for Parents and Youth,” a new guide to help families protect themselves online. 

"Parents don’t need to be technology experts to help their children navigate the digital world safely” said EFF Public Interest Technology Director Babette Ngene. “At EFF, we believe in empowering families with the knowledge and confidence to make informed decisions about their digital lives. It’s about meeting families where they are and giving parents the guidance they need to have meaningful conversations with their children about digital safety, based on what works best for their families.” 

EFF launches this crucial resource as state and local governments consider enacting well-meaning but ill-advised laws that cut young people off from essential information and experiences, particularly harming vulnerable youth and marginalized groups who often find safety in supportive online communities they can't access offline. Such laws also entail age gating, which compromises the privacy of all internet users and stifles young users’ ability to learn, grow, and express themselves.

title: DHS Said They Searched Man Who Wiped GrapheneOS Phone for Child Abuse Material. They Lied
content:
When a Department of Homeland Security official sent out an alert to stop Samuel Tunick, a Stop Cop City activist, at an airport in January 2025, they said the reason was because he was suspected of “terrorist activities,” according to new filed court records which include a screenshot of the alert and photos of Tunick’s interrogation.

Tunick ultimately provided Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officials with a code that, when entered, wiped his security- and privacy-focused GrapheneOS phone. Tunick is now being criminally charged for that alleged act, in one of the most high profile technology civil rights cases in recent memory.

The court records also showed that CBP officials lied to Tunick during his interrogation. Instead of saying he was being targeted for suspected terrorism — although this search happened just at the start of the second Trump administration, it has dramatically broadened what organizations or people may be considered such — they said they needed his phone to look for “kiddie porn.”

title: Q&A: Why a pivotal IPCC meeting in Ethiopia ended in ‘profound disappointment’
content:
Countries have failed – for the sixth time running – to agree on the timeline for publishing the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change’s (IPCC) next set of influential reports.

The IPCC’s 65th session (IPCC-65) was seen by many to be the final opportunity for countries to agree on a schedule where its seventh assessment report (AR7) would be published in time for the UN’s second “global stocktake” of climate action.

Before last week’s meeting in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, IPCC chair Prof Sir Jim Skea had warned that releasing the reports in time for the stocktake in 2028 would depend on a timeline being agreed by the end of 2026.

But the week-long meeting descended into fraught disagreements between governments, resulting in Skea “suspending” the talks on Friday evening with no decision made.

Countries were also unable to agree on the IPCC’s budget for the rest of the AR7 cycle, leaving the body with a “serious funding crisis”.

The IPCC has pledged to reconvene the meeting at the “earliest opportunity”; however, it has not yet given an indication of when this will be.

title: Ahead of Macron’s Visit to Bahrain, Civil Society Urges France to Address Human Rights Abuses
content:
Ahead of French President Emmanuel Macron’s visit to Bahrain from 19 to 21 October 2026, human rights organisations have urged him to put human rights at the centre of discussions with King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. The organisations warn that closer cooperation between France and Bahrain risks emboldening the authorities amid an escalating crackdown on dissent.

Since the outbreak of the Iran–US–Israel war, the Bahraini authorities have intensified their crackdown on fundamental freedoms:

  • More than 700 people have been arrested, including children. Dozens have received lengthy prison sentences following unfair trials, including life sentences as documented by Al Amal Center for Human Rights and Justice and Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy (BIRD).
  • In April, the authorities revoked the citizenship of 69 Bahrainis, including 33 children, the youngest just 19 days old, leaving the majority stateless.

title: CSC:n Espoon pääkonttori muuttaa uusiin tiloihin Keilaniemen Porttiin
content:
Muutto uuteen toimistoon tapahtuu vaiheittain loka-marraskuun aikana. Vanha vuokrasopimus Espoon Keilanimen Life Science Centerissä on päättymässä vuoden 2026 aikana. Keilaniemen Portissa sijaitsevat tilat valikoituivat uusiksi toimitiloiksi vuonna 2023 tehdyn toimitilavuokrasopimuksen kilpailutuksen kautta.

Uuteen Espoon toimistoon haluttiin luoda toimitilat, jotka mahdollistavat hyvän työpäiväkokemuksen ja tukevat työntekijöiden hyvinvointia. Uudessa toimistossa on runsaasti erilaisia sekä itsenäiseen työskentelyyn että yhteistyöhön soveltuvia tiloja sekä nykyistä laajemmat neuvottelu- ja vierailijatilat.

Jotta työntekijöiden arjessa tapahtuisi mahdollisimman vähän muutosta, päädyttiin pysymään Keilaniemessä, jossa myös CSC:n vanha toimisto sijaitsi. Kohdevalintaa ohjasivat vahvasti myös vastuullisuuteen liittyvät tekijät.

”Uusi pääkonttorimme tarjoaa CSC:lle ennen kaikkea tarkoituksenmukaiset tilat. Toimiston pitää olla paras mahdollinen paikka tehdä työtä. Työympäristön täytyy mahdollistaa sujuva arki ja tukea myös hybridityön tekemistä”, CSC:n toimitusjohtaja Kimmo Koski sanoo.

Myös CSC:n Kajaanin toimipiste muutti uusiin, nykyaikaisiin tiloihin aiemmin tänä vuonna.

title: A Wealth Tax on Billionaires? California Voters to Decide Prop 40
content:
As voters across the United States cast ballots on November 3, Californians are weighing whether to approve a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of billionaires in the state. The tax would apply to roughly 250 Californians who now hold an estimated $2.3 trillion in wealth. Supporters say the wealth tax could raise up to $100 billion, with about 90% going toward healthcare. The remaining funds would support education and food assistance programs.

If Proposition 40 passes, it will mark the first time a government in the U.S. successfully taxes the wealth — rather than just the income — of the ultra-rich.

“It’s past time that billionaires pay their fair share,” says Lorena Gonzalez, president of the California Federation of Labor Unions, which is backing the initiative.

We also speak with California Congressmember Ro Khanna, who criticizes fellow Democrats like Governor Gavin Newsom for opposing Proposition 40. “We can either be a Democratic Party that stands for the working class in the tradition of the New Deal, or we can continue to cater to the donor class,” says Khanna.

title: Hyperscale has arrived
content:
The day has finally arrived: My new book Hyperscale is now on bookshelves in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, and beyond!

It tells the story of the data center buildout the tech industry has embarked on in recent years, what it’s cost communities on the frontlines in many different parts of the world, and why we can — and must — demand a better future than the one Sam Altman and Elon Musk are trying to force on us.

When I set off on the adventure of putting this book together two years ago, I figured data centers were going to become a bigger story. But it was impossible to guess my book when come out when the data center backlash would be reaching its fever pitch — and confidence in the AI project might be started to waver.

I’m not just saying this because it’s my book, but it’s truly one that meets the moment it’s arriving in, among so many other great books taking on the power of tech billionaires that have come out in the past couple months.

If you haven’t already picked up a copy, you should grab one from Bookshop in the US or the UK, go to your local bookstore, or visit the book’s website for more purchasing options.

title: Europe faces new energy crisis as diesel shortages and fuel prices rise
content:
Russia’s war against Ukraine and tensions in the Middle East have exposed just how dependent Europe remains on energy imports — and how vulnerable it is to turmoil in global markets.

Addressing the European Parliament during its October plenary session, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen warned that gas prices had surged by 140% since the end of February, while diesel prices had doubled. Over the same period, Europe’s fossil fuel import bill had risen by €100 billion.

“Businesses are under severe pressure, people are struggling to pay their bills, and the situation could get worse as winter approaches,” von der Leyen warned. She stressed the need for immediate action to protect those most in need.

“When we import fossil fuels, we also import the shocks and crises that come with them,” she added.

The European Commission argues that Europe must reduce its dependence on fossil fuels and make greater use of clean electricity generated at home. According to Ursula von der Leyen, more than 70% of Europe’s electricity in 2026 comes from domestic low-carbon sources, including renewables and nuclear power.

title: Victory! Court Rules OPM Data Disclosure to DOGE Is Unlawful
content:
In a victory for data privacy, a federal court in New York definitively ruled that the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) violated the law when it disclosed millions of federal employee records to DOGE agents. In a summary judgment ruling issued on October 20, 2026, the court found that OPM violated two provisions of the Privacy Act—one restricting disclosure of personal records between agencies and another requiring agencies to protect the security and confidentiality of records.

Since the case was filed, many DOGE agents have left the government and OPM has rescinded their database access. However, OPM should still clean up the cybersecurity mess it created. The court will decide the remedy at a later date.

"By virtue of the Court’s summary judgment ruling, OPM’s decision to grant DOGE Agents broad access to its systems of recordings containing [personally identifiable information (PII)] has been held unlawful," Judge Denise Cote wrote.

"The record also provides no support for a finding that it was the pursuit of a modernization agenda that prompted OPM to grant sweeping and expedited access to a score of DOGE Agents to its systems of records containing PII," she added.

title: Suomen Bocuse d’Or -joukkue valmistautuu Lyonin maailmanmestaruuskilpailuihin - kilpailun ensimmäisinä raaka-aineina Bresse-kana, vol-au-vent, perunalisäke, sekä kastikkeet
content:
Bocuse d’Or -kilpailun 40-vuotisjuhlavuoden kunniaksi Grand Finale 2027 palaa gastronomian perusperiaatteiden äärelle. Vatiteeman lähtökohtana ovat klassisen gastronomian suuret perinteet, mutta samalla kilpailijoille annetaan mahdollisuus tuoda esiin oman maansa ruokakulttuuria, raaka-aineita ja kulinaarista identiteettiä.

Bresse-kana klassisen gastronomian ytimessä

Kilpailijat saavat käyttöönsä kolme Bresse-kanaa, jotka toimitetaan effilé-muodossa, eli niistä on poistettu ainoastaan sisäelimet. Kaikki kolme kanaa on kypsennettävä kokonaisuudessaan, ja kaikki syötävät osat on hyödynnettävä. Käyttämättä jätetyistä kanan osista seuraa rangaistus. Valmiilla tarjoiluvadilla kanat esitellään kolmena erillisenä, keskenään identtisenä ja selkeästi tunnistettavana kokonaisuutena.

Kanan kanssa tarjoillaan kuuma jus-liemi, jonka valmistukseen kilpailijoilla on vapaat kädet.

”National tribute” - kansallinen kunnianosoitus vol-au-ventin hengessä

Toinen keskeinen osa muodostuu kahdesta keskenään identtisestä, vol-au-ventin hengessä toteutetusta kokonaisuudesta. Niiden tulee ilmentää kilpailijan edustaman maan kulinaarista identiteettiä ja gastronomista perintöä.

title: Cohesion builds the precondition for a competitive Europe and the Baltic Sea Region
content:
The Baltic Sea Region, like all macro-regions, faces challenges that no country, region or city can tackle alone. Resilience, competitiveness, climate work and connectivity all require territorial solutions. This was the starting point for the session “Fit for purpose – EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region builds a competitive, prosperous and carbon neutral region” at the EU Week of Regions and Cities 2026.

The EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region Action Plan (2026, pending Commission approval) gave the framework for the discussion. The recently updated Action Plan is the most geographically and thematically comprehensive framework for transnational work in the Baltic Sea Region. The Member States of the Strategy highlight the urgent need to respond to challenges such as a rapidly evolving security environment and increasingly complex multi-hazard risks: accelerating climate change and persistent environmental pressures, demographic change, and the demands of the green and digital transitions.

title: Webinar: Unpacking public action for information integrity on climate and the environment
content:
A few days before COP31 kicks off in Antalya, Türkiye, the Forum on Information and Democracy will bring together international experts and policymakers for an online webinar on public policies to strengthen information integrity on climate and the environment.

Climate disinformation, denial and greenwashing continue to undermine public understanding and slow progress towards the ecological transition. How can governments respond? What policies are already being implemented around the world, and what lessons can be drawn from these experiences?

Published on 13 October, the Forum’s new report, Mapping International Policy and Regulatory Frameworks for Climate and Environmental Information Integrity, offers the first international mapping of government efforts to address these challenges. Covering 23 countries and the European Union, it provides a practical resource for governments, civil society organizations, journalists and all stakeholders working to protect the integrity of public debate on climate and the environment.

title: Built for boats, adrift on land: Bangladesh’s Bede community struggles with a fixed-address system
content:
‘We cannot change the river, and we cannot stop moving’

Originally published on Global Voices

Boats and people on the Turag River, Dhaka, Bangladesh. Image via Flickr by Wonderlane. CC BY 2.0.

For nomadic Bede families on the Jamuna River in central Bangladesh, moving is a routine part of life. A study published in May 2026 in the journal Cambridge Prisms: Global Mental Health looked at three nomadic settlements in Tangail district of central Bangladesh: Jugiyar Char, Palima and Char Nikrail. It found that these families move several times a year, driven by seasonal floods and erosion, as well as searches for paying audiences. However, climate change and increasingly unpredictable river conditions are forcing these communities to land.

The researchers conducted a micro-case study through 12 interviews and one focus group during Bangladesh’s 2025 monsoon season (June through October). It describes displacement as an ongoing condition, not a single event. “We cannot change the river, and we cannot stop moving,” one sardar, or community leader, told them.

title: US: Order ‘No ICE’ Zones during Election Period
content:
(Washington, DC) – The United States government should order federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers not to operate in the vicinity of polling places, early voting locations, or drop boxes during the midterm electoral period, Human Rights Watch said today. The presence of these federal agents could deter people from voting. 

“ICE officers’ abuses have already seriously affected US citizens who have been stopped, beaten, detained, deported, and even killed,” said Philippe Bolopion, executive director at Human Rights Watch. “Voters should not have to fear being caught in an ICE dragnet when they head to the polls.”

In-person early voting is already taking place in the majority of states. In a nationwide September poll, 40 percent of respondents said they expect some kind of ICE presence at polls, with even higher percentages among non-white respondents expecting to see ICE agents in places people vote.

title: Israel’s Fateful Election: A Nation On The Brink
content:
Israel’s next election will decide far more than who governs. It will help determine whether the country can reclaim its democratic foundations, restore its international standing, and fulfil its founding promise—or continue down a path that endangers the very future its leaders claim to defend.

By Alon Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — Hardly any election in Israel’s history has carried such profound consequences. Israelis will face a choice that reaches far beyond party allegiance: what kind of country will they leave their children? After 7 October and three years of devastating wars, Israel’s security, democratic character, and promise as a Jewish homeland demand an unsparing national reckoning—one that confronts democratic erosion through judicial subversion, institutional capture, press intimidation, dissent suppression, minority disenfranchisement, unchecked executive power, perpetual warfare, and isolation.

title: Concert dessiné : Žižek Says!
content:
Concert : Žižek Says!

Jeudi 12 novembre 2026 à 20h 

Un concert dessiné exceptionnel à l’Institut finlandais : Ville Ranta, artiste récompensé pour ses bandes dessinées audacieuses, dessine le concert sous les yeux du public. Le duo tumultueux, composé de l’accordéoniste Niko Kumpuvaara et du saxophoniste-chanteur Joonatan Rautiola, peint des utopies surréalistes mêlant des influences musicales finlandaises, françaises et ukrainiennes.

L’œuvre principale du concert Žižek Says ! est un spectacle de théâtre musical sur le thème du pouvoir : les musiciens essaient de se tromper mutuellement en jouant faux, les instruments sont manipulés comme des marionnettes et à la fin, la voix chantée s’empare du corps du musicien, comme nous plongeant dans une psychanalyse à la Žižek. Dans cette œuvre jouée en première mondiale à l’Institut finlandais, le compositeur Miika Hyytiäinen allie humour, potentiel insoupçonné de la voix humaine et théâtre musical expérimental.

title: Internet Archive Honors Poynter and IRE for Preserving Local News Online
content:
As newsrooms across the United States close, years of reporting are at risk of disappearing. Stories documenting local elections, holding public officials accountable, investigating community problems and recording everyday life can become difficult or impossible to find when the news organizations that produced them shut down. Much of this reporting now exists only in digital formats, where it can be lost when websites go offline or archives are never created.

Local journalism captures the first draft of history in communities across the country. Preserving it means ensuring that future generations can understand not only what happened, but how communities responded, how decisions were made and how those decisions shaped people’s lives.

Two journalism organizations – the Poynter Institute and Investigative Reporters and Writers (IRE) – have stepped up to provide tools and training to preserve local news online.

For their work, the Internet Archive is honoring Poynter and IRE with the 2026 Internet Archive Hero Award.  The annual award recognizes individuals and organizations that have demonstrated leadership in making information available to people around the world.

title: Julkisen sanan neuvosto hakee kahta yleisön edustajaa kaudelle 2027–29
content:
Hae vaikuttajaksi Julkisen sanan neuvostoon

Jos arvostat sananvapautta ja sen vastuunalaista käyttöä mediassa, sinulle on tarjolla luottamustehtävä Julkisen sanan neuvostossa JSN:ssä.

Neuvosto hakee nyt kahta uutta yleisöä edustavaa jäsentä ja heille henkilökohtaisia varajäseniä kaudelle 2027–29.

JSN valvoo

JSN puolustaa sananvapautta ja valvoo kantelujen pohjalta, että tiedotusvälineet noudattavat Journalistin ohjeita, media-alan reilun pelin sääntöjä.

JSN on tiimi

Julkisen sanan neuvosto on 13 eritaustaisen henkilön tiimi, johon jäsenet valitaan kolmeksi vuodeksi kerrallaan. Jäsenistä kahdeksan on media-ammattilaisia. Yleisöä edustaa viisi jäsentä. Yksi neuvoston kolmesta varapuheenjohtajasta on aina yleisön edustaja.

JSN arvostaa yhdenvertaisuutta ja jäsentensä taustojen erilaisuutta. Toivomme hakijoiksi eri-ikäisiä, eri sukupuolta olevia, eri puolilla Suomea asuvia, erilaisen koulutustaustan omaavia ja eri kieli-, kulttuuri- tai vähemmistöryhmistä tulevia henkilöitä.

JSN:n perussopimuksessa määrätään, että kahdella yleisöä edustavalla jäsenellä tulee mahdollisuuksien mukaan olla erityistä perehtymistä sananvapausasioihin tai eettisiin kysymyksiin.

title: Om museikunnighet – ”museum literacy”
content:
Ett aktivt medborgarskap handlar om att fullt ut delta i samhället och utnyttja sin grundlagsskyddade yttrande- och åsiktsfrihet. Flera samhällsinstitutioner stöttar det aktiva medborgskapet. Museer gör det genom att vara tillgängliga för alla och bidra till fri åsiktsbildning. Genom att öka sin kunnighet om hur ett museum fungerar och vad det gör kan medborgare, däribland lärare och skolelever, få ut mer av sina besök och sin användning.

Medie- och informationskunnighet brukar delas in i olika slags förmågor. Dessa är ibland illustrerade som ”kunnighetscirklar”, som tillsammans bildar en helhet (Unesco, 2011). Här förekommer bland annat bibliotekskunnighet, spelkunnighet, filmkunnighet med flera kunnigheter eller kompetenser. Kunnighet motsvaras i detta sammanhang av begreppet litteracitet – på engelska talar man om media and information literacy.

Monelle riittävä taso on sellainen, joka takaa mielenrauhan.

”Sellainen, josta joka kuukausi jäisi myös hiukan säästöön ekstra­kuluihin, kuten hammaslääkäriin, vaatteisiin, kenkiin. Tällä hetkellä nettona 2 500 euroa olisi riittävä.”

title: Sudan As A Mirror For Today’s World
content:
Sudan has often served as a mirror for judging the health of the liberal world order because it has repeatedly been a laboratory for multilateral interventions to prevent atrocities and stabilize the humanitarian situation.

During the second Sudanese civil war, which stretched from 1983 to 2005, an estimated more than two million people died. In Darfur during the first decade of the 2000s, international observers estimated that 300,000 people died and another 2-3 million people were displaced.

At the time, finding a solution to Sudan’s conflicts was a priority for the United States and the coalitions it galvanized. For instance, Sudan’s second civil war came to an end only after intense mediation by the troika of the United States, the United Kingdom and Norway, as well as Sudan’s African neighbors, in 2005.  The level of Western concern and diplomatic resources mobilized to intervene in Sudan’s conflicts in the early 2000s feels almost unimaginable today.

title: Doctor Who’s Tom Baker Plays Douglas Adams’ Digital “Agent” in the AI-Predicting Hyperland (1990)
content: Cast your mind, if you will, back to the year 2020. It now feels like a different time, what with the spreading COVID-19 pandemic and the heated sociopolitical battles being waged online, and indeed in the (socially distanced) streets. That spring, we featured here on Open Culture an amusing retro-technological diversion called Hyperland. First broadcast on BBC2, the program stars The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy author Douglas Adams as himself and Doctor Who’s Tom Baker as his agent. “You want fifteen percent?” the former asks the latter when they first meet in a vast wasteland of flickering television sets. Not at all: “I’m here to do your every slightest bidding,” Baker explains, “to fetch and carry for you, to work tirelessly and selflessly on your behalf, always ready, always willing, no job too small or too menial.”

title: How Trump’s FBI Purge Saved Lindsey Graham and James Clyburn From a Bribery Investigation
content:
On March 3, 2020, Sen. Lindsey Graham walked into a private dining room at Charlie Palmer Steak in Washington, D.C. Graham’s time was expensive. He was meeting with two executives and a lobbyist from a Hawaiian naval defense contractor called Navatek. And he had required them to commit to $40,000 in campaign contributions for a 45-minute meeting.

Navatek’s CEO, Martin Kao, was confident that was all the time he needed.

“Shoot all he has to really do is stop by and say ‘yes,’” Kao wrote to a Navatek lobbyist and a fellow executive the day before, in an email seen by ProPublica. “That should only take a minute and he’s on his way. We don’t need to pretend we give a shit about each other.”

At the dinner, Graham ate little and talked a lot. But Kao got the “yes” he was hoping for: Graham agreed to steer a $10 million government contract Navatek’s way in his native South Carolina, Kao later recounted to the FBI. In exchange, he said, Graham asked Kao to pledge a total of $100,000 to his reelection campaign.

Hear the reporters discuss their reporting on the FBI on ”Paper Trail.”

title: Tule tekemään kanssamme podcast-jakso
content:
Oletko halunnut kokeilla podcastin tekemistä, mutta tarvitset apua alkuun pääsemisessä?

Ehdota meille ideaa podcast-jaksoa varten! Toteutamme Lähi-itä NYT -podcastsarjassa erikoisjakson yhteistyökumppanin kanssa, joka voit olla juuri sinä.

Lähi-itä NYT on podcast, jossa ääneen pääsevät Lähi-idän ja Pohjois-Afrikan alueen asiantuntijat. Useimmat jaksot perustuvat haastateltavien vieraiden itse tekemään tutkimukseen. Kohdeyleisöä ovat alueeseen jo valmiiksi perehtyneet kuulijat, joten aiheiden toivotaan olevan mieluummin suppeita kuin liian laajoja. Sisällön tulisi perustua ainakin osittain tutkimukseen, mieluiten mahdollisimman tuoreeseen. Tutustu aiempiin jaksoihin Lähi-itä NYT -sivuilla.

Aiempaa kokemusta podcastin tekemisestä ei tarvita. Tärkeämpää on hyvä idea ja sanavalmiit puhujat. Mukaan studioon mahtuu kolme esiintyjää, joista esimerkiksi yksi voi haastatella muita. Podcastimme on perinteisesti toteutettu haastatteluina, mutta voit ehdottaa myös toisenlaista toteutustapaa.

Yhteistyön kautta saat:

  • Pääsyn studioon
  • Tukea jakson käsikirjoituksen työstämiseen
  • Äänitteen editoimisen julkaisukuntoon
  • Julkaisukanavan jaksollesi

title: Socialists push for EU law on deepfakes
content:
BRUSSELS — European legislators are calling for EU-wide regulations to ban noxious deepfakes and hold technology platforms responsible for preventing their spread.

A draft of the tech objectives of the center-left Socialists and Democrats group in the European Parliament, seen by POLITICO, calls for a ban on harmful, non-consensual or deceptive deepfakes — a move that would require platforms and AI providers to prevent their spread rather than wait for victims to complain.

The push comes amid a Europe-wide debate over who controls a person’s digital identity as AI increasingly allows for the easy production of everything from a politician’s fake endorsement to the clone of your neighbor’s voice to pull off a scam. Denmark this month introduced a plan to amend its copyright law to bar sharing digital replicas without consent. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni applied to trademark a recording of her voice to protect against unauthorized use.

Despite the increased public attention and legislative activity, competing laws across borders could allow deepfakes to proliferate and make enforcement difficult both for platforms and authorities.

title: Americans, this is your chance to slap down the tech broligarchs
content:
The midterms will be a referendum on the GOP’s alignment with tech overlords over the public they’re meant to serve

Welcome back to How We Win, a Guardian opinion series with leading thinkers, offering bold ideas for America’s political future. Last week, Robert Reich highlighted the link between corruption and affordability. Today’s edition was written by Guardian US columnist Rebecca Solnit. Sign up for future editions here.

“The world should accept some bad things happening,” Sam Altman, the head of OpenAI, said recently, “for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.” Like so many things tech oligarchs say, it’s incoherent, since Altman would like to deny the world and the people in it the agency to decide whether or not we should accept his bad things. Surveys show that most Americans would like to pause AI; opposition to AI datacenters is a factor in many races in the midterm elections. People are outraged and anxious about what tech hath wrought, mad enough to fight back in what is coming to seem like a human v machine battle.

title: Elderly women are often victims of gender-based violence. Why is it so hard for them to get help?
content:
In 1997, Ana Orantes appeared on an Andalusian television programme to recount a lifetime of abuse at the hands of her husband. Just a few days after her harrowing testimony, she was brutally murdered by her abuser. Her case prompted a widespread reckoning on gender-based violence in Spain, which led to significant legislative reforms.

Ana Orantes died at the age of 60 as an elderly woman who had suffered violence and abuse for 40 years. But today, despite the impact that her case had, older victims of gender-based violence remain marginalised, to the point of being practically invisible. They do not fit the social stereotype of a victim, which we tend to associate with a young woman, often with young children in her care.

But while gender-based violence affects all kinds of women, of all ages and from all walks of life, not all victims find themselves in the same circumstances. And for any intervention to work, it must take this complex reality into account.

Elder gender-based abuse often merges two realities: domestic violence stretching back years or decades, and abuse of older people associated with dependence and care, often in the form of neglect or psychological abuse.

title: Palestinian citizens face a painful choice in Israel’s election: To vote or not
content:
Elections are typically framed as a choice for voters. For Palestinian citizens of Israel, however, the country’s national ballots pose more of a dilemma.

Constituting about one-sixth of eligible voters in Israel, Palestinian citizens could hold the difference in a race expected to be close. But voting involves a trade-off: By casting a ballot for their best interests, many Palestinian citizens believe they also risk legitimizing a process that seeks to silence their voice and a system that treats their citizenship as conditional.

The coming Israeli election on Oct. 27, 2026, brings that tension to a new peak. Since the last general election in 2022, the destruction and mass killing in Gaza, restrictions on Palestinian citizens’ speech and protest and leading opposition parties’ rejection of having Arab political partners have sharpened the dilemma of seeking protection through institutions that reinforce their exclusion.

Having devoted most of my academic career to studying relations between Israel and its Palestinian citizens, I see the question facing Palestinian citizens of Israel as part of a much longer struggle over survival, citizenship and political belonging.

title: Become Part of the Legacy of Abolitionist and Educator, Myrtilla Miner
content:
Today’s post is from Lauren Algee, a Senior Digital Collections Specialist & By the People community manager at the Library of Congress. 

In 1851, more than a decade before the Emancipation Proclamation was issued, the School for Colored Girls opened in Washington, D.C. with the mission of training Black women educators. The institution was the first of its kind in the District and only the fourth in the nation. Today, the Library of Congress and the By the People volunteer transcription program invite you to celebrate the life and legacy of its courageous and barrier-breaking founder, Myrtilla Miner (1815-1864).

Miner spent her young adulthood teaching in New York, Rhode Island, and Mississippi. In the latter she was denied permission to conduct classes for enslaved children, after which she resolved to open her own school for “colored” women teachers. 

Frederick Douglass recalled that when she came to him asking for support for her endeavor, he “thought the proposition was reckless, almost to the point of madness” but “her resolution was taken, and was not to be shaken or changed.”

title: Nicaragua ja Ortega – toksinen ja päättymätön liittouma
content:
Nicaraguan demokratian ja ihmisoikeuksien tilanne on heikentynyt vuosi vuodelta samalla kun vanheneva presidentti Daniel Ortega rajoittaa kansalaisten vapauksia ja viitoittaa tietä luovuttaakseen vallan lopullisesti kanssahallitsija-vaimolleen Rosario Murillolle. Niskassa painavat Somozan diktatuurin muistot, sandinistisen vallankumouksen valuviat ja myrskyisät suhteet Yhdysvaltoihin. 

Artikkeliin on haastateltu kirjoittajan nicaragualaista ystävää, joka asuu maassa.

Nicaragualla on poikkeuksellisen väkivaltainen poliittinen historia ja pitkä kokemus sekä diktatuurista, vallankumouksesta että Yhdysvaltain vaikutuksesta. Itsenäistymisen jälkeen 1900-luvun alussa Nicaragua oli Yhdysvaltojen hallinnassa, ja miehitys päättyi Anastasio Somoza Garcian valtaannousuun. Somoza käynnisti 70 vuotta kestäneen sortavan diktatuurin, joka päättyi vuoden 1979 vallankumoukseen sandinistien johdolla.

title: Väitös: Taiteilijoiden kiinnittyminen monialaisiin työyhteisöihin vaatii toimintaprosessien selkiyttämistä
content:
Taiteilijoiden osaaminen kiinnostaa erityisesti sosiaali-, terveys- ja hoiva-alojen työyhteisöjä. Taiteilijoiden soveltavilla työskentelymenetelmillä voidaan vahvistaa organisaatioiden kulttuurihyvinvointiin liittyvää osaamista sekä uudistaa työarjen käytäntöjä sosiaalisesti kestävämpään suuntaan. TaM Niina Oinas on kehittänyt väitöstutkimuksessaan prosessimallin, jolla taiteilijoiden monialaista yhteistyötä voitaisiin vahvistaa.

Jo useamman vuosikymmenen ajan kansalliset ja kansainväliset tutkimukset ovat osoittaneet taiteilijoiden osaamisen vahvistavan useita eri toimialoja, erityisesti kohtaavassa työssä. Erilaiset hierarkioista vapaat, taideperustaiset toimintamallit ovat osoittautuneet tehokkaiksi uudistamisen työvälineiksi erityisesti sosiaali-, terveys- ja hoiva-aloilla. Käytännön tasolla taiteilijoiden työllistyminen uusille monialaisille sektoreille ei kuitenkaan ole vakiintunut viimeisten vuosikymmenten aikana.

– Taiteilijoiden monialainen työskentely eri organisaatioissa toteutuu edelleen lähinnä yksittäisillä apurahoilla tai ostopalveluna tuotettavilla lyhytaikaisilla tilauksilla, Niina Oinas kertoo.

title: Do we really need all this cheese water?
content: A spoonful of whey in your morning cereal, a protein shake after an intense leg session. For many of us, focusing on protein in our diets has become a habit. Fewer of us know where the protein taking over our supermarkets actually comes from. Gym-goers' favourite product, whey powder, is a by-product of cheesemaking: it starts as the yellowish liquid left over after milk is thickened into curds and strained. That liquid is then dried into powder. Whey keeps most of milk’s lactose and water-soluble vitamins and about a fifth of its protein. For centuries, people drank it (for example the Scottish whey wine called “blaand“) or used it as a medicine for gut health. Today, up to 200 million tonnes of whey are produced as a by-product of industrial cheesemaking globally. The European Union alone makes more than a quarter of it. The hype around high-protein food has increased demand for whey, but production volumes have stayed the same, as they're linked to cheese production. As a result, the price of whey has skyrocketed in Europe in recent months. About a third of Europeans – and especially younger people – want to increase their protein intake, according to a recent survey by the EIT

title: Nobel Peace Laureate Navi Pillay on ICC, Gaza, Rape as War Crime, Her South African Roots & Mandela
content:
We speak with the acclaimed South African human rights lawyer and international jurist Navi Pillay, who was awarded this year’s Nobel Peace Prize. Pillay has been the United Nations high commissioner for human rights and a judge at both the International Criminal Court and at an international tribunal investigating the 1994 genocide in Rwanda. Most recently, she led the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Hours after Pillay was announced as winner of the Nobel Prize, the United States imposed sweeping new sanctions against the International Criminal Court.

“It’s extremely shocking to me, totally unacceptable, that the United States administration can today impose sanctions against the International Criminal Court,” says Pillay, speaking to Democracy Now! from The Hague.

title: Third meeting: Information integrity in the age of AI, from manipulation to regulatory responses
content:
The Workstream on Safeguarding Access to Reliable Information in the Age of AI held its third meeting on 1 October 2026. Co-chaired by Luxembourg, Spain and Ukraine, the closed-door online session brought together representatives of signatory States of the Partnership for Information and Democracy, civil society and researchers. The discussion focused on information integrity and manipulation: the technical challenges identified, the open questions for research, regulatory gaps and the policy responses emerging across regions.

Key insights from researchers, government and regulatory authorities

How AI is changing manipulation

The first half of the meeting focused on the issues at stake, looking at how AI also affects and distorts the flow of information itself through algorithmic gatekeeping, influence operations, and manipulation. It is increasingly used to sow distrust, to emphasize some views for political gain, or, as some speakers emphasized for economic gain.

title: Guatemala: Prominent Anti-Corruption Lawyer Fatally Shot
content:
(Washington, DC) – Guatemalan authorities should carry out a thorough, prompt, and credible investigation into the killing of Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, a prominent anti-corruption lawyer, former prosecutor, and former head of Guatemala’s tax agency, Human Rights Watch said today.

On October 17, 2026, armed assailants shot and killed Solórzano Foppa at the Campo Marte sports complex in Guatemala City. Another man, identified by authorities as Gustavo Adolfo Aguilar Gamarro, was also killed in the attack. Guatemalan authorities arrested two men in connection with the crime, but prosecutors said there was no evidence linking them to the attack and a judge ordered their release. 

“The killing of Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa is a shocking attack against a lawyer who played a prominent role in some of Guatemala’s most important anti-corruption efforts,” said Juanita Goebertus, Americas director at Human Rights Watch. “Guatemalan authorities should ensure a thorough, prompt, and credible investigation capable of identifying not only the gunmen, but also anyone who planned, ordered, or facilitated this crime.”

title: Decoding Pro-Israel Buzzwords in a Time of Genocide
content:
By Norman Solomon*

SAN FRANCISCO | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — Nearly two years ago, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International released in-depth reports documenting that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Months later, Israeli human rights groups did likewise. Support for Israel has declined steeply among Americans, but its defenders continue to maintain a siege of buzzwords against Palestinian rights.

As historian Rashid Khalidi emphasized in his book Brokers of Deceit: How the U.S. Has Undermined Peace in the Middle East, “language matters.” Standard terms and tropes “are the essential building blocks of a lofty and solid edifice of denial of an entire narrative, of the existence of an entire people, which is basic to the affirmation of a formidable counterreality.”

Prominent groups, notably the Anti-Defamation League, the American Jewish Committee, AIPAC and Christians United for Israel – along with allies in Congress, the Executive Branch and the punditocracy – rely on the same buzzwords to defame critics of Israel and deny its systematic crimes against Palestinian people. title: Illustrated concert: Žižek Says!
content:
Concert: Žižek Says!

Thursday, 12 November 2026 at 8pm

An exceptional concert at Institut finlandais, illustrated by Ville Ranta, who has won awards for his bold comics, draws the concert for the audience, his illustrations based on expressive contemporary musical works. In a tumultuous duo, accordionist Niko Kumpuvaara and singer-saxophonist Joonatan Rautiola paint surrealist utopias by blending Finnish, French and Ukrainian music. 

The main work of the concert Žižek Says! is a musical theatre performance about power: the musicians try to bluff each other by playing inaccurately, the instruments are moved like puppets and in the end, the singing voice takes over the musician’s body as if in a Žižekian psychoanalysis. In this work played here for a world premiere at Institut finlandais, composer Miika Hyytiäinen combines humour with the savage possibilities of the human voice and experimental musical theatre.

title: Albanian PM Offers Dialogue Amid Crackdown on Violent Protests
content:
After months of public unrest and more than a week of escalating anti-government protests, Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama has called demonstrators to the negotiating table, setting up chairs labeled "DIALOGUE" at the bottom of the stairs leading into the government building. 

"Now, whoever wants unconditional dialogue, wherever they want, whenever they want, even here if they want, I am available along with the Government," Rama said in a video posted to Facebook on Tuesday. "The only ones who are not welcome are those who commit violence and those who do not distance themselves from violence."

The overture comes as student-led demonstrations enter their eighth day, with crowds demanding Rama's resignation over allegations of widespread corruption. During a meeting with education officials, Rama characterized the recent unrest as a "hybrid war," claiming that foreign and political actors are exploiting genuine economic concerns to incite violence and attempt to overthrow the government.

Meanwhile, the streets of Tirana have seen severe clashes, with demonstrators throwing stones and firecrackers at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons.

title: Hear How Clare Torry’s Vocals on Pink Floyd’s “The Great Gig in the Sky” Made the Song Go from Pretty Good to Downright Great
content:
Smack in the middle of Pink Floyd’s classic Dark Side of the Moon sits a song many listeners may hear as an extended bridge between the two true centerpieces, “Time” and “Money.” But I’ve always thought of “The Great Gig in the Sky” as the album’s true center, a swirling, swinging, soulful prog-rock masterpiece, carried to stratospheric heights by British singer Clare Torry. The song’s wordless gospel vocal makes it an ecstatic, even hopeful, tent pole supporting Dark Side’s brilliantly cynical songs about the banality and injustice of modern life.

“The Great Gig in the Sky,” that is to say, provides much-needed emotional release in an album that can sound, writes Alexis Petridis, “like one long sigh.” Yet if you know the story of Dark Side of the Moon and of Clare Torry’s defining contribution, you’ll know that her incredible soaring vocal was sheer happenstance, an improvisation by a young singer brought in at the last minute by producer Alan Parsons—and one who wasn’t a particular fan of the band. (“If it had been The Kinks,” she remembered, “I’d have been over the moon.”)

title: ‘Terror of kings’: why the 1066 appearance of Halley’s comet terrified the medieval world
content:
A sequence on the Bayeux tapestry shows King Harold alongside a crowd gazing at the sky, beneath the embroidered caption Isti mirant stella (“those people marvel at the star”). Above Harold sits Halley’s comet, with ghost-like invasion boats in the border below – a Norman framing of Harold as a doomed usurper whose betrayal invited destruction.

A comet, or the regum terror (terror of kings) as the contemporary Norman writer William of Poitiers put it, was widely taken as a portent of change in human affairs.

The accurate record of the appearance of the comet is not the point of the depiction in the Bayeux tapestry. As most western European sources concur, the comet appeared in the evening sky from April 24, 1066. It remained visible for one or two weeks – four months or so after Harold’s coronation.

Modern computation indicates that the comet came within about 15 million kilometres from Earth, supporting a contemporary Chinese report that it was as bright as Venus, with a tail extending 15 degrees across the sky. The sudden appearance of such a bright comet must have made a deep impression on those who witnessed it.

title: Hyljekarkottimet ehkäisivät kalastajien verkkovaurioita Naantalinaukolla
content:
Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) tutkimuksessa akustisten hyljekarkotinten soveltuvuutta kokeiltiin ensimmäistä kertaa kokonaisen merenlahden mittakaavassa. Naantalinaukolla toteutetun tutkimuksen tulokset viittaavat siihen, että hylkeet vaurioittivat kaupallisten kalastajien verkkoja harvemmin karkotinten ollessa käytössä.

Luonnonvarakeskus (Luke) tutki vuosina 2018–2025 akustisten hyljekarkotinten käyttöä Naantalinaukolla. Noin 40 neliökilometrin laajuiselle lahtialueelle johtaviin kapeisiin salmiin sijoitettiin karkotinlaitteita, joiden avulla hylkeiden pääsyä alueelle pyrittiin estämään.

Naantalinaukolla toimii useita aktiivisia kaupallisia kalastajia. Alue on myös tärkeä virkistyskalastusalue ja kuhan lisääntymisalue. Keskeisin kalastettava laji on kuha, mutta alueella kalastetaan paljon myös ahventa, haukea ja siikaa. Hylkeet ovat haitanneet erityisesti Naantalinaukon verkkokalastusta.

Tutkimus oli ensimmäinen laatuaan näin laajassa mittakaavassa. Luke toteutti sen yhteistyössä Suomen Ammattikalastajaliiton ja paikallisten kalastajien kanssa.

title: Vihreät pitää paikkansa myönteisyysmittauksessa, kokoomus romahti imagovertailussa vihreiden taakse
content:
Vihreät on kolmen myönteisimmin arvioidun puolueen joukossa, kertoo Verianin tuore Puoluebarometri. SDP:hen suhtautuu myönteisesti 48 prosenttia suomalaisista ja keskustaan 43 prosenttia. Vihreät on kolmantena 41 prosentilla, ja sen perässä tulevat vasemmistoliitto, jonka arvioi positiivisimmaksi 38 prosenttia vastaajista, sekä Liike Nyt, 36 prosenttia.

Kokoomus ylsi vasta kuudennelle sijalle. Pääministeripuolueesta myönteisen käsityksen omaa 32 prosenttia, RKP:stä 29, perussuomalaisista 27 ja kristillisdemokraateista 24 prosenttia vastaajista.

Suurin muutos on Liike Nytillä, jonka myönteisten arvioiden osuus kasvoi yhdeksän prosenttiyksikköä. Keskustaan ja kokoomukseen suhtaudutaan nyt hieman kielteisemmin kuin puoli vuotta sitten.

Kuvaa täydentää Verianin tekemä imagotutkimus, jonka muun muassa Yle ja Iltalehti ovat saaneet. Tutkimuksen tilaavat eduskuntapuolueet osana puoluebarometria, eikä sitä ole tarkoitettu julkisuuteen. Iltalehti uutisoi imagotuloksista ensimmäisenä.

title: Elected women never asked to be nudified, yet here we are
content: As a person of a marginalised gender, existing online means being constantly amazed by all the ways the internet can be used against you, no matter how powerful you are. One of the latest additions to that arsenal are “nudification” apps, AI-powered tools that can be prompted to create fake, sexually explicit pictures and videos of people, usually without their consent. All you need is a single photo of them. Two recent reports by Berlin thinktank Agora Digitale Transformation looked at how these tools are affecting politicians. The first one found 147 members of national European parliaments were either directly depicted in fake nudes or listed on sites that help people create them. Unsurprisingly, women were far more likely to be affected than men – 33 times more likely, in fact. Surprisingly, political affiliation hardly affected who was targeted, but seniority did. People in more prominent positions were more likely to be affected. Agora's second report zoomed in on the European Parliament and found similar patterns: one in six female representatives had been affected, for a total of 46 women and four men. “Imagine going to work and seeing naked images of yourself,” said Lena

title: ‘Reverse-Engineer Anything’ Is the New Wild West of AI
content:
Over the weekend, it became fashionable to use AI to replace the operating systems on smart TVs with vibe coded or AI reverse-engineered ones to make them less bloated. People have taken proprietary internet-of-things devices that were bricked and abandoned by their creators and used AI to hack them and install new software on them, giving functionality the original developers took away.  

In the last few days I have seen people hack smart picture frames to become AI-powered smart calendars, baby monitors to remove all ads, and bricked Lululemon mirrors to bring them back to life with new software. And dozens and dozens of TVs to install AI-written software that removes bloatware, ads, and simplifies the user interface.

title: Hunger Amid Plenty Is a Political Failure, UN Rights Chief Warns
content:
The world produces more than enough food, yet conflict, inequality, waste and the concentration of farmland leave billions without an adequate diet.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — The world’s farms produce more food than ever before. The average global supply now exceeds 3,000 calories per person a day. Yet more than a quarter of humanity cannot regularly obtain enough food—or food of sufficient quality—to live a healthy life.

For UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk, this contradiction makes hunger more than a humanitarian emergency. It is evidence of economic and political systems that fail to distribute the world’s abundance fairly.

Addressing the UN-hosted Committee on World Food Security in Rome on 19 October, Türk described hunger as an avoidable tragedy. The international community, he argued, already possesses the food, knowledge and resources needed to prevent it.

What is missing is the political determination to make the right to food a reality.

The scale of global food production challenges the long-standing assumption that hunger is mainly caused by shortages.
snippet:
The world produces more than enough food, yet conflict, inequality, waste and the concentration of farmland leave billions without an adequate diet.

title: South Pacific Ponzi Scam “King” Noah Musingku Dies
content:
A fugitive South Pacific Ponzi scammer—who later proclaimed himself “king” of a remote armed territory at the center of Papua New Guinea’s Bougainville island—has been given a royal burial following his death from an unspecified illness, according to local media and photographs of the funeral posted on social media.

Noah Musingku was accused of stealing tens of millions of dollars from victims across the region in a 1990s pyramid scheme known as U-Vistract. Following the collapse of the scheme, Musingku fled in the early 2000s to his home island of Bougainville, a region then still recovering from a devastating decade-long civil war.

Styling himself as King David Peii II of the twin kingdoms of Papaala and Me’ekamui, Musingku set up a pseudo-state with its own armed militia, banking system, and local currency known as the Bougainville kina (BVK). The BVK was later declared illegal by Papua New Guinea’s government.

title: I’m a CTO. AI still needs your human expertise | Madhu Shashanka
content:
AI is increasingly getting good at doing some tasks, but it can never replace human workers’ judgment

Autonomous cars, which may be the safest we have built, keep getting easily avoidable parking tickets. While Waymos crash far less often than human drivers over tens of millions of miles, they’re still terrible at performing basic tasks – keeping out of disabled parking spots and tow-away zones, or steering clear of a church garage during Sunday service, according to the Wall Street Journal.

That is the state of AI today: impressively capable at something complex, yet embarrassingly clumsy at something easy. And it has implications for what work will remain human and what will be automated by AI.

Madhu Shashanka is co-founder, chief scientist and chief technology officer at Concentric AI, a data security software company

title: New long-clawed British dinosaur is the first of its kind in Europe
content:
The fossilised skull of a new species of mysterious meat-eating dinosaur from the Isle of Wight has been rediscovered in the collections of the Natural History Museum after over 100 years in storage.

Over its nearly 150-year history, this London museum has become home to over 30 million specimens, making it fairly easy to forget about the odd fossil or rock here and there. This is almost definitely what happened to the only known fossil of the UK’s newest dinosaur, a two-legged meat-eating theropod (the dinosaur family including birds) which we have named Invictibellatrix amberina in a new study.

title: Pelko koneiden ylivallasta syntyi jo 200 vuotta sitten – uutuuskirja paljastaa tekoälyn romanttiset juuret
content:
Tekoälyn historia alkaa kauan ennen tietokoneita. Uusi kulttuurihistoriallinen teos tutkii ajattelevien koneiden kulttuurihistoriaa 1600-luvulta 1840-luvulle. Erityisesti romantiikan ajan kirjallisuus ja filosofia auttavat ymmärtämään, mistä nykyiset koneälyyn liittyvät toiveet ja kauhukuvat ovat peräisin.

"Romantikot pelkäsivät koneiden ottavan vallan ihmisistä. Tunnetuin esimerkki tästä on Mary Shelleyn romaani Frankenstein, jossa tiedemiehen valmistama keinotekoinen olento karkaa laboratoriosta. Samalla romantikkojen dystopiat vahvistivat mielikuvaa siitä, että kone voisi ajatella ja kilpailla ihmisen kanssa. Koneälyn uhka ja lupaus kasvoivat yhdessä", kulttuurihistorian dosentti Nivala sanoo Turun yliopiston tiedotteessa.

Ajattelevien koneiden historiaan kuuluu myös näyttäviä huijauksia. Romantiikan ajan yleisöjä hämmästytti Turkkilainen shakkikone, joka näytti pelaavan shakkia itsenäisesti. Todellisuudessa siirroista vastasi laitteen sisään piilotettu ihminen.

title: We brought back the lynx, but will we save the rest?
content: When Portuguese biologist Henrique Pereira was a kid in the 1980s, there were almost no vultures left in southern Europe. Now, “you cannot drive more than a few days in Portugal or Spain without seeing vultures flying over,” he told The European Correspondent. “There was a huge recovery.” The professor of biodiversity conservation at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg told The European Correspondent about the success stories of European wildlife recovery: bears, lynxes, and wolves, for example. Wildlife that was once close to extinction made a comeback. A new WWF report looks into global wildlife loss and paints a less pretty picture: the size of global vertebrate wildlife populations has shrunk by an average of 73% since 1970. title: Scientists Discover A Strange Particle Explains the Origin of Reality
content:
Scientists have discovered that an exotic particle that existed at the birth of the universe might solve one of the biggest mysteries in cosmology and help explain reality as we know it, according to a new study in Physical Review Letters.

Our modern universe is dominated by matter, but it also contains fleeting amounts of antimatter, which is like a bizarro version of matter made of particles with the same mass, but opposite electrical charges. For instance, matter contains positively-charged protons and negatively-charged electrons, whereas antimatter is made up of the inverse: negatively-charged antiprotons and positively-charged positrons. 

As a result of these opposite features, matter and antimatter particles annihilate each other when they meet. This mutual destruction is the source of a major cosmic mystery, given that equal amounts of matter and antimatter are predicted to have formed in the split-seconds following the Big Bang. Yet somehow, matter emerged as the far more dominant substance in the cosmos, an asymmetry that has yet to be explained.

title: Germany’s Colonial Reckoning Returns to the Bundestag
content:
Debate over the genocide committed in Namibia has revived questions about recognition, reparations and whether Germany is willing to confront its colonial past as seriously as other chapters of its history.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 20 October 2026 (IDN) — Over a century after German colonial troops committed mass killings in what is now Namibia, the subject has resurfaced in the Bundestag with significant political momentum.

The whole thing was kicked off by an opposition motion calling for Germany to recognise the genocide against the Ovaherero and Nama unambiguously and to go beyond development aid to what the proponents would describe as restorative justice. DW reported on the ensuing parliamentary debate and the long-standing dispute over recognition and reparations.

title: Googlebook review: Google’s new laptops are woefully underbaked
content:
Great hardware let down by software flaws on these pricey machines that combine ChromeOS with Android

Google’s attempt to create a new type of laptop to compete with Windows and macOS machines is finally here, combining the best of ChromeOS and Android into the new Googlebook. With advanced links to Android phones and the best of Google built in, can these Googlebooks really compete with a MacBook Air or Surface Laptop? I took two for a spin to find out.

For years, Chromebooks have been the boss of budget laptops, but Googlebooks take a different, far more premium approach. Made by a range of traditional PC makers, including Acer, Asus, Dell, HP and Lenovo, they start at £999 (€1,099/$899/A$2,299) – a far cry from the £160 Chromebooks.

title: Julkaistavia koulutuksen arviointituloksia loka-joulukuussa
content:
Karvin loppuvuoden 2026 julkistukset esittelevät ajankohtaista arviointitietoa eri koulutusasteilta. Syksyn ja talven aikana julkaistavat raportit ja artikkelit käsittelevät muun muassa pedagogista johtamista, opintopolkuja, koulupudokkuutta sekä oppimisen ja koulunkäynnin tuen toteutumista. Tulokset avaavat myös ammatillisen koulutuksen eri alojen osaamista, maahanmuuttotaustaisten sijoittumista työelämään sekä toiminnanohjauksen kokeilun käynnistymistä.

Tässä tiedotteessa on ennakkotietoa Kansallisen koulutuksen arviointikeskuksen (Karvi) tulevista julkistamisista ajalla lokakuu 2026 - joulukuu 2026. Seuraava kooste tulevista julkistamisista julkaistaan tammikuussa 2027.

Oppimisen ja koulunkäynnin tuen uudistus astui voimaan 1.8.2025. Artikkelissa tuodaan esiin rehtoreiden ja opettajien näkemyksiä siitä, millaisena he kokevat tuen uudistuksen ja miten uusia tuen muotoja on kouluissa otettu käyttöön.

Artikkeli julkaistaan loka-marraskuussa 2026.

Aineisto on kerätty osana oppimistulosarviointien tiedonkeruuta, joten tuloksista tullaan raportoidaan erikseen pienempänä artikkelina.

title: States must act as Israeli state-driven settler violence escalates at the start of Palestinian olive harvest
content:
Responding to the latest acts of state-driven Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank over the weekend, which also targeted a delegation of European diplomats and a Washington Post photojournalist, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa, Heba Morayef, said:

“Once again, Israel’s apartheid system is turning the olive harvest into a season of horror for Palestinian families across the occupied West Bank. State-driven attacks by settlers on farmers that damage, destroy and steal crops, combined with Israeli military restrictions on access to groves, are causing immense suffering and economic loss for Palestinians.

“The series of attacks by settlers over the weekend against Palestinian residents of Khirbet Abu Falah and Taybeh in the Ramallah area, which also targeted a Washington Post photojournalist and a delegation of European diplomats, offer a glimpse into a reality of relentless aggression against Palestinians. Attempts by senior Israeli officials and electoral candidates across the political spectrum to portray this state-sponsored brutality as the work of a few individuals are a blatant distortion of reality.

A themed issue was published in late 2025 which focused on the experiences of those involved in the encampment and the issues it addressed. Two excerpts can be found below as well as the table of contents and a link to a PDF of the publication.

This issue serves as an archive of the 110 days that students at the Australian National University spent at the Gaza Solidarity Encampment. It has been developed to mark a decisive moment in the history of social movements at ANU and, indeed, in the whole of so-called australia, and to bear witness to what took place, despite ongoing attempts to erase or sanitise the record.

title: The future of early cancer detection with metamaterial technology and artificial intelligence
content:
Early detection and effective treatment of cancer are critical to improving patient survival outcomes. The rapid advancement of machine learning (ML), particularly deep learning, has led to significant improvements in the accuracy and efficiency of cancer screening, detection, and monitoring.

However, despite these advances, ML-based approaches face a significant limitation: the substantial computational resources required for the analysis and interpretation of medical images.

Detecting cancer at the earliest possible stage gives patients the best chance of successful treatment. Early diagnosis improves outcomes by enabling timely access to care and is therefore a critical public health strategy in all settings.

title: Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa: Prominent Anti-Corruption Lawyer in Guatemala Assassinated
content:
The prominent Guatemalan anti-corruption lawyer Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa was fatally shot along with another man on Saturday at a sports center in Guatemala City. For years, Solórzano Foppa had been outspoken against Guatemala’s most powerful politicians, business leaders and companies. He was known for his anti-corruption work as head of the Criminal Investigations Directorate within the Public Prosecutor’s Office and later as head of Guatemala’s tax authority, when he helped prosecute dozens of powerful Guatemalan business figures.

“In more recent years, he developed a social media presence, and he was forcefully denouncing corruption,” says Roman Gressier, a journalist based in Guatemala City. “We were thinking about [the killing of Solórzano Foppa] not only as an assassination, but also having a deep effect on freedom of expression.”

“Juan Francisco was a young lawyer coming from a background of pro-democracy and revolutionary activists,” says Silvia Solórzano Foppa, Juan Francisco’s mother. Her son was 43 years old when he was killed.

title: Päästökauppadirektiivin ja markkinavakausvarantopäätöksen muuttaminen
content: Komission ehdotuksella uudistetaan EU:n yleistä päästökauppajärjestelmää (EU ETS) vuoden 2030 jälkeiselle ajalle. Ehdotuksen tavoitteena on saattaa päästökauppa linjaan EU:n vuoden 2040 ilmastotavoitteen kanssa sekä samalla huomioida eurooppalaisen teollisuuden kilpailukyky ja hiilivuotoriskit. Ehdotus on laaja. Se sisältää muun muassa muutoksia päästöoikeuksien kokonaismäärään ja markkinavakausvarantoon, ilmaisjakoon, kansainvälisten ilmastoyksiköiden ja pysyvien hiilenpoistojen käyttöön sekä päästökauppatulojen käyttöön ja uusiin rahastoihin. Lisäksi päästökaupan soveltamisalaa laajennettaisiin meri- ja lentoliikenteessä sekä yhdyskuntajätteen polttoon. Tässä lausunnossa keskitytään päästöoikeuksien kokonaismäärään, teollisuuden ilmaisjakoon sekä innovaatiotukeen ja teollisuuden vähähiilistämispankkiin.
